7f0c252a-bd45-4fe0-b306-478eeb07b97b.label: Equal Vision Records
7f0c252a-bd45-4fe0-b306-478eeb07b97b.lede: Vic DiCara played guitar beside Zack de la Rocha in Inside Out, then built 108 out of Vedic scripture. The band toured in a school bus turned temple, fought anti-Krishna flyer crews, and broke up in 1996 when DiCara left for India to live as a monk. It came back in 2005, minus the temple.

db008806-16f6-48fc-8521-3d953709689d.name: A Day to Remember
db008806-16f6-48fc-8521-3d953709689d.label: Victory
db008806-16f6-48fc-8521-3d953709689d.lede: A Day to Remember played seven shows in its first year in Ocala, Florida, then signed to Victory Records, covered Kelly Clarkson, sued the label, released its own album mid-lawsuit and won a verdict.

bc1c8f3f-6f36-4086-a470-87ed813dd429.name: Alexisonfire
bc1c8f3f-6f36-4086-a470-87ed813dd429.label: Distort Entertainment
bc1c8f3f-6f36-4086-a470-87ed813dd429.lede: Five kids from St. Catharines took their name from a porn star's website, put three singers on one record and sold platinum in Canada. They broke up badly in 2011, then came back with an album, thirteen years after the last one, that won a Juno.

f73634fa-c89b-4bc3-8cd0-81891bcafa9e.name: American Nightmare
f73634fa-c89b-4bc3-8cd0-81891bcafa9e.label: Equal Vision Records
f73634fa-c89b-4bc3-8cd0-81891bcafa9e.lede: Wesley Eisold roadied for Ten Yard Fight, then started a Boston band that listened to the Smiths. The band lost its name to a cease and desist and watched his words turn up on Fall Out Boy records, then got the name back and ended up suing WWE over it.

a7572df1-aad3-4851-ab0c-6013a5dbbb6d.name: Andalusians
a7572df1-aad3-4851-ab0c-6013a5dbbb6d.label: Dischord
a7572df1-aad3-4851-ab0c-6013a5dbbb6d.lede: Basla Andolsun had played bass in Del Cielo and Beauty Pill. In 2007 she picked up a guitar, worked songs out on a four-track, and ended up with six of them on Dischord.

bad5bc3a-a2e8-41d7-95aa-b5734784fbb1.name: Antelope
bad5bc3a-a2e8-41d7-95aa-b5734784fbb1.label: Dischord
bad5bc3a-a2e8-41d7-95aa-b5734784fbb1.lede: Antelope had one guitar, three players and no fixed drummer: Bee Elvy and Mike Andre swapped kit and bass, and Justin Moyer played guitar over both. Dischord put out three records in five years, then the band quit in 2008.

99200bf8-65e3-4073-93f6-fb81a4078d61.name: Aquarium
99200bf8-65e3-4073-93f6-fb81a4078d61.label: Dischord
99200bf8-65e3-4073-93f6-fb81a4078d61.lede: A keyboard, a drum kit and a projector loaded with old school films: Aquarium played DC rooms, toured once, made one album, and Dischord put out a two-song 7" in 2009.

34837d89-0c07-4675-b39e-bd495364fcca.name: Artificial Peace
34837d89-0c07-4675-b39e-bd495364fcca.label: Dischord
34837d89-0c07-4675-b39e-bd495364fcca.lede: Four kids from Bethesda pulled one of the biggest crowds in early DC hardcore, recorded 17 songs in a single Inner Ear session, and broke up with three of them on Flex Your Head. The other 14 waited until 2010.

17e137fb-59e5-4fd7-af48-afc34995396c.name: Atreyu
17e137fb-59e5-4fd7-af48-afc34995396c.label: Victory Records
17e137fb-59e5-4fd7-af48-afc34995396c.lede: Yorba Linda kids named their band after the boy in The Neverending Story and took a Victory Records album to number 9 on the Billboard 200. Twenty-two years in, they parted ways with the singer who started it all at 14.

1f5b789d-afaf-45ca-a0d6-87502dcef08f.name: Autoclave
1f5b789d-afaf-45ca-a0d6-87502dcef08f.label: Dischord
1f5b789d-afaf-45ca-a0d6-87502dcef08f.lede: Christina Billotte and Mary Timony wrote for the same band for about a year, played roughly fifteen shows, and left one 7" behind before they split for four cities.

d67ff511-57b8-4d02-94d3-6c6a331c2ae4.name: Avail
d67ff511-57b8-4d02-94d3-6c6a331c2ae4.label: Lookout!
d67ff511-57b8-4d02-94d3-6c6a331c2ae4.lede: [[Joe Banks]] moved a Reston hardcore band into a Richmond rowhouse, put the drummer on the microphone, and spent a decade writing Richmond into the song titles. The band quit in 2007 without announcing it, then sold out The National in about ten seconds in 2019.

adf5ac61-4d7b-4cbc-95ce-ee2dc486f884.name: Bane
adf5ac61-4d7b-4cbc-95ce-ee2dc486f884.label: Equal Vision Records
adf5ac61-4d7b-4cbc-95ce-ee2dc486f884.lede: Aaron Dalbec was still a Converge guitarist when he started the band in Worcester that became Bane. It made four albums for Equal Vision, called Don't Wait Up its last in 2014, played a final show in Worcester in 2016, and came back for Stu Maguire in 2021 and for Boston in 2023.

172d89ba-95ab-4e30-92a2-fe836ba0601e.name: Battery
172d89ba-95ab-4e30-92a2-fe836ba0601e.label: Revelation
172d89ba-95ab-4e30-92a2-fe836ba0601e.lede: Battery started as Fury in Washington in 1990, sold better in Europe than at home, and broke up six months after its Revelation album. Twenty years on, a new song looked back at singer Brian McTernan's teenage stay in a mental hospital.

976b28a1-dd68-4c43-ba08-ba15b58963b2.name: Beauty Pill
976b28a1-dd68-4c43-ba08-ba15b58963b2.label: Dischord
976b28a1-dd68-4c43-ba08-ba15b58963b2.lede: Beauty Pill started as a Dischord band the Dischord crowd didn't quite know what to do with, then lived through Chad Clark's failing heart, an album recorded in a museum and a transplant without ever settling into one shape.

aa396ea8-6874-47d9-9331-47f39e37f991.name: Bed Maker
aa396ea8-6874-47d9-9331-47f39e37f991.label: Dischord
aa396ea8-6874-47d9-9331-47f39e37f991.lede: Four DC lifers played one show in February 2020 before the pandemic shut it down. The debut LP came out on Dischord in 2024, and a 7" followed in 2026.

8c016ef4-0d18-4795-86dd-35ec90a509c9.name: Beefeater
8c016ef4-0d18-4795-86dd-35ec90a509c9.label: Dischord
8c016ef4-0d18-4795-86dd-35ec90a509c9.lede: Tomas Squip, a vegetarian who had drummed in Red C, fronted a band called Beefeater for two years and two LPs, while Fred Smith's guitar taught DC punk to swing.

e5c7b94f-e264-473c-bb0f-37c85d4d5c70.name: Belle and Sebastian
e5c7b94f-e264-473c-bb0f-37c85d4d5c70.label: Matador
e5c7b94f-e264-473c-bb0f-37c85d4d5c70.lede: Stuart Murdoch spent seven years too ill to work, then found his songs on a Glasgow course for unemployed musicians. The band that grew around him beat Steps at the Brits, lost a singer mid-tour and, in 2017, left its drummer at a Walmart.

9a5d50be-8dff-4f2f-8852-aa4eafb8f985.name: Better Than a Thousand
9a5d50be-8dff-4f2f-8852-aa4eafb8f985.label: Revelation
9a5d50be-8dff-4f2f-8852-aa4eafb8f985.lede: Two guys whose band had gone quiet cut a youth crew demo in Atlanta, handed the mic to Ray Cappo between Shelter tours, and wound up playing America, Europe, Asia and South America without much rehearsal.

9463868f-edc8-427e-ac07-ea89698e5f15.name: Big Black
9463868f-edc8-427e-ac07-ea89698e5f15.label: Touch and Go
9463868f-edc8-427e-ac07-ea89698e5f15.lede: Steve Albini started Big Black alone at Northwestern with a drum machine, poached two guys from Naked Raygun, and spent six years making noise that was ugly on purpose and exact to the beat. Then he quit, on schedule, with the major labels at the door.

50d90400-e7ea-4465-92a5-404605e51ee7.name: Black Eyes
50d90400-e7ea-4465-92a5-404605e51ee7.label: Dischord
50d90400-e7ea-4465-92a5-404605e51ee7.lede: Two drummers face each other across the stage, a bassist stands at the front and another at the back, and one guitarist holds the middle. That was the whole band for three years and two albums, and they split before the second one came out. Twenty-one years after that, they made a third.

b2abb7e0-9375-4915-821f-287d2f7dac20.name: Bluetip
b2abb7e0-9375-4915-821f-287d2f7dac20.label: Dischord
b2abb7e0-9375-4915-821f-287d2f7dac20.lede: Two Swiz veterans started over in 1995 as The Ohio Blue Tip, went through five drummers in six years, and closed with a record that named Jason Farrell's next band.

b024b1bd-2020-4b7c-83f7-4660133c89fa.name: Bold
b024b1bd-2020-4b7c-83f7-4660133c89fa.label: Revelation
b024b1bd-2020-4b7c-83f7-4660133c89fa.lede: A Westchester band too young for the CBGB door cut one album in Youth of Today's studio, borrowed its look from Run-D.M.C. and Van Halen, and watched the record outlive the band by decades.

0798d15b-64e2-499f-9969-70167b1d8617.name: Boredoms
0798d15b-64e2-499f-9969-70167b1d8617.label: Warner Bros.
0798d15b-64e2-499f-9969-70167b1d8617.lede: Eye's other band drove an excavator through a club wall. Boredoms took that appetite to Warner Bros., the Lollapalooza main stage and sunset drum rituals for 77, 88 and 111 players.

8db9ae5b-4412-434a-aedd-dc2bb316c355.name: Brainiac
8db9ae5b-4412-434a-aedd-dc2bb316c355.label: Touch and Go
8db9ae5b-4412-434a-aedd-dc2bb316c355.lede: Brainiac came out of Dayton with a battered Moog, a singer who changed voices mid-song and a habit of wrecking anything that sounded like a hit. The band reportedly told Geffen where to go, and lost [[Tim Taylor]] in 1997 while making an Interscope album.

7bbe7d6d-1289-4a0d-9c55-3476edf2840f.name: Branch Manager
7bbe7d6d-1289-4a0d-9c55-3476edf2840f.label: Dischord
7bbe7d6d-1289-4a0d-9c55-3476edf2840f.lede: Branch Manager came out of Reston, Virginia, made two albums for Dischord, got Ian MacKaye to help mix the second, and broke up in December 1997 after a tour that went badly enough for the label to mention it.

502429d5-da95-4a78-bfc9-7c8cf93504e6.name: Burn
502429d5-da95-4a78-bfc9-7c8cf93504e6.label: Revelation
502429d5-da95-4a78-bfc9-7c8cf93504e6.lede: Burn put four songs on one Revelation seven-inch in 1990, with a swing and a stop-start menace New York hardcore hadn't heard, then waited twenty-seven years for a full-length.

2339bc21-aa92-4850-86f0-4bb9433910c8.name: Butthole Surfers
2339bc21-aa92-4850-86f0-4bb9433910c8.label: Touch and Go
2339bc21-aa92-4850-86f0-4bb9433910c8.lede: A Trinity University Accountant of the Year and an MBA student bought stolen strobe lights, toured with a naked dancer, made some of the strangest records of the eighties, then sued their own label and won.

ce18f6e0-4f3b-4819-ab53-5179bc9896c1.name: By a Thread
ce18f6e0-4f3b-4819-ab53-5179bc9896c1.label: Revelation
ce18f6e0-4f3b-4819-ab53-5179bc9896c1.lede: Two guitarists from the Vancouver hardcore band Strain slowed down in 1996, pressed one white-vinyl LP on Revelation in 1999, and have kept coming back to By a Thread ever since.

68025033-de1b-42f5-8a21-bedfb8895dda.name: Califone
68025033-de1b-42f5-8a21-bedfb8895dda.label: Thrill Jockey
68025033-de1b-42f5-8a21-bedfb8895dda.lede: What was left of Red Red Meat went through the junk drawer of American music and came back with bottles, hand drums, tape hiss and a heron-headed god from Tim Rutili's dreams.

04482c2e-88ab-4709-a412-85748b7ac825.name: Cap'n Jazz
04482c2e-88ab-4709-a412-85748b7ac825.label: Jade Tree
04482c2e-88ab-4709-a412-85748b7ac825.lede: Suburban Chicago teenagers with a French horn, an a-ha cover and a 28-word album title split up in Little Rock in 1995. Nearly every band that came out of the wreckage became someone's favorite.

81a3c11e-ac20-4bb4-8614-06b157e802d8.name: Chain of Strength
81a3c11e-ac20-4bb4-8614-06b157e802d8.label: Revelation
81a3c11e-ac20-4bb4-8614-06b157e802d8.lede: Chain of Strength put out two seven-inches in about three years. Ray Cappo signed them after hearing a demo in Ryan Hoffman's car, and the clothes drew as much argument as the songs.

b6a722a5-e776-43e4-a3a3-2bfa74b0fb44.name: Channels
b6a722a5-e776-43e4-a3a3-2bfa74b0fb44.label: Dischord
b6a722a5-e776-43e4-a3a3-2bfa74b0fb44.lede: J. Robbins and Janet Morgan put two lead voices in a trio with Darren Zentek, made one album, and stopped in 2006 when their baby son was diagnosed with SMA. Ten years later they came back with a single named for a face that needs slapping.

e754303f-655e-41f4-9dbe-b11b5614bd3d.name: Charalambides
e754303f-655e-41f4-9dbe-b11b5614bd3d.label: Kranky
e754303f-655e-41f4-9dbe-b11b5614bd3d.lede: Two clerks at a Houston record store named their band after a customer. They married, divorced and kept going, and when Tom Carter went into a coma in Berlin, other musicians made an album to pay his bills.

c08d2dcd-3c9a-4e5c-b444-c48936de2707.name: Chavez
c08d2dcd-3c9a-4e5c-b444-c48936de2707.label: Matador
c08d2dcd-3c9a-4e5c-b444-c48936de2707.lede: Chavez made two records for Matador, got a spin on Beavis and Butt-Head, and never officially broke up. They just wandered off to play with Johnny Cash, write for HBO and direct movies, and the records stayed in circulation among guitar players.

b755836a-0cb6-4577-a678-55a5a6402d70.name: Chiodos
b755836a-0cb6-4577-a678-55a5a6402d70.label: Equal Vision Records
b755836a-0cb6-4577-a678-55a5a6402d70.lede: Six kids from Davison, Michigan named their band after the effects brothers behind Killer Klowns from Outer Space, sold more than 39,000 copies of one album in a week, fired their singer, took him back, and ended up arguing over who gets to play the old songs.

a2496a3c-8f42-4b98-b780-6f8d64f56441.name: Circa Survive
a2496a3c-8f42-4b98-b780-6f8d64f56441.label: Equal Vision Records
a2496a3c-8f42-4b98-b780-6f8d64f56441.lede: Anthony Green quit Saosin because he was scared, then built a band in Philadelphia around effects-drenched guitars and that voice. It lasted eighteen years, through a major-label detour, a stay in a mental health facility and a relapse.

01b418b2-5e47-4ce2-9144-ad7d35214103.name: Circus Lupus
01b418b2-5e47-4ce2-9144-ad7d35214103.label: Dischord
01b418b2-5e47-4ce2-9144-ad7d35214103.lede: Chris Thomson left Ignition's bass behind, took a microphone to Madison and then to Washington, and Dischord put out two albums of the result. Joan Jett produced a single on the way out.

1649c891-eea0-45b2-8caf-c85d985ff3bd.name: CIV
1649c891-eea0-45b2-8caf-c85d985ff3bd.label: Revelation
1649c891-eea0-45b2-8caf-c85d985ff3bd.lede: Walter Schreifels wrote the songs, three Gorilla Biscuits played them, and a talk-show spoof the band shot itself landed on MTV's Buzz Bin and Beavis and Butt-head.

ae1b47d5-5128-431c-9d30-e08fd90e0767.name: Coheed and Cambria
ae1b47d5-5128-431c-9d30-e08fd90e0767.label: Equal Vision
ae1b47d5-5128-431c-9d30-e08fd90e0767.lede: Coheed and Cambria started in Nyack, New York, with a breakup over gas money. Thirty years later it has told one science-fiction story across ten of its eleven albums, gone gold on a hardcore label, and outlasted a rhythm section's addiction, rehab and a pharmacy robbery.

6d152109-c447-446d-9a06-3621c920bebd.name: Comeback Kid
6d152109-c447-446d-9a06-3621c920bebd.label: Victory
6d152109-c447-446d-9a06-3621c920bebd.lede: Two guitarists in a Winnipeg Christian hardcore band started a side project named for a Mario Lemieux headline. Then one of them walked up to the microphone and stayed there.

3da0eca9-11c3-42ba-958b-240af52474c1.name: Constant Elevation
3da0eca9-11c3-42ba-958b-240af52474c1.label: Revelation
3da0eca9-11c3-42ba-958b-240af52474c1.lede: Sammy Siegler sat in on a Movielife tour around 2002 and kept Vinnie Caruana's voice in his head for sixteen years. Then he wrote his first complete songs on a tiny acoustic and asked Caruana to scream over them.

d471b090-3866-4cf3-b8a0-476e11f30a58.name: Coriky
d471b090-3866-4cf3-b8a0-476e11f30a58.label: Dischord
d471b090-3866-4cf3-b8a0-476e11f30a58.lede: Ian MacKaye and Amy Farina of the Evens took Joe Lally back from Rome, practiced for three years, and played their first show in a church without a name. Then a pandemic delayed the record.

9ffa627f-32c2-4cb1-bfad-00cf348abc70.name: Cro-Mags
9ffa627f-32c2-4cb1-bfad-00cf348abc70.label: Victory
9ffa627f-32c2-4cb1-bfad-00cf348abc70.lede: Lower East Side kids, a Hare Krishna singer and a bassist who'd been in a punk band since he was eleven made the New York hardcore record every other band gets measured against. Then they spent forty years in court, and once backstage with a knife, over who owns the name.

6c13db70-bd59-44a0-8c6a-eeb0d0c8f40d.name: Crownhate Ruin
6c13db70-bd59-44a0-8c6a-eeb0d0c8f40d.label: Dischord
6c13db70-bd59-44a0-8c6a-eeb0d0c8f40d.lede: Fred Erskine and Joe McRedmond finished with Hoover in 1994 and were on stage as Crownhate Ruin barely two months later, with drummer Vin Novara and a darker set of songs. Some Hoover fans weren't thrilled. The band kept touring, made one album for Dischord, and was done by December 1996.

a1bdb520-0253-486e-a139-48a9c144a93e.name: Curl Up and Die
a1bdb520-0253-486e-a139-48a9c144a93e.label: Revelation
a1bdb520-0253-486e-a139-48a9c144a93e.lede: Self-described nerds from Las Vegas, Curl Up and Die plugged into a generator to play the desert, got booed for asking moshers not to punch girls, and named a seven-minute song after a Carson Daly lookalike contest.

4709dd69-1034-4634-9e88-d1099453b192.name: Dag Nasty
4709dd69-1034-4634-9e88-d1099453b192.label: Dischord
4709dd69-1034-4634-9e88-d1099453b192.lede: Brian Baker walked out of Minor Threat with songs that wanted a melody, and Dag Nasty got three singers in two years while making Can I Say, the record people still point to.

52ae8d28-e8f6-4ac5-8653-c9ffcc0bfc0f.name: Damnation A.D.
52ae8d28-e8f6-4ac5-8653-c9ffcc0bfc0f.label: Revelation
52ae8d28-e8f6-4ac5-8653-c9ffcc0bfc0f.lede: Ken Olden spent his days in D.C. youth crew band [[Battery]] and his nights in the same house tuning down to C for Damnation A.D., a darker band that loved The Cure as much as Crowbar.

df81eb3f-1267-4af1-a0f8-5319ab44c09c.name: Deadline
df81eb3f-1267-4af1-a0f8-5319ab44c09c.label: Dischord
df81eb3f-1267-4af1-a0f8-5319ab44c09c.lede: Brendan Canty picked up drumsticks at fifteen and was in a band within months. Deadline got three songs on Flex Your Head, opened for Flipper, and broke up in September 1982, leaving a last session that waited five years for a record.

db0e5c06-c091-46d4-bd42-5ba2ee299123.name: Deathfix
db0e5c06-c091-46d4-bd42-5ba2ee299123.label: Dischord
db0e5c06-c091-46d4-bd42-5ba2ee299123.lede: Brendan Canty, Fugazi's drummer, picked up a guitar and a microphone, found his keyboard player in the back of Bob Mould's Cadillac, and made a D.C. record in love with 1972.

4f416ed7-dda2-45de-a6f1-b986e861cf4b.name: Deerhunter
4f416ed7-dda2-45de-a6f1-b986e861cf4b.label: 4AD
4f416ed7-dda2-45de-a6f1-b986e861cf4b.lede: Bradford Cox started Deerhunter in Atlanta under a name he hated, lost his bassist in 2004 and watched fans download his records before he could release them. By Halcyon Digest it was the indie band a lot of people name first.

e3d01dcb-eb41-4ce9-8506-bfd70aa8d651.name: Didjits
e3d01dcb-eb41-4ce9-8506-bfd70aa8d651.label: Touch and Go
e3d01dcb-eb41-4ce9-8506-bfd70aa8d651.lede: Rick Sims fronted the Didjits in sunglasses and a feather boa, with his brother Brad on drums, and made Touch and Go records that mostly ran under 30 minutes. One song, Killboy Powerhead, then rode the Offspring's Smash into more than 11 million homes.

b93697af-a318-417a-b16e-a9eb47fbe2f8.name: Don Caballero
b93697af-a318-417a-b16e-a9eb47fbe2f8.label: Touch and Go
b93697af-a318-417a-b16e-a9eb47fbe2f8.lede: Don Caballero named itself after an SCTV mob boss, built its sound around a drummer called the Octopus, and went through bassists and club walls until its American Don line-up ended in a snowbank on I-75. The man at the kit, Damon Che, kept the name going anyway.

fac027c9-e8db-4546-9515-9d48d1a7185c.name: Down to Nothing
fac027c9-e8db-4546-9515-9d48d1a7185c.label: Revelation
fac027c9-e8db-4546-9515-9d48d1a7185c.lede: David Wood and Daniel Spector, friends since age five, started a straight edge band in Richmond, wrote a record that sends fans to Belle Isle, and kept it going while Wood played bass for Terror almost 300 days a year.

9b0a6218-d0ad-4131-8c80-53b8f78913ee.name: Drain
9b0a6218-d0ad-4131-8c80-53b8f78913ee.label: Revelation
9b0a6218-d0ad-4131-8c80-53b8f78913ee.lede: Drain began as UC Santa Cruz students trying every style at once and turned into a thrash-crossover band in board shorts. Revelation put out the debut just as touring stopped, a San Jose parking-lot show in June 2021 drew 2,000 people and helped start a hardcore boom, and Epitaph came next.

95692409-79fa-407c-beff-996d630f03f7.name: Drowningman
95692409-79fa-407c-beff-996d630f03f7.label: Revelation
95692409-79fa-407c-beff-996d630f03f7.lede: Drowningman started in a Burlington, Vermont basement, went through at least 19 members in ten years, and blew up a tape machine making Rock and Roll Killing Machine. Its way out of a label deal was an album so bad nobody would release it.

88a6037e-87ba-492a-a54c-c927aa620cb8.name: Earth Crisis
88a6037e-87ba-492a-a54c-c927aa620cb8.label: Victory
88a6037e-87ba-492a-a54c-c927aa620cb8.lede: Karl Buechner, a Syracuse skater, spent three years finding four other vegans who didn't drink, then helped invent metalcore with them and took vegan straight edge onto 48 Hours, CNN and, eventually, Geraldo.

63b1219b-1910-4dfc-8ea5-6df6b2e7ac75.name: Edie Sedgwick
63b1219b-1910-4dfc-8ea5-6df6b2e7ac75.label: Dischord
63b1219b-1910-4dfc-8ea5-6df6b2e7ac75.lede: Justin Moyer played bass in El Guapo, then put on a wig and a dress and became Andy Warhol's most famous Superstar. As Edie Sedgwick he sang songs named for Angelina Jolie, Rob Lowe and Ol' Dirty Bastard, and Ian MacKaye produced some of them.

cbdd4684-3db9-476c-a0a9-5e2ad7c728a7.name: The Effects
cbdd4684-3db9-476c-a0a9-5e2ad7c728a7.label: Dischord
cbdd4684-3db9-476c-a0a9-5e2ad7c728a7.lede: Devin Ocampo, Matt Dowling and David Rich had spent years in other people's bands and finally ended up in one together. They cut nine songs with J. Robbins in Baltimore and sent them to Dischord.

2d8d08d8-c1b1-4494-b299-32dd4a7f8dfe.name: Egg Hunt
2d8d08d8-c1b1-4494-b299-32dd4a7f8dfe.label: Dischord
2d8d08d8-c1b1-4494-b299-32dd4a7f8dfe.lede: In the spring of 1986 Ian MacKaye and Jeff Nelson flew to London for a distribution meeting and spent Easter weekend in a garage studio in Wood Green. Four songs later, the two Minor Threat founders had made the last music they would ever record together.

be23bf0a-67c6-4b2f-ba2a-89d983f5ebdd.name: El Guapo
be23bf0a-67c6-4b2f-ba2a-89d983f5ebdd.label: Dischord
be23bf0a-67c6-4b2f-ba2a-89d983f5ebdd.lede: Justin Moyer and Rafael Cohen started a band with an accordion and an oboe, made a Dischord record in a Philadelphia living room, then found a Chicago band with beer-commercial backing already owned the name.

751b1385-9595-46ee-b634-8f90f892682a.name: Eleventh Dream Day
751b1385-9595-46ee-b634-8f90f892682a.label: Thrill Jockey
751b1385-9595-46ee-b634-8f90f892682a.lede: Rick Rizzo and Janet Beveridge Bean started the band in a Louisville punk house and took it to Chicago, where Atlantic offered seven records and kept them for three. They've kept making loud ones, on their own schedule, ever since.

b3250fd8-d202-4d4a-8fb3-1fdf88176aff.name: Elliott
b3250fd8-d202-4d4a-8fb3-1fdf88176aff.label: Revelation
b3250fd8-d202-4d4a-8fb3-1fdf88176aff.lede: Three Louisville hardcore veterans set out to sound like none of their old bands, then added pianos, samplers and a string section. They broke up in 2003, seven months after their third album, and came back nineteen years later.

9d1ad8e3-8740-429a-bdc5-52f96a9c4431.name: Embrace
9d1ad8e3-8740-429a-bdc5-52f96a9c4431.label: Dischord
9d1ad8e3-8740-429a-bdc5-52f96a9c4431.lede: Embrace played nine shows in under a year, and the album came out a year after they split. It's where Ian MacKaye slowed hardcore down to see what else it could say.

899baef6-af48-4caa-aff6-c1562a5dc12d.name: Engine Kid
899baef6-af48-4caa-aff6-c1562a5dc12d.label: Revelation
899baef6-af48-4caa-aff6-c1562a5dc12d.lede: Seattle straight edge kids who wanted to be Slint recorded in Steve Albini's basement, covered Coltrane for twelve minutes on Revelation, then split. Their guitarist went on to found Southern Lord and Sunn O))).

53e6b385-b421-4516-9f03-b2bc4a958d51.name: Fall Silent
53e6b385-b421-4516-9f03-b2bc4a958d51.label: Revelation
53e6b385-b421-4516-9f03-b2bc4a958d51.lede: Fall Silent started in Reno with Crowbar records and punk 7"s, got Levi Watson beaten up in Salt Lake City over one song, and found its biggest audience in Japan because Max Ward wore their shirt. Watson crashed the car in New Jersey in 2002, the band ended a year later, and it came back in 2015 with Watson now a math teacher.

e866e006-4c80-4753-b53f-1bc5d88ccddd.name: Faraquet
e866e006-4c80-4753-b53f-1bc5d88ccddd.label: Dischord
e866e006-4c80-4753-b53f-1bc5d88ccddd.lede: Faraquet played so few shows in its first life that the 2025 comeback sold out Tokyo twice. In between came one album of odd meters and melody, a tour with Fugazi, and a trip to Brazil.

c6d7e9ab-e369-4dc2-b6a8-1fa7def9c069.name: Farside
c6d7e9ab-e369-4dc2-b6a8-1fa7def9c069.label: Revelation
c6d7e9ab-e369-4dc2-b6a8-1fa7def9c069.lede: Farside came out of Orange County with Zack de la Rocha on second guitar, passed on the major labels when punk went gold in 1994, and broke up after three albums on Revelation.

6ca65199-3330-4cb6-8589-f57930d60c28.name: Fastbreak
6ca65199-3330-4cb6-8589-f57930d60c28.label: Revelation
6ca65199-3330-4cb6-8589-f57930d60c28.lede: Fastbreak started in a Connecticut suburb at fifteen, named their first album after a Jerky Boys prank call, moved to Boston, signed to Revelation, and called it quits in 2000.

136e19b3-8da4-43c2-86f1-87e161710d2c.name: Fell to Low
136e19b3-8da4-43c2-86f1-87e161710d2c.label: Revelation
136e19b3-8da4-43c2-86f1-87e161710d2c.lede: Fell to Low came out of Ojai loving Slint and Unwound, signed to Revelation, and made one album: six songs, mastered by Shellac's Bob Weston, ending on a three-part closer named for the stages of a Saturn V.

c6332c9e-a2e3-4d2d-8ad7-a6b3ee837717.name: Fidelity Jones
c6332c9e-a2e3-4d2d-8ad7-a6b3ee837717.label: Dischord
c6332c9e-a2e3-4d2d-8ad7-a6b3ee837717.lede: Two Beefeater refugees started a band with the people they lived with, spent two years stretching punk into stranger shapes, quit in 1990, and came back in 2023 after a podcast got them talking about old cover songs.

430d9771-8feb-4b81-ba2d-c33ddcd0c8c1.name: Fire Party
430d9771-8feb-4b81-ba2d-c33ddcd0c8c1.label: Dischord
430d9771-8feb-4b81-ba2d-c33ddcd0c8c1.lede: Four friends started Fire Party in a D.C. basement in 1986, made two EPs for Dischord, and spent three months in Europe opening for Scream, where Dave Grohl was the drummer. At home people kept calling them an all-girl band. They kept asking to be judged on the songs.

e5a37410-100f-4703-afa0-14778c6b2a99.name: Forced Order
e5a37410-100f-4703-afa0-14778c6b2a99.label: Revelation
e5a37410-100f-4703-afa0-14778c6b2a99.lede: Five Southern Californians from Twitching Tongues, Disgrace and Soul Search spent four years rebuilding 1990s Cleveland hardcore, crunch and all, then played their last show in the Santa Ana club where they'd once celebrated Vanished Crusade.

50e68a47-b6e4-4178-84d5-8955206a0b7f.name: Freakwater
50e68a47-b6e4-4178-84d5-8955206a0b7f.label: Thrill Jockey
50e68a47-b6e4-4178-84d5-8955206a0b7f.lede: Two Kentucky singers recorded harmonies in a basement in 1985 and went on making honky-tonk for indie crowds for thirty years, through a long silence and a reissue that restarted them.

f9e0402f-c675-46d9-985f-07001bba6480.name: French Toast
f9e0402f-c675-46d9-985f-07001bba6480.label: Dischord
f9e0402f-c675-46d9-985f-07001bba6480.lede: James Canty and Jerry Busher had spent twenty years in the same D.C. rooms without sharing a band. Once they did, they traded guitar, bass, drums and keys song by song and sounded like a crowd.

19202b40-eb93-48a0-b6fc-fce9568182aa.name: Fucked Up
19202b40-eb93-48a0-b6fc-fce9568182aa.label: Matador
19202b40-eb93-48a0-b6fc-fce9568182aa.lede: Fucked Up came out of Toronto hardcore with stage names, a blizzard of seven-inches and a screamer called Pink Eyes. Then came flutes, a Polaris Prize, a 77-minute rock opera and a zodiac cycle that took twenty years to finish.

233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace.name: Fugazi
233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace.label: Dischord
233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace.lede: Fugazi kept the door at five dollars across more than a thousand shows, and when the man who once offered the Rolling Stones their own label came backstage, they politely stayed on Dischord.

74963434-dcb6-4b14-98cc-99873b06db66.name: Future Islands
74963434-dcb6-4b14-98cc-99873b06db66.label: 4AD
74963434-dcb6-4b14-98cc-99873b06db66.lede: Three friends from eastern North Carolina played show after show for eight years before four minutes on Letterman, a chest-thump and a growl, made the whole country ask who Sam Herring was.

c67fddd4-970b-4bfb-8996-314c29b08f27.name: Gameface
c67fddd4-970b-4bfb-8996-314c29b08f27.label: Revelation
c67fddd4-970b-4bfb-8996-314c29b08f27.lede: Jeff Caudill and Todd Trout kept running into the same two faces at Orange County punk shows, and in 1990 made them a band. Their drummer died in 1994, they carried on as his memorial, and by the late '90s Gameface had become the warmest-sounding band on Revelation.

d8661c02-f423-4d72-8044-40ff05daf7a1.name: Gang of Four
d8661c02-f423-4d72-8044-40ff05daf7a1.label: EMI
d8661c02-f423-4d72-8044-40ff05daf7a1.lede: Four Leeds students took their name from a Chinese political purge, walked off Top of the Pops rather than change one word, and played a guitar so brittle and funky that Flea, Kurt Cobain and Michael Stipe all pointed to it as an influence.

93709b1c-57ae-445c-9033-f15ca67b2de0.name: Garrison
93709b1c-57ae-445c-9033-f15ca67b2de0.label: Revelation
93709b1c-57ae-445c-9033-f15ca67b2de0.lede: Joe Grillo and Ed McNamara wrote songs in Boston for a year before their first show, then played hundreds more across the US, Europe and Japan, trying to make Drive Like Jehu sound like a pop band.

837cd182-8da4-4c1c-924c-03daf72f0237.name: Girls Against Boys
837cd182-8da4-4c1c-924c-03daf72f0237.label: Touch and Go
837cd182-8da4-4c1c-924c-03daf72f0237.lede: Girls Against Boys started as studio tinkering between Eli Janney and Fugazi's drummer, picked up a singer and a second bass, and made three records for Touch and Go that got them on late-night TV and the UK chart. Then Geffen signed them and told them, mid-tour, that it was about to stop existing.

55ffb0fe-e4e1-4674-b7b0-efd1e1fdf6d4.name: Give
55ffb0fe-e4e1-4674-b7b0-efd1e1fdf6d4.label: Revelation
55ffb0fe-e4e1-4674-b7b0-efd1e1fdf6d4.lede: Crucial John Scharbach named Give while deployed in Iraq, then spent six years pressing flower-covered 7"s for half the labels in hardcore before Revelation, the label that shaped his ear, put out the 12".

429f9fbf-0a0b-4a9e-a88c-94d48aa466ed.name: Glassjaw
429f9fbf-0a0b-4a9e-a88c-94d48aa466ed.label: Warner Bros.
429f9fbf-0a0b-4a9e-a88c-94d48aa466ed.lede: Two campers from Long Island made a debut on Roadrunner, quit the label and told fans to stay away from it. The third album took fifteen years, and Amazon leaked it first.

3648db01-b29d-4ab9-835c-83f6a5068fe4.name: Godspeed You! Black Emperor
3648db01-b29d-4ab9-835c-83f6a5068fe4.label: Constellation
3648db01-b29d-4ab9-835c-83f6a5068fe4.lede: A Montreal collective with no singer and no use for your approval makes hour-long records about the end of the world, gets held by the FBI at an Oklahoma gas station, and calls the gala that just handed it a prize insane.

0320a32e-b781-40df-bf48-5cb5ee842762.name: Gorilla Biscuits
0320a32e-b781-40df-bf48-5cb5ee842762.label: Revelation
0320a32e-b781-40df-bf48-5cb5ee842762.lede: Three Queens kids took their name from quaalude slang, then put out Start Today, the most cheerful straight edge record in New York hardcore and, 100,000 CDs later, the best seller Revelation has.

9b952ee8-d45d-4a26-8066-57849d871e06.name: Government Issue
9b952ee8-d45d-4a26-8066-57849d871e06.label: Dischord
9b952ee8-d45d-4a26-8066-57849d871e06.lede: [[John Stabb]] outlasted almost a dozen bandmates in nine years, and Government Issue kept changing its sound whether the hardcore kids liked it or not.

c9065214-ba09-4c2c-b341-35713b702264.name: Gray Matter
c9065214-ba09-4c2c-b341-35713b702264.label: Dischord
c9065214-ba09-4c2c-b341-35713b702264.lede: Dante Ferrando and Mark Haggerty walked out of Iron Cross, went back to the friends they'd played with since junior high, and made hardcore sing. The band broke up for college, came back, and Ferrando went on to open the Black Cat.

7e571e09-887e-4544-b993-eb75e7837ec1.name: Grouper
7e571e09-887e-4544-b993-eb75e7837ec1.label: Kranky
7e571e09-887e-4544-b993-eb75e7837ec1.lede: Liz Harris grew up in a commune called The Group, took her stage name from what the kids there called each other, and has recorded under tape hiss thick enough that a microwave beep and a fever both ended up on the records.

7d663fe4-debe-495f-a8f3-202c8293f0bd.name: Growing
7d663fe4-debe-495f-a8f3-202c8293f0bd.label: Kranky
7d663fe4-debe-495f-a8f3-202c8293f0bd.lede: Kevin Doria played bass, Joe Denardo played left-handed guitar, and in Olympia they ran volume pedals into several amps at once and called it Growing. Brooklyn gave them a beat; the comeback gave them sides that run 20 minutes.

6c85f4c3-026c-4c16-9a7c-f546f42ed0fb.name: Guided by Voices
6c85f4c3-026c-4c16-9a7c-f546f42ed0fb.label: Matador
6c85f4c3-026c-4c16-9a7c-f546f42ed0fb.lede: A Dayton fourth-grade teacher who once pitched a college no-hitter spent a decade making four-track records almost nobody heard. Then he got discovered, quit the classroom, and has now put out 44 albums as Guided by Voices.

64368968-d520-49ea-a248-9ccc29e1467f.name: Hammered Hulls
64368968-d520-49ea-a248-9ccc29e1467f.label: Dischord
64368968-d520-49ea-a248-9ccc29e1467f.lede: The kid on the cover of Minor Threat's first record sings, the guitarist from Helium plays bass, and two DC road dogs fill out a band that may have made the last record ever finished at Inner Ear.

4c18be5e-2e53-41a4-a4a1-d9080ff88f8c.name: Happy Go Licky
4c18be5e-2e53-41a4-a4a1-d9080ff88f8c.label: Dischord
4c18be5e-2e53-41a4-a4a1-d9080ff88f8c.lede: Four members of Rites of Spring came back in spring 1987 with tape loops, half-improvised songs and no studio. They played seven shows, all in Washington, and broke up on New Year's Day.

40b7efb7-1268-4a80-b354-600afdcbe9e2.name: Hatebreed
40b7efb7-1268-4a80-b354-600afdcbe9e2.label: Victory
40b7efb7-1268-4a80-b354-600afdcbe9e2.lede: A prep cook's weekend band got thrown off Warped Tour, found a home in metal, and watched its singer take over the host's chair on MTV2's Headbangers Ball.

194eeda1-e662-43bc-b9be-32fc1afecc8b.name: Hawthorne Heights
194eeda1-e662-43bc-b9be-32fc1afecc8b.label: Victory
194eeda1-e662-43bc-b9be-32fc1afecc8b.lede: Hawthorne Heights took its name from a hotel sign in Ohio, made Victory Records' biggest-selling debut, landed at No. 3 on the Billboard 200 and sued the label, all in about two years.

198bed0f-a246-4116-9c7a-0140cbd372b7.name: Himsa
198bed0f-a246-4116-9c7a-0140cbd372b7.label: Revelation
198bed0f-a246-4116-9c7a-0140cbd372b7.lede: Seattle hardcore kids flipped a word for nonviolence into a band name, played through a dozen members, said no to a lot of tours, and quit right after what was reportedly their best record. Eight years on, they came back on Halloween.

d8e0e0b1-8cd9-40c7-b413-71cfcaa90547.name: Holy Rollers
d8e0e0b1-8cd9-40c7-b413-71cfcaa90547.label: Dischord
d8e0e0b1-8cd9-40c7-b413-71cfcaa90547.lede: Holy Rollers were a DC trio who, in 1989, did what nobody else in the Dischord orbit was doing: all three sang at once, in harmony.

d691df14-6955-4cae-9dcc-318fb7d75984.name: Hoover
d691df14-6955-4cae-9dcc-318fb7d75984.label: Dischord
d691df14-6955-4cae-9dcc-318fb7d75984.lede: A guitarist who kept playing along at rehearsals turned Victor Deluxe into Hoover: three singers, one nearly hour-long album, and a split once the tour ended.

b3aa7443-5572-4c1f-99e5-a91e13cd3e5b.name: Iceburn
b3aa7443-5572-4c1f-99e5-a91e13cd3e5b.label: Revelation
b3aa7443-5572-4c1f-99e5-a91e13cd3e5b.lede: Salt Lake City straight edge kids cover Miles Davis on a hardcore label, grow into a seven-piece free jazz collective, go quiet for two decades, then return with two songs that fill an entire LP.

4d9fb84a-8104-48c1-aa16-21f53c9053cc.name: Ignite
4d9fb84a-8104-48c1-aa16-21f53c9053cc.label: Revelation
4d9fb84a-8104-48c1-aa16-21f53c9053cc.lede: Ignite formed in Orange County and found its first big crowds in Germany. Along the way came a U2 cover its label vetoed, a singer who spent almost three years in Pennywise, and a replacement who auditioned by singing over two Ignite instrumentals.

3cb2b7d6-1f0b-4ac5-b67f-52132f3d3b61.name: Ignition
3cb2b7d6-1f0b-4ac5-b67f-52132f3d3b61.label: Dischord
3cb2b7d6-1f0b-4ac5-b67f-52132f3d3b61.lede: Alec MacKaye and Chris Bald took what was left of Faith, added a Gray Matter drummer and a bassist who sometimes reached for a saxophone, and spent three years playing sets that could end in wreckage. The twenty-six songs they left behind fit on one CD.

f8a4cb28-0443-48af-b58a-b2b2ab51206d.name: In My Eyes
f8a4cb28-0443-48af-b58a-b2b2ab51206d.label: Revelation
f8a4cb28-0443-48af-b58a-b2b2ab51206d.lede: Anthony Pappalardo got thrown out of Ten Yard Fight and had In My Eyes going within two months, a Boston straight edge band with a rule against X imagery. It made two Revelation records and quit before it got old.

0049c4d7-6459-4b54-a865-fd19969f427f.name: Inside Out
0049c4d7-6459-4b54-a865-fd19969f427f.label: Revelation
0049c4d7-6459-4b54-a865-fd19969f427f.lede: Inside Out put out one seven-inch, toured the East Coast once and played a last show in Long Beach in May 1991. The title they'd picked for the second record went with Zack de la Rocha to Los Angeles.

f626335d-d234-408d-a67c-37a3c2c7e98a.name: Integrity
f626335d-d234-408d-a67c-37a3c2c7e98a.label: Victory
f626335d-d234-408d-a67c-37a3c2c7e98a.lede: Dwid Hellion was printing T-shirts for an invented straight edge band when he decided to make it real. Integrity went on to the darkest corner of Victory Records, and moved to Belgium after its singer met a girl on tour.

b23e8a63-8f47-4882-b55b-df2c92ef400e.name: Interpol
b23e8a63-8f47-4882-b55b-df2c92ef400e.label: Matador
b23e8a63-8f47-4882-b55b-df2c92ef400e.lede: Daniel Kessler found his bassist in an NYU philosophy class and his drummer in a vintage clothing shop, and Interpol went on to make Pitchfork's record of 2002. It left Matador for Capitol, came back, and in 2024 played to an estimated 160,000 in Mexico City.

c235e5fd-4144-4e53-95ff-b33dc5f239c8.name: Into Another
c235e5fd-4144-4e53-95ff-b33dc5f239c8.label: Revelation
c235e5fd-4144-4e53-95ff-b33dc5f239c8.lede: A Youth of Today singer, a Bold drummer and a thrash bassist put a Wurlitzer into hard rock, and the hardcore kids stagedived anyway, until a major label shipped the album with somebody else's music on the disc.

13afe528-54f1-4955-bbec-a4bafb590edb.name: Iron Cross
13afe528-54f1-4955-bbec-a4bafb590edb.label: Dischord
13afe528-54f1-4955-bbec-a4bafb590edb.lede: Sab Grey moved into the Dischord House in 1981 with an Oi! haircut and started what Wikipedia counts as the first band in the US to take on both the skinhead look and the sound. Three songs on Flex Your Head, one EP and one song called "Crucified" later, the band was being picketed in print while the song went off to live in other people's hands.

016fba14-1fc6-4986-86c2-2113ec9b28de.name: Jawbox
016fba14-1fc6-4986-86c2-2113ec9b28de.label: Dischord
016fba14-1fc6-4986-86c2-2113ec9b28de.lede: Jawbox sent Atlantic a list of demands and Atlantic said yes to every line. The band got a song on Beavis and Butt-Head, and hate mail from D.C.

dfebd6c0-dae7-4cc8-a8e9-0dbaa382209f.name: The Jesus Lizard
dfebd6c0-dae7-4cc8-a8e9-0dbaa382209f.label: Touch and Go
dfebd6c0-dae7-4cc8-a8e9-0dbaa382209f.lede: Two Scratch Acid refugees moved to Chicago, found a guitarist and a drummer, and made four records with Steve Albini. Then came Capitol, a split, and Rack, 26 years after the last album.

675ec992-a8e4-41f8-b28b-1aad0c8a9ad1.name: Jets to Brazil
675ec992-a8e4-41f8-b28b-1aad0c8a9ad1.label: Jade Tree
675ec992-a8e4-41f8-b28b-1aad0c8a9ad1.lede: Blake Schwarzenbach came out of Jawbreaker's breakup, got turned down by Geffen, and took a band name off a poster in Breakfast at Tiffany's. The first album sold more than anything else Jade Tree ever released.

0f2fea44-7e03-47f9-86e6-91d0a22fd0ee.name: Joan of Arc
0f2fea44-7e03-47f9-86e6-91d0a22fd0ee.label: Jade Tree
0f2fea44-7e03-47f9-86e6-91d0a22fd0ee.lede: Joan of Arc broke up after its first show, drew a 1.9 from Pitchfork, paired ex-members off by pulling names from a hat and rewrote Orwell with the band in the cast. Tim Kinsella was the only constant for all 25 years.

d1ab8ca8-fb9f-4e78-a422-3cd5406dc0b1.name: The Jon Spencer Blues Explosion
d1ab8ca8-fb9f-4e78-a422-3cd5406dc0b1.label: Matador
d1ab8ca8-fb9f-4e78-a422-3cd5406dc0b1.lede: A Pussy Galore veteran, a guitarist from Appleton, Wisconsin and a drummer from Queens turned the blues into a New York noise machine with two guitars, drums and a theremin, and talked Beck, the Beastie Boys, R.L. Burnside and Weird Al into coming along.

3827fbb6-e219-4e2d-9af8-35cc9a7d8d8e.name: Judge
3827fbb6-e219-4e2d-9af8-35cc9a7d8d8e.label: Revelation
3827fbb6-e219-4e2d-9af8-35cc9a7d8d8e.lede: Mike Ferraro quit Youth of Today because he couldn't keep muzzling himself, then wrote Judge's songs so hard the crowds started throwing them back at him. He walked away in 1991 and stayed gone for twenty years.

c5300096-cfb0-4801-b146-166e2d02f08a.name: Kid Dynamite
c5300096-cfb0-4801-b146-166e2d02f08a.label: Jade Tree
c5300096-cfb0-4801-b146-166e2d02f08a.lede: Dan Yemin and Dave Wagenschutz left Lifetime behind, found a singer who was headed for film school, and fit 38 songs onto two Jade Tree records. The band ended in February 2000, then kept coming back for benefits and festivals until 2013.

c2006163-bbbc-4f17-b1e6-a3fc7d2df156.name: Kill Holiday
c2006163-bbbc-4f17-b1e6-a3fc7d2df156.label: Revelation
c2006163-bbbc-4f17-b1e6-a3fc7d2df156.lede: Two Unbroken members, Steven Miller and Rob Moran, traded San Diego's metallic hardcore for long, moody indie rock. Four releases later, Revelation put out the seven-minute songs.

6a2f72b1-d660-409e-b190-6470157d3a38.name: Killdozer
6a2f72b1-d660-409e-b190-6470157d3a38.label: Touch and Go
6a2f72b1-d660-409e-b190-6470157d3a38.lede: Three Madison guys took their name from a TV movie about a possessed bulldozer, dedicated an EP to a folk singer who was still alive, handed Butch Vig the record that got him the Nirvana job, and signed off on a tour called Fuck You, We Quit!

f323fac7-b32e-49d5-b0ea-ef66fcf61416.name: Kiss It Goodbye
f323fac7-b32e-49d5-b0ea-ef66fcf61416.label: Revelation
f323fac7-b32e-49d5-b0ea-ef66fcf61416.lede: Tim Singer and Keith Huckins left Deadguy, took the rhythm section of Rorschach, and moved to Seattle to make one album. They split before the Sub Pop EP they'd recorded could come out.

7cf7ef41-9637-4bf2-ae99-d8d6611ccdc6.name: Labradford
7cf7ef41-9637-4bf2-ae99-d8d6611ccdc6.label: Kranky
7cf7ef41-9637-4bf2-ae99-d8d6611ccdc6.lede: Labradford took its name from a Louisville basketball player, and its first 7-inch landed on the desk of a Chicago distributor so squarely that two men there started Kranky just to release the album. Years later the band drifted to a stop without ever announcing one.

c9329809-8510-45b9-9202-5640398ddaee.name: Lifetime
c9329809-8510-45b9-9202-5640398ddaee.label: Jade Tree
c9329809-8510-45b9-9202-5640398ddaee.lede: Dan Yemin moved from Michigan to New Jersey in 1989 to start a band. Two Jade Tree records and about 45 minutes later, Lifetime was done, and the next decade's emo bands were covering the songs.

978a36f7-85c6-44ca-a02e-7564e8fa8284.name: Lightning Bolt
978a36f7-85c6-44ca-a02e-7564e8fa8284.label: Load Records
978a36f7-85c6-44ca-a02e-7564e8fa8284.lede: Two Brians from a Providence art school set up on the floor wherever the crowd happens to be: one on a bass strung with banjo strings, one drumming with a telephone mic strapped inside a mask.

c8003d4e-cc21-491e-9bab-fc986cdc0ce0.name: Living Hell
c8003d4e-cc21-491e-9bab-fc986cdc0ce0.label: Revelation
c8003d4e-cc21-491e-9bab-fc986cdc0ce0.lede: Members of three dead New England hardcore bands started Living Hell in 2007. Their demo got pressed by two labels, then Revelation put out The Lost and the Damned, which ends in more than five minutes of static.

4f2c565b-ac40-4678-ba61-4fcf3b97edbc.name: Loscil
4f2c565b-ac40-4678-ba61-4fcf3b97edbc.label: Kranky
4f2c565b-ac40-4678-ba61-4fcf3b97edbc.lede: Scott Morgan drummed for Destroyer, named his own project after a line of Csound code and sent a demo to Chicago. Kranky has been releasing the results since, long records about Vancouver's harbors, islands and weather.

42faad37-8aaa-42e4-a300-5a7dae79ed24.name: Low
42faad37-8aaa-42e4-a300-5a7dae79ed24.label: Sub Pop
42faad37-8aaa-42e4-a300-5a7dae79ed24.lede: A married couple from Duluth, members of the LDS Church, started Low in 1993 and played as slowly and softly as they could while grunge was loud. They kept at it for almost thirty years, until Mimi Parker's death in November 2022 ended the band.

5af88bca-9c13-424a-b63c-b5c96c69cb0e.name: Lungfish
5af88bca-9c13-424a-b63c-b5c96c69cb0e.label: Dischord
5af88bca-9c13-424a-b63c-b5c96c69cb0e.lede: A tattoo artist who read poems over tape loops started a band that held one riff until it turned into weather. Lungfish made eleven albums for Dischord, most with Ian MacKaye producing, and sounded like nobody else on the label.

28c5d97f-4321-4ef4-8ac2-d9d93b0eb16c.name: Man or Astro-man?
28c5d97f-4321-4ef4-8ac2-d9d93b0eb16c.label: Touch and Go
28c5d97f-4321-4ef4-8ac2-d9d93b0eb16c.lede: Auburn students in space jumpsuits swore they were aliens sent to play surf music, then backed it up with tesla coils, six John Peel sessions and a second touring band made of their own clones.

fff14e91-ae03-4105-8fbb-3a318d6c01ca.name: Marginal Man
fff14e91-ae03-4105-8fbb-3a318d6c01ca.label: Dischord
fff14e91-ae03-4105-8fbb-3a318d6c01ca.lede: Marginal Man ran two guitars when DC hardcore mostly ran one, took its name from a sociology class, and said goodbye with two sold-out sets at the 9:30 Club, the room where it had started.

312c14d9-7897-4608-944a-c5b1c76ae682.name: The Meatmen
312c14d9-7897-4608-944a-c5b1c76ae682.label: Touch and Go
312c14d9-7897-4608-944a-c5b1c76ae682.lede: Robert Vermeulen taught third and fifth grade in Williamston, Michigan, and ran a punk zine off the school copier at 3 a.m. As Tesco Vee he fronted the Meatmen, the dirtiest band in hardcore, and by 1983 had two Minor Threat guitarists playing behind him.

c545a7bf-c8d7-4368-8009-22e19d8911ce.name: Medications
c545a7bf-c8d7-4368-8009-22e19d8911ce.label: Dischord
c545a7bf-c8d7-4368-8009-22e19d8911ce.lede: Devin Ocampo and Chad Molter had been swapping instruments since high school. After Faraquet they started Medications, made two records for Dischord in two years, and came back five years later with a third that put the harmonies out front.

151cbcfa-4618-4f26-a769-f15d33743262.name: Milemarker
151cbcfa-4618-4f26-a769-f15d33743262.label: Jade Tree
151cbcfa-4618-4f26-a769-f15d33743262.lede: Milemarker started in Chapel Hill as a collective, set its drum kit on fire, then moved to Chicago to make synth-punk for Jade Tree with Steve Albini behind the board. It never announced a breakup, which is how a band ends up on a U.S. tour in 2017 with two members living in Germany.

db9d25d7-a85b-4a29-b2ff-8f5b69ed691e.name: Mission of Burma
db9d25d7-a85b-4a29-b2ff-8f5b69ed691e.label: Matador
db9d25d7-a85b-4a29-b2ff-8f5b69ed691e.lede: Mission of Burma lasted four years the first time, put out one EP and one album, and ended when Roger Miller's ears gave out. Nineteen years later the Boston band everyone had been covering came back and made four more records as loud as the first.

a96ac800-bfcb-412a-8a63-0a98df600700.name: Modest Mouse
a96ac800-bfcb-412a-8a63-0a98df600700.label: Matador
a96ac800-bfcb-412a-8a63-0a98df600700.lede: Isaac Brock built Modest Mouse out of Issaquah strip malls, a video-store friendship and a drummer found at a metal show. The band made the Northwest's most restless records, then picked up a Smith, a platinum hit and three decades of trouble.

1b4e059e-856e-49a8-b7ca-c3ee67dcde23.name: Morning Again
1b4e059e-856e-49a8-b7ca-c3ee67dcde23.label: Revelation
1b4e059e-856e-49a8-b7ca-c3ee67dcde23.lede: Morning Again went through two singers and a future New Found Glory guitarist in its first year, signed to Revelation, made one album and broke up four months after it came out. The vegan straight edge band from Cooper City, Florida kept coming back anyway.

4d4f5d92-0589-42fa-bc0e-1bd73e17a2ce.name: Mouse on Mars
4d4f5d92-0589-42fa-bc0e-1bd73e17a2ce.label: Thrill Jockey
4d4f5d92-0589-42fa-bc0e-1bd73e17a2ce.lede: Jan St. Werner and Andi Toma, friends from the Rhineland and by Wikipedia's account born the same day in the same hospital, have spent three decades making electronic records with live drummers, Mark E. Smith and a speech program they taught to sing.

ae888df0-2a19-4895-a654-e0093875d5b6.name: Nation of Ulysses
ae888df0-2a19-4895-a654-e0093875d5b6.label: Dischord
ae888df0-2a19-4895-a654-e0093875d5b6.lede: Five DC kids declared themselves a political party, not a band, and wrote a thirteen-point plan to destroy America. Ian Svenonius talked, the trumpet answered, and it lasted four years.

a8971728-0985-4b30-a209-142784e7c3b8.name: Necros
a8971728-0985-4b30-a209-142784e7c3b8.label: Touch and Go
a8971728-0985-4b30-a209-142784e7c3b8.lede: Skate-park kids from a Toledo suburb put out Touch and Go's first record, lent their drummer to the Misfits for the last show of the original lineup, and handed the label to the bassist who ran it for decades.

286e4fb9-4d6a-40de-ac50-01eff6a3c13e.name: Negative Approach
286e4fb9-4d6a-40de-ac50-01eff6a3c13e.label: Touch and Go
286e4fb9-4d6a-40de-ac50-01eff6a3c13e.lede: John Brannon fronted a Detroit teenage hardcore band that fit ten songs on one seven-inch and an album into 16 minutes 53 seconds, then split before the album came out. Twenty-three years later he was back, and still had no computer.

25b75a66-ce83-4db3-b136-395a3c3784c4.name: The New Pornographers
25b75a66-ce83-4db3-b136-395a3c3784c4.label: Matador
25b75a66-ce83-4db3-b136-395a3c3784c4.lede: It started in 1997 as a side project for a pop songwriter, a country singer, a cryptic poet and a filmmaker on keyboards. Ten albums later, through Matador, Concord and Merge, the New Pornographers are still going.

23d26104-95e2-473f-a704-ab0bcd702da3.name: No For An Answer
23d26104-95e2-473f-a704-ab0bcd702da3.label: Revelation
23d26104-95e2-473f-a704-ab0bcd702da3.lede: Orange County's straight edge band put out one six-song 7" on Revelation, lent its drum stool to a future Rage Against the Machine singer for a spell, and left Dan O'Mahony with a verdict he still delivers himself: the most musically feeble thing any of them did.

f57177fc-474e-4488-8b04-3ef43cfce8ed.name: Office of Future Plans
f57177fc-474e-4488-8b04-3ef43cfce8ed.label: Dischord
f57177fc-474e-4488-8b04-3ef43cfce8ed.lede: J. Robbins said yes to one opening slot in Baltimore, put a cello where the second guitar usually goes, and woke up seven years later with a band and a Dischord album he'd recorded in his own studio.

0b534406-23e2-48fe-a7ad-44d4d367a4be.name: One King Down
0b534406-23e2-48fe-a7ad-44d4d367a4be.label: Equal Vision
0b534406-23e2-48fe-a7ad-44d4d367a4be.lede: An Albany straight edge band went through three singers in five years, kept a bassist on the Equal Vision payroll, and made one six-song EP that fans still rate first. Along the way, a guitarist auditioned for the Foo Fighters.

94f18045-7fe2-41df-bf24-0bed21c88eb8.name: One Last Wish
94f18045-7fe2-41df-bf24-0bed21c88eb8.label: Dischord
94f18045-7fe2-41df-bf24-0bed21c88eb8.lede: One Last Wish played six shows in four months, cut twelve songs at Inner Ear, and then waited 13 years for a release, because Dischord didn't want to be the label of dead bands.

66ae7e89-680b-4f0f-a990-8a4e0bdf3d51.name: Orange 9mm
66ae7e89-680b-4f0f-a990-8a4e0bdf3d51.label: Revelation
66ae7e89-680b-4f0f-a990-8a4e0bdf3d51.lede: [[Chaka Malik]] brought a hatchet on stage with [[Burn]], guitarist [[Chris Traynor]] was in the crowd, and they set out to make hardcore that grooved like A Tribe Called Quest. Two major labels paid to find out whether it would sell.

f505c9ad-0298-46d5-ada6-c4e88b145ae2.name: Owls
f505c9ad-0298-46d5-ada6-c4e88b145ae2.label: Jade Tree
f505c9ad-0298-46d5-ada6-c4e88b145ae2.lede: Cap'n Jazz minus Davey von Bohlen makes one Steve Albini-recorded album for Jade Tree, tours it and quits, then comes back ten years later for a second one on Polyvinyl.

eeef9e6a-460b-49ca-840f-b55481b47297.name: Pan American
eeef9e6a-460b-49ca-840f-b55481b47297.label: Kranky
eeef9e6a-460b-49ca-840f-b55481b47297.lede: Mark Nelson played guitar in Labradford, the band Kranky was founded to release, and in 1997 started Pan American for the music that was too electronic for it. He's still at it, with records built around his son's heartbeat and his father's death.

36bfa85f-737b-41db-a8fc-b8825850ffc3.name: Pavement
36bfa85f-737b-41db-a8fc-b8825850ffc3.label: Matador
36bfa85f-737b-41db-a8fc-b8825850ffc3.lede: Stephen Malkmus and Scott Kannberg cut a first EP in a Stockton drummer's house, took mud and rocks at Lollapalooza, hung handcuffs on a mic stand at Brixton, and came back to find a 1999 B-side had become their biggest song.

2f360fd9-6440-4896-9f45-8156e8b0b204.name: Pedro the Lion
2f360fd9-6440-4896-9f45-8156e8b0b204.label: Jade Tree
2f360fd9-6440-4896-9f45-8156e8b0b204.lede: A pastor's son wrote Jade Tree's darkest records almost entirely by himself, split his Christian audience with a record about adultery and murder, shut the band down in 2006, and then revived it to tell the story of his own childhood.

5a797e16-f69a-4957-820f-1152ec19d236.name: Pelican
5a797e16-f69a-4957-820f-1152ec19d236.label: Hydra Head
5a797e16-f69a-4957-820f-1152ec19d236.lede: Four Chicagoans kept metal's riffs and left the singer out. Their songs ran so long that a 75-minute set held five of them, and the second guitar chair changed hands twice.

d1e1c4d7-cf24-4ea2-96e4-f74e3f4d97ef.name: Pitch Black
d1e1c4d7-cf24-4ea2-96e4-f74e3f4d97ef.label: Revelation
d1e1c4d7-cf24-4ea2-96e4-f74e3f4d97ef.lede: Pitch Black came out of Oakland with a keyboard player, a cowbell and two albums on Revelation, a label built on youth crew, and closed the second one with a song called Executives and Art Directors.

4e4b66fe-5b09-4faf-8362-1c7ffb411fd4.name: Primal Rite
4e4b66fe-5b09-4faf-8362-1c7ffb411fd4.label: Revelation
4e4b66fe-5b09-4faf-8362-1c7ffb411fd4.lede: Primal Rite came out of San Francisco in 2016 with a cassette and two 7"s, then signed to Revelation, which pressed a 7" in 2017 and the band's first LP in 2018.

eb191485-2b05-412b-84b6-78638ec6dcc2.name: Pupils
eb191485-2b05-412b-84b6-78638ec6dcc2.label: Dischord
eb191485-2b05-412b-84b6-78638ec6dcc2.lede: Daniel Higgs and Asa Osborne of Lungfish took away the bass and drums, recorded at home, and left one Dischord album behind, with songs called Mysterium, Lamb With Human Hands and Witness the Sidewalk Weeping Pools of Martian Brine.

a934e33f-b3cb-47dd-9638-f7f1f25fe162.name: Q and Not U
a934e33f-b3cb-47dd-9638-f7f1f25fe162.label: Dischord
a934e33f-b3cb-47dd-9638-f7f1f25fe162.lede: Q and Not U spent seven years trying to get D.C. punk crowds to dance, then quit while they were still climbing, leaving three albums on Dischord and one very colorful cover.

3c9f8bef-a658-4204-9ee8-7e95d2535b32.name: Quicksand
3c9f8bef-a658-4204-9ee8-7e95d2535b32.label: Revelation
3c9f8bef-a658-4204-9ee8-7e95d2535b32.lede: Walter Schreifels left the youth crew behind, tuned down, and cut a seven-inch for Revelation that got a major label's attention. Two Polydor-era albums and two breakups later, Quicksand are on their fifth record.

4e9323df-ca77-4e43-addf-bb520fb1b983.name: Rain
4e9323df-ca77-4e43-addf-bb520fb1b983.label: Dischord
4e9323df-ca77-4e43-addf-bb520fb1b983.lede: Rain lasted about a year, cut six songs with [[Ian MacKaye]] and broke up before any of them came out. [[Guy Picciotto]] put the record out three years later, on a label he ran himself.

899dea17-b403-42e0-9673-2623c40081af.name: Rapeman
899dea17-b403-42e0-9673-2623c40081af.label: Touch and Go
899dea17-b403-42e0-9673-2623c40081af.lede: Rapeman lasted two years and put out one EP and one album, and the name got Steve Albini's trio picketed in 1988 and, by his own 2020 account, indefensible.

b7b3172f-fcea-4881-818e-a250c6c19024.name: Ray & Porcell
b7b3172f-fcea-4881-818e-a250c6c19024.label: Revelation
b7b3172f-fcea-4881-818e-a250c6c19024.lede: Ray Cappo and John Porcelly made two songs with a drum machine that cost about $10, and Revelation pressed 5,000 copies. The window photo on the sleeve has outlasted both songs.

103f165a-a56b-4313-84b8-9a99e1d67305.name: Reptile House
103f165a-a56b-4313-84b8-9a99e1d67305.label: Dischord
103f165a-a56b-4313-84b8-9a99e1d67305.lede: Reptile House was Baltimore's answer to D.C.: a singer who'd turn into Daniel Higgs, a drummer who'd land in Samhain, and a debut 7" that sat out of print for a quarter century.

23712215-fb3c-4abb-bd49-9593e9c9046d.name: Right Brigade
23712215-fb3c-4abb-bd49-9593e9c9046d.label: Revelation
23712215-fb3c-4abb-bd49-9593e9c9046d.lede: Boston straight edge kids from Fastbreak and Follow Through played SSD-style hardcore, sold over a thousand demos locally, and ended up on Revelation with a bio calling them the biggest band in hardcore.

b2ff1a6d-9198-4646-b068-8965242d245b.name: Rites of Spring
b2ff1a6d-9198-4646-b068-8965242d245b.label: Dischord
b2ff1a6d-9198-4646-b068-8965242d245b.lede: Rites of Spring played about fifteen shows, cut one album and left a four-song single in the can. Forty years on, the band still gets credited with a genre name it never used.

593f8594-83ad-4df4-a9b8-e4d225f55440.name: Saves the Day
593f8594-83ad-4df4-a9b8-e4d225f55440.label: Equal Vision
593f8594-83ad-4df4-a9b8-e4d225f55440.lede: A New Jersey high school band wrote the blueprint for a decade of emo and pop-punk, partly in an NYU psychology class. They survived a van wreck and a major label that dropped them days after their album came out, and Chris Conley outlasted more than a dozen bandmates.

75687111-1585-4df2-83e6-ce52e7fa2bb0.name: Scratch Acid
75687111-1585-4df2-83e6-ce52e7fa2bb0.label: Touch and Go
75687111-1585-4df2-83e6-ce52e7fa2bb0.lede: Scratch Acid lasted five years and well over a hundred shows, long enough for [[David Yow]] to play Jesus on a cross and charge a crowd with cookie dough pulled from his pants, before the band split into [[The Jesus Lizard]] and [[Rapeman]].

b9f52132-28af-4cea-9558-165cd125f9b7.name: Scream
b9f52132-28af-4cea-9558-165cd125f9b7.label: Dischord
b9f52132-28af-4cea-9558-165cd125f9b7.lede: Two brothers from the Virginia suburbs made Dischord's first full-length by a single band, toured Europe before most American hardcore bands dared, and handed a 17-year-old named Dave Grohl his first real gig.

8d7bf045-1526-404d-b37c-6f49b714d614.name: Sense Field
8d7bf045-1526-404d-b37c-6f49b714d614.label: Revelation
8d7bf045-1526-404d-b37c-6f49b714d614.lede: A Harbor City hardcore band became one of the first emo bands on Revelation, sat out five years at Warner Bros., and still ended up playing Save Yourself for Jay Leno.

a90071a3-279e-4596-8727-e3f4200f17d3.name: Sensor Ghost
a90071a3-279e-4596-8727-e3f4200f17d3.label: Dischord
a90071a3-279e-4596-8727-e3f4200f17d3.lede: Three D.C. lifers from Puff Pieces, Antelope and Weed Tree started a no-wave trio, then drove to Inner Ear twice with Ian MacKaye and Don Zientara. The second trip became Dischord No. 198, pressed on translucent yellow vinyl.

4e4b4490-1c10-4e0c-b794-afa4688f88a6.name: Severin
4e4b4490-1c10-4e0c-b794-afa4688f88a6.label: Dischord
4e4b4490-1c10-4e0c-b794-afa4688f88a6.lede: Alec Bourgeois and Eugene Bogan came home from college, got Gray Matter's Mark Haggerty and Swiz's Alex Daniels, and in four years made one album and a run of singles for Superbad and Dischord. Dischord calls the sound melodic and chaotic.

3f6c4af4-bb50-4672-998e-5e806b696fb3.name: Shades Apart
3f6c4af4-bb50-4672-998e-5e806b696fb3.label: Revelation
3f6c4af4-bb50-4672-998e-5e806b696fb3.lede: A summer project from Bridgewater, New Jersey made its first record for $720, shot a Soft Cell cover for MTV in the bassist's backyard, and heard its major-label single on a Florida station right before Ricky Martin.

2aaa7913-72ae-469b-9fdb-4c79cd70ed2e.name: Shai Hulud
2aaa7913-72ae-469b-9fdb-4c79cd70ed2e.label: Revelation
2aaa7913-72ae-469b-9fdb-4c79cd70ed2e.lede: A band named for the sandworms of Dune found its first big singer in a fourteen-year-old, lost singers about as fast as it found them, and once tried to change its name rather than keep auditioning.

604f273a-d3c1-4b5b-ab83-99541f9368ea.name: Shellac
604f273a-d3c1-4b5b-ab83-99541f9368ea.label: Touch and Go
604f273a-d3c1-4b5b-ab83-99541f9368ea.lede: [[Steve Albini]], the most famous recording engineer in rock, kept the same trio for 32 years, took questions from the crowd mid-set, gave an album to 779 named friends, and saw the last Shellac record come out ten days after he died.

d5157104-76b1-4b8b-90c2-9ff994f940db.name: Shelter
d5157104-76b1-4b8b-90c2-9ff994f940db.label: Revelation
d5157104-76b1-4b8b-90c2-9ff994f940db.lede: Ray Cappo shaved his head, took vows and left Youth of Today a Krishna devotee, then took a busload of monks on tour with a hardcore band. For a few years in the '90s the pit was full of tulasi beads.

de5db393-7bcd-4ddc-98c7-1e9a48366f3f.name: Shook Ones
de5db393-7bcd-4ddc-98c7-1e9a48366f3f.label: Revelation
de5db393-7bcd-4ddc-98c7-1e9a48366f3f.lede: Shook Ones sold their first Revelation covers at a basement show in Ballard, came home from four weeks in Europe to lost jobs and a dead phone, and walked away from the label in 2007. A decade on, they went back to Revelation with a record every member wrote.

5a6e19e0-3ff0-4b3d-869e-3c539d6d8707.name: Shudder to Think
5a6e19e0-3ff0-4b3d-869e-3c539d6d8707.label: Dischord
5a6e19e0-3ff0-4b3d-869e-3c539d6d8707.lede: Shudder to Think ran a glam falsetto through Dischord's straight-edge corridors, took a Buzz Clip to Sony, scored films for a decade, and came back to Dischord twenty-seven years later with a new single.

e204ed91-3684-4561-b29b-d0b53f8459a7.name: Sick of It All
e204ed91-3684-4561-b29b-d0b53f8459a7.label: Revelation
e204ed91-3684-4561-b29b-d0b53f8459a7.lede: [[Lou Koller]] and [[Pete Koller]] started the band in their parents' Queens basement, and Revelation is still pressing that first seven-inch in new colors. They carried New York hardcore from the CBGB matinees to MTV to festival fields, and in the band's 40th year Lou died.

8dc812b1-d387-4c45-8173-f0d5bd0c318f.name: Side By Side
8dc812b1-d387-4c45-8173-f0d5bd0c318f.label: Revelation
8dc812b1-d387-4c45-8173-f0d5bd0c318f.lede: Side By Side lasted about a year and a half and split before their only record came out. That seven-song 7" has been repressed for nearly four decades.

64c9ed9d-0b97-4e01-946c-2ef5f342e236.name: Silkworm
64c9ed9d-0b97-4e01-946c-2ef5f342e236.label: Touch and Go
64c9ed9d-0b97-4e01-946c-2ef5f342e236.lede: Three friends from Missoula and a drummer from Seattle made records for twenty years that critics loved and crowds mostly missed. A driver at a Skokie red light ended it in 2005.

d89de379-665d-425c-b2e9-41b95d1edb36.name: Silverstein
d89de379-665d-425c-b2e9-41b95d1edb36.label: Victory
d89de379-665d-425c-b2e9-41b95d1edb36.lede: Shane Told formed Silverstein in Burlington, Ontario in 2000 as a side project, learned to scream because his guitarist asked, and then watched four Victory records get sung back to the band word for word.

5159b146-3475-44f1-bbb5-2c52dceef2cf.name: Since By Man
5159b146-3475-44f1-bbb5-2c52dceef2cf.label: Revelation
5159b146-3475-44f1-bbb5-2c52dceef2cf.lede: Since By Man put dance beats under breakdowns, took the Milwaukee hardcore scene to Revelation Records, and broke up on MySpace when the third album wouldn't come.

1ac2e44d-7ba5-4917-8345-f4becc40c0fe.name: Sinking Ships
1ac2e44d-7ba5-4917-8345-f4becc40c0fe.label: Revelation
1ac2e44d-7ba5-4917-8345-f4becc40c0fe.lede: Sinking Ships hid ten copies of their first 7" around Seattle, made one album for Revelation, and called it quits within five years.

84c597b8-2855-423d-bcff-6a8a97eca89c.name: Skewbald
84c597b8-2855-423d-bcff-6a8a97eca89c.label: Dischord
84c597b8-2855-423d-bcff-6a8a97eca89c.lede: Minor Threat lost its guitarist to college, so Ian MacKaye and Jeff Nelson wrote songs in the Dischord House basement with two friends, recorded them once, and never played a show. The tape got traded for ten years, sometimes as lost Minor Threat.

ffe8acdb-3fa3-4f7e-8939-c3862138502d.name: Slant 6
ffe8acdb-3fa3-4f7e-8939-c3862138502d.label: Dischord
ffe8acdb-3fa3-4f7e-8939-c3862138502d.lede: Christina Billotte left Autoclave for something faster, took a 1963 Silvertone and a drummer who learned the instrument to join, and made two albums in three years. The New York Times later called one of them arguably the best album of the riot grrrl era.

e36e78eb-3ace-4acd-882c-16789e700ab7.name: Sleater-Kinney
e36e78eb-3ace-4acd-882c-16789e700ab7.label: Kill Rock Stars
e36e78eb-3ace-4acd-882c-16789e700ab7.lede: Two guitarists from Olympia named their band after a freeway exit, skipped the bass, and sang their own breakup on record. A breakdown before a Brussels show stopped them in 2006; eight years later they announced a record they had already made.

2869c510-2679-4a3f-bf15-e5e8b49f2f28.name: Slint
2869c510-2679-4a3f-bf15-e5e8b49f2f28.label: Touch and Go
2869c510-2679-4a3f-bf15-e5e8b49f2f28.lede: Slint took its name from a pet fish, split up months before its second album came out, and never toured it. Spiderland has sold year after year since, to people who swear it changed how a rock band can sound.

d9c78028-a30b-470b-b964-2f85cab51cc2.name: Smart Went Crazy
d9c78028-a30b-470b-b964-2f85cab51cc2.label: Dischord
d9c78028-a30b-470b-b964-2f85cab51cc2.lede: Smart Went Crazy, five DC players with an electric cello, made a 73-minute second album for Dischord, covered Laurie Anderson on it, and split within a year. Chad Clark says he was relieved.

7df26b91-56ae-456f-96ae-6be57a1c99c3.name: Snakes
7df26b91-56ae-456f-96ae-6be57a1c99c3.label: Dischord
7df26b91-56ae-456f-96ae-6be57a1c99c3.lede: Two Georgetown kids from SOA made a goofy pop record so far from hardcore that Dischord put it out under a fake label name, then came back for a second one five years later.

90f7f8df-db45-4a6c-89fb-9e912f77eabd.name: Snapcase
90f7f8df-db45-4a6c-89fb-9e912f77eabd.label: Victory Records
90f7f8df-db45-4a6c-89fb-9e912f77eabd.lede: A West Seneca basement band cut its first single with Goo Goo Doll Robby Takac, made a 1997 record Turnstile and Drug Church still name, and quit in 2005 when it got tough to keep flogging a dead horse.

e54cb250-3502-4c32-9482-70488bd9a8cb.name: SOA
e54cb250-3502-4c32-9482-70488bd9a8cb.label: Dischord
e54cb250-3502-4c32-9482-70488bd9a8cb.lede: Henry Garfield paid for Dischord's second record out of his wages as a Georgetown ice cream manager, and the band was finished before its first birthday.

16cf8c3c-93a7-40a4-be20-460491346d49.name: Soccer Team
16cf8c3c-93a7-40a4-be20-460491346d49.label: Dischord
16cf8c3c-93a7-40a4-be20-460491346d49.lede: Two Dischord co-workers started writing songs in a basement in Southeast D.C. Nine years, a stretch in Flint and a husband on drums later, they had two albums on the label where they'd met.

5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9.name: Sonic Youth
5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9.label: DGC
5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9.lede: Sonic Youth spent thirty years retuning guitars, jamming screwdrivers under the strings and getting an art-school crowd onto major-label radio. It ran from a downtown gallery noise festival to the Lollapalooza headline slot, and it ended when the marriage at its center did.

df59ffcc-e1d3-4752-b4c7-b77c749b65ce.name: Soul Search
df59ffcc-e1d3-4752-b4c7-b77c749b65ce.label: Revelation
df59ffcc-e1d3-4752-b4c7-b77c749b65ce.lede: Soul Search put out a cassette, then 7"s on Thick Skin, Triple-B, Back To Back and Closed Casket Activities. In 2014 Revelation pressed one of them again as Rev155.

de2e8176-32c2-4abe-b718-9392dffd8ffe.name: Soulside
de2e8176-32c2-4abe-b718-9392dffd8ffe.label: Dischord
de2e8176-32c2-4abe-b718-9392dffd8ffe.lede: They began as Lunchmeat on a split single with Dave Grohl's first band, played an illegal East Berlin show in 1989 with no guitars in the room, and split before their best record came out. Twenty-five years later they were back.

843e9ff5-c56d-4262-97d1-ae4f82d7e635.name: Speak 714
843e9ff5-c56d-4262-97d1-ae4f82d7e635.label: Revelation
843e9ff5-c56d-4262-97d1-ae4f82d7e635.lede: Joe Foster turned up with five songs already recorded, Dan O'Mahony sang them with his jaw wired shut, and Revelation had the record out inside the year. Speak 714 lasted about as long as the paperwork.

84eac621-1c5a-49a1-9500-555099c6e184.name: Spoon
84eac621-1c5a-49a1-9500-555099c6e184.label: Matador
84eac621-1c5a-49a1-9500-555099c6e184.lede: Britt Daniel and Jim Eno made a $3,000 debut for Matador, got signed and dropped by Elektra inside a year, and wrote a single about the executive who did it. A decade of steady records on Merge later, Metacritic named Spoon its top artist of the 2000s.

a1154343-1ea1-4007-97d3-2382482a90cd.name: Stars of the Lid
a1154343-1ea1-4007-97d3-2382482a90cd.label: Kranky
a1154343-1ea1-4007-97d3-2382482a90cd.lede: Adam Wiltzie and Brian McBride started a band in Austin on Christmas Day 1992 and spent thirty years trading tapes and making music slow enough that it barely admits to moving. Along the way they named a song after Fulham's football ground.

cbc9199f-944b-42e9-a945-627c9fc0ba6e.name: Streetlight Manifesto
cbc9199f-944b-42e9-a945-627c9fc0ba6e.label: Victory
cbc9199f-944b-42e9-a945-627c9fc0ba6e.lede: Tomas Kalnoky quit Catch 22 after one album, then spent fifteen years re-recording it, touring in a van that kept getting robbed, and fighting Victory Records until he bought his masters back.

5e911223-4228-4a14-8f6c-7d2dfeb62530.name: Strife
5e911223-4228-4a14-8f6c-7d2dfeb62530.label: Victory Records
5e911223-4228-4a14-8f6c-7d2dfeb62530.lede: Strife started in Thousand Oaks as a straight edge band, got Chino Moreno, Dino Cazares and Igor Cavalera onto its second album, split two years later, and came back in 2001 no longer edge.

ac82cb46-f2b2-4f99-9cfa-d0c322a4ba16.name: Strike Anywhere
ac82cb46-f2b2-4f99-9cfa-d0c322a4ba16.label: Jade Tree
ac82cb46-f2b2-4f99-9cfa-d0c322a4ba16.lede: Strike Anywhere borrowed its name from a song by singer Thomas Barnett's old band and spent two decades turning Richmond's buried history into tuneful, angry hardcore. A stolen notebook and a Weimar-era antifascist logo got into the story along the way.

9b98f3ed-d24a-479e-bd15-97c16de9f13f.name: SUMAC
9b98f3ed-d24a-479e-bd15-97c16de9f13f.label: Thrill Jockey
9b98f3ed-d24a-479e-bd15-97c16de9f13f.lede: Aaron Turner wanted the heaviest music of his life, got a drummer by way of Kurt Ballou, and spent the next decade pulling his own riffs apart to make room for improvisation.

61653550-fd9b-4401-8248-44f2d064d384.name: Superchunk
61653550-fd9b-4401-8248-44f2d064d384.label: Matador
61653550-fd9b-4401-8248-44f2d064d384.lede: Mac McCaughan and Laura Ballance started a band and a record label in the same Chapel Hill summer, and kept both going for more than 35 years. The band's first single was about a Kinko's co-worker; its thirteenth album came out in 2025.

ae7c0f49-c885-4b94-9424-fe4d890a5d6a.name: Supertouch
ae7c0f49-c885-4b94-9424-fe4d890a5d6a.label: Revelation
ae7c0f49-c885-4b94-9424-fe4d890a5d6a.lede: Supertouch put funk, quiet parts and major chords into late-'80s New York hardcore, fronted by a b-boy singer and named after a Bad Brains song. The scene mostly wanted mosh parts, and the band never got the credit.

350bce49-c21b-4137-b50a-0766ded07e4d.name: Taking Back Sunday
350bce49-c21b-4137-b50a-0766ded07e4d.label: Victory
350bce49-c21b-4137-b50a-0766ded07e4d.lede: Taking Back Sunday cut its debut in two weeks for $10,000 and watched it go platinum 21 years later. In between, two members quit, Warner Bros. took the band to No. 2, and the Tell All Your Friends line-up played together again in 2010.

e6f8912b-7df9-4aae-b551-2cd03dc29588.name: Teenage Fanclub
e6f8912b-7df9-4aae-b551-2cd03dc29588.label: Creation
e6f8912b-7df9-4aae-b551-2cd03dc29588.lede: Three songwriters from Glasgow sold a neighbour's fridge to make a debut, then a moneybag sleeve beat Nirvana in Spin and drew a letter from Gene Simmons.

c051f242-5907-42ce-b25f-678f14323dac.name: Ten Yard Fight
c051f242-5907-42ce-b25f-678f14323dac.label: Equal Vision
c051f242-5907-42ce-b25f-678f14323dac.lede: Anthony Moreschi played Ten Yard Fight's first show in football gear, the band fired a guitarist for wanting to stop singing about football, and its last show, on a Boston Sunday with the playoffs next door at Fenway, turned into straight edge's own holiday.

697eba1a-bf52-46b1-a19f-4d7190b63e5c.name: Terror
697eba1a-bf52-46b1-a19f-4d7190b63e5c.label: Victory Records
697eba1a-bf52-46b1-a19f-4d7190b63e5c.lede: Scott Vogel quit music, moved from Buffalo to Los Angeles, and took a call from the members of Carry On who had regrouped. By the band's own count, Terror has played more than 3,000 shows since.

b93c736f-a82f-4cae-9e57-a60b12d7055f.name: Texas Is the Reason
b93c736f-a82f-4cae-9e57-a60b12d7055f.label: Revelation
b93c736f-a82f-4cae-9e57-a60b12d7055f.lede: Texas Is the Reason made one album, nine songs for Revelation, then broke up in Germany on the eve of a Capitol deal. The record became the label's best seller, and the band keeps coming back on anniversaries.

3a3b3e5d-2d28-4108-875e-30686d2710e8.name: The Evens
3a3b3e5d-2d28-4108-875e-30686d2710e8.label: Dischord
3a3b3e5d-2d28-4108-875e-30686d2710e8.lede: [[Ian MacKaye]] turned the volume down, sat behind a baritone guitar across from [[Amy Farina]]'s drums, and found that two people in a barn, a museum or a theater lobby could hit harder than most bands with a wall of amps.

9cba6b36-ed3a-44d5-85d8-bc4181905f41.name: The Explosion
9cba6b36-ed3a-44d5-85d8-bc4181905f41.label: Revelation
9cba6b36-ed3a-44d5-85d8-bc4181905f41.lede: The Explosion sold 250 demo tapes on a Kid Dynamite tour, landed on Spin's top 20 of 2000, and settled a legal threat with an EP. Then Virgin dropped them, and the album they'd finished for it waited five years.

f735a867-9a16-451f-8f83-669ed42e2574.name: Faith
f735a867-9a16-451f-8f83-669ed42e2574.label: Dischord
f735a867-9a16-451f-8f83-669ed42e2574.lede: Faith lasted about two years and left one side of a split LP and an eight-song EP, and a lot of D.C. kids felt closer to them than to Minor Threat.

d5da1841-9bc8-4813-9f89-11098090148e.name: The Fall
d5da1841-9bc8-4813-9f89-11098090148e.label: Matador
d5da1841-9bc8-4813-9f89-11098090148e.lede: One man from Prestwich ran The Fall for 42 years, through 31 studio albums, 24 Peel sessions and roughly 60 musicians hired and fired, and stayed until the end.

a7997562-8edf-428f-8c98-f25d8e07c70e.name: The Judas Factor
a7997562-8edf-428f-8c98-f25d8e07c70e.label: Revelation
a7997562-8edf-428f-8c98-f25d8e07c70e.lede: Rob Fish put The Judas Factor together right after Ressurection, fired his old guitarist inside three shows, and made two Revelation records that stop being hardcore halfway through. One early member now sits in New York City government.

26cad87d-5be0-467f-955f-b3ccecce007a.name: Make-Up
26cad87d-5be0-467f-955f-b3ccecce007a.label: Dischord
26cad87d-5be0-467f-955f-b3ccecce007a.lede: Nation of Ulysses called itself a political party. Its successor ran like a church: matching suits, a congregation instead of an audience, and a five-year plan to quit once everybody started copying them.

62788614-b33c-42c9-9b6e-c9375362b57e.name: The Messthetics
62788614-b33c-42c9-9b6e-c9375362b57e.label: Dischord
62788614-b33c-42c9-9b6e-c9375362b57e.lede: Fugazi's rhythm section found a jazz guitarist from D.C., played one show with him for [[Ian MacKaye]] and walked out with a Dischord deal. Eight years later they were on the label that put out A Love Supreme.

0a91cea1-52f2-4212-aa2f-7baf3627d71f.name: The Movielife
0a91cea1-52f2-4212-aa2f-7baf3627d71f.label: Revelation
0a91cea1-52f2-4212-aa2f-7baf3627d71f.lede: Vinnie Caruana fronted a Long Island band that swapped members with the groups that became Taking Back Sunday, Bayside and Brand New. The Movielife made one record for Revelation that keeps getting repressed, wrecked two vans, and ended in 2003 with a note on its website.

bb9faf52-7ba4-4857-ad58-b83bdd7bce33.name: The Nerve Agents
bb9faf52-7ba4-4857-ad58-b83bdd7bce33.label: Revelation
bb9faf52-7ba4-4857-ad58-b83bdd7bce33.lede: Eric Ozenne named a band after the chemical weapons he'd trained against in the Marines, put eyeliner on Bay Area hardcore, and quit at the top. His daughter Grace was born two weeks later.

63a6fae8-d39e-4de6-bfd4-9bcbf489a565.name: The Promise Ring
63a6fae8-d39e-4de6-bfd4-9bcbf489a565.label: Jade Tree
63a6fae8-d39e-4de6-bfd4-9bcbf489a565.lede: The Promise Ring grew out of two dead Milwaukee bands and a loaned Cap'n Jazz guitarist, then turned emo into power pop and nearly died doing it: a van through a Nebraska snowstorm, a brain tumor found the day a tour was due to leave, and a last album made to get away from the word.

06f73938-04f9-4b08-adc3-2978bb957de9.name: The Rival Mob
06f73938-04f9-4b08-adc3-2978bb957de9.label: Revelation
06f73938-04f9-4b08-adc3-2978bb957de9.lede: Brendan Radigan, drummer of the powerviolence band [[Mind Eraser]], picked up a microphone in 2007 and fronted a Boston band that played late-'80s hardcore like nobody had told them it was over.

74171cb6-1ff8-42bd-be8a-96660c22e3e0.name: The Sea and Cake
74171cb6-1ff8-42bd-be8a-96660c22e3e0.label: Thrill Jockey
74171cb6-1ff8-42bd-be8a-96660c22e3e0.lede: A painter, a cartoonist, a photographer and Chicago's busiest drummer take their name from a Gastr del Sol song title they bent on purpose, then make the lightest-sounding records of the post-rock years.

84e8d8bf-da21-4488-89e5-50a4c12ff4fa.name: The Teen Idles
84e8d8bf-da21-4488-89e5-50a4c12ff4fa.label: Dischord
84e8d8bf-da21-4488-89e5-50a4c12ff4fa.lede: Four Wilson High kids took a Greyhound to California, came home with an X for the back of the hand, and put their $600 into a thousand hand-glued sleeves that became Dischord No. 1.

af0dea4e-c501-47f2-8695-129f254d425f.name: Warmers
af0dea4e-c501-47f2-8695-129f254d425f.label: Dischord
af0dea4e-c501-47f2-8695-129f254d425f.lede: The kid slumped on the cover of the first Minor Threat EP grew up, took up guitar, and built a trio that treated silence as a member of the band.

e95a296e-a34c-4496-9a7c-a95683d487b5.name: These Arms Are Snakes
e95a296e-a34c-4496-9a7c-a95683d487b5.label: Jade Tree
e95a296e-a34c-4496-9a7c-a95683d487b5.lede: [[Botch]] ended in 2002, and its bassist, [[Brian Cook]], started a Seattle band with a name its members thought sounded ridiculous. Four drummers, a van that met a semi-truck and a winter on tour with Underoath later, it ended when the gear gave out at the last show.

9a47ec35-e682-4350-800e-d26981a86d10.name: Thirty-Two Frames
9a47ec35-e682-4350-800e-d26981a86d10.label: Revelation
9a47ec35-e682-4350-800e-d26981a86d10.lede: Jay Palumbo quit Elliott after False Cathedrals and started a Kentucky hardcore band, then handed the tapes to Elliott's drummer to engineer. The result was one EP, out on two labels in 2002.

0acae232-d31a-4211-b6d0-6af1b6350274.name: Thursday
0acae232-d31a-4211-b6d0-6af1b6350274.label: Victory
