0acae232-d31a-4211-b6d0-6af1b6350274.lede: A New Brunswick basement band cut Full Collapse in 20 days, fell out with Victory Records over it, and cost its next label $1.2 million to get free. Then Thursday broke up, spent five years apart while Geoff Rickly fought heroin, and came back.

c7ee3bc9-780c-42c0-91e9-4cd70ad692d3.name: Tim Hecker
c7ee3bc9-780c-42c0-91e9-4cd70ad692d3.label: Kranky
c7ee3bc9-780c-42c0-91e9-4cd70ad692d3.lede: Tim Hecker was a policy analyst for the Canadian government before he left to study noise at McGill. He has put pipe organs through distortion, a falling piano on a record cover, and spent twenty years arguing that ambient music shouldn't be background.

1154d345-8061-4d04-a52a-6214288523ac.name: Title Fight
1154d345-8061-4d04-a52a-6214288523ac.label: Revelation
1154d345-8061-4d04-a52a-6214288523ac.lede: Two twelve-year-old twins and their friend took a name off a cable TV guide, built a stage in an abandoned pizza shop, and ended up pointing hardcore kids toward Dinosaur Jr. and shoegaze.

79e910c5-c331-43ed-af3b-ae15ac9a147f.name: Title Tracks
79e910c5-c331-43ed-af3b-ae15ac9a147f.label: Dischord
79e910c5-c331-43ed-af3b-ae15ac9a147f.lede: John Davis spent seven years drumming in Q and Not U, then picked up a guitar, took the vocals and wrote record-collector power pop, some of it mixed in mono.

e0953daa-860f-4dc8-9f1a-b12587cdaf17.name: Tortoise
e0953daa-860f-4dc8-9f1a-b12587cdaf17.label: Thrill Jockey
e0953daa-860f-4dc8-9f1a-b12587cdaf17.lede: Tortoise runs two bassists, three drummers who also play vibraphone and marimba, and no singer. Chicago gave the band a genre name it never wanted, and thirty years of records have kept outrunning it.

7c5acaaa-3f74-4e16-82b2-f8046fce4338.name: Trans Am
7c5acaaa-3f74-4e16-82b2-f8046fce4338.label: Thrill Jockey
7c5acaaa-3f74-4e16-82b2-f8046fce4338.lede: Three friends from suburban Maryland fired their singer, plugged in a Casio and named the band after a Pontiac. Thirty years on, they're still poking post-rock with vocoders and Van Halen.

b4ae94e2-0d98-4b9e-8f24-30d1050d4531.name: Trial
b4ae94e2-0d98-4b9e-8f24-30d1050d4531.label: Equal Vision
b4ae94e2-0d98-4b9e-8f24-30d1050d4531.lede: Greg Bennick juggled for a living and sang in a Seattle straight edge band that made one album, broke up the next year, then played more shows dead than alive.

9ee8b35d-9305-4aa3-9565-cf2a658a2da0.name: Trusty
9ee8b35d-9305-4aa3-9565-cf2a658a2da0.label: Dischord
9ee8b35d-9305-4aa3-9565-cf2a658a2da0.lede: Trusty were a pop-punk band from Little Rock who loved Washington's scene enough to move there in 1992. Two Dischord albums later, one of them closing on a song named for the Orange Line, they packed up and went back south.

de38fbd3-7155-497a-bf3c-1a8db3091859.name: Underdog
de38fbd3-7155-497a-bf3c-1a8db3091859.label: Revelation
de38fbd3-7155-497a-bf3c-1a8db3091859.lede: Two skaters met at CBGB and built a hardcore band that could sing. They handed a guitar to the first Black skater on a Thrasher cover, made one album, and split the minute the van got home.

16d88df0-a2a9-4b3b-87ff-84e90e312d40.name: Untouchables
16d88df0-a2a9-4b3b-87ff-84e90e312d40.label: Dischord
16d88df0-a2a9-4b3b-87ff-84e90e312d40.lede: Ian MacKaye's kid brother sang, a drummer who'd never played drums took over mid-band, and the singer kept passing out. Sonic Youth covered their best song eleven years after they quit.

120e728a-4078-47b7-a31c-d581ade28bde.name: Urge Overkill
120e728a-4078-47b7-a31c-d581ade28bde.label: Touch and Go
120e728a-4078-47b7-a31c-d581ade28bde.lede: Nash Kato and Eddie "King" Roeser met at Northwestern, took to lounge suits and medallions, found a drummer called Blackie Onassis, and cut a Neil Diamond cover on a whim that Quentin Tarantino used for Uma Thurman's dance in Pulp Fiction.

d9d0b8bb-37f0-44d1-8f6b-89f83a7f6e1d.name: Violent Reaction
d9d0b8bb-37f0-44d1-8f6b-89f83a7f6e1d.label: Revelation
d9d0b8bb-37f0-44d1-8f6b-89f83a7f6e1d.lede: Tom Pimlott was the only straight edge kid he knew in Liverpool, so he recorded Violent Reaction alone, moved to Leeds for a band, and ended up the first group from outside America that Revelation signed.

960a1d2f-2b5f-4fcf-bf11-4957529a6508.name: Void
960a1d2f-2b5f-4fcf-bf11-4957529a6508.label: Dischord
960a1d2f-2b5f-4fcf-bf11-4957529a6508.lede: Four Columbia, Maryland teenagers started a band in 1980, played each part as fast as they could, and ended up on one side of a split LP with Faith that people are still arguing about. The album they made after it never came out.

496da466-68e9-4cbb-9e86-cbb57eda861a.name: Warzone
496da466-68e9-4cbb-9e86-cbb57eda861a.label: Revelation
496da466-68e9-4cbb-9e86-cbb57eda861a.lede: Raybeez, a drummer Agnostic Front had let go, took over the mic of his side band, kept a Lower East Side crew around him and handed Revelation Records its catalog number one.

6b342fb3-6c3d-4ade-9030-1cc919e0451e.name: Where Fear and Weapons Meet
6b342fb3-6c3d-4ade-9030-1cc919e0451e.label: Revelation
6b342fb3-6c3d-4ade-9030-1cc919e0451e.lede: Two Morning Again alumni and a Poison the Well bassist cut fifteen songs in about twenty-one minutes for Revelation, then spent the next five years changing singers.

98619afb-e691-48e4-bf65-824e053cd689.name: Whirlpool
98619afb-e691-48e4-bf65-824e053cd689.label: Revelation
98619afb-e691-48e4-bf65-824e053cd689.lede: Two guys who worked at Revelation wanted a Pixies-style band with a man and a woman singing, made two records, and then lost their drummer and a guitarist to Sense Field's Warner Bros. deal.

915d3d51-8a51-4864-a1f4-016bae819c7f.name: Will Haven
915d3d51-8a51-4864-a1f4-016bae819c7f.label: Revelation
915d3d51-8a51-4864-a1f4-016bae819c7f.lede: Four Sacramento friends set out to sound like Neurosis and ended up on the road with the Deftones. They broke up after one last night at the Capitol Garage, and have kept coming back since 2005.

1bf10bf6-f9cf-460a-afd1-81a9b1b0128d.name: Windy & Carl
1bf10bf6-f9cf-460a-afd1-81a9b1b0128d.label: Kranky
1bf10bf6-f9cf-460a-afd1-81a9b1b0128d.lede: Windy Weber and Carl Hultgren have made slow guitar and bass drones in Dearborn since 1993, with no drummer, a mountain of delay and a record shop that kept the lights on.

87061322-24d2-4ba9-8f25-455a44d0e354.name: World Be Free
87061322-24d2-4ba9-8f25-455a44d0e354.label: Revelation
87061322-24d2-4ba9-8f25-455a44d0e354.lede: Four veterans of Terror, Strife, Judge and Gorilla Biscuits named a band after a basketball player who renamed himself World, then used it to play the melodic, positive hardcore they grew up on.

3f542031-b054-454d-b57b-812fa2a81b11.name: Yo La Tengo
3f542031-b054-454d-b57b-812fa2a81b11.label: Matador
3f542031-b054-454d-b57b-812fa2a81b11.lede: Ira Kaplan and Georgia Hubley went through roughly fifteen bass players before James McNew stayed. Three decades on, the band still makes records that whisper, roar, and play eight nights of Hanukkah.

7029a4cb-83bc-4e5e-8d94-af9caefc453c.name: Youth Brigade
7029a4cb-83bc-4e5e-8d94-af9caefc453c.label: Dischord
7029a4cb-83bc-4e5e-8d94-af9caefc453c.lede: Nathan Strejcek and Danny Ingram, two Wilson High friends from bands that had just ended, start Youth Brigade in late 1980 and are finished by December 1981. They leave eleven songs on Dischord, and D.C. has to wait thirty years for more.

9ca27db4-f127-4aeb-ae87-29e21f558c13.name: Youth of Today
9ca27db4-f127-4aeb-ae87-29e21f558c13.label: Revelation
9ca27db4-f127-4aeb-ae87-29e21f558c13.lede: Ray Cappo and John Porcelly left a Danbury hardcore band, picked the plainest name available, and aimed it at New York. Put an X on it, skip the beer, skip the burger, mean every word: a whole scene copied the dress code.

9941a936-196a-4a62-ae53-a69cbc33f20e.name: Black Flag
9941a936-196a-4a62-ae53-a69cbc33f20e.label: SST
9941a936-196a-4a62-ae53-a69cbc33f20e.lede: Greg Ginn started SST to put out his own band, Raymond Pettibon gave the band four black bars, and five singers came through in seven years. Ginn kept the name through all of it.

d4ad0149-d8ae-4105-8009-0221fce9ff35.name: Minutemen
d4ad0149-d8ae-4105-8009-0221fce9ff35.label: SST
d4ad0149-d8ae-4105-8009-0221fce9ff35.lede: Three friends from San Pedro wrote songs that ended before a DJ could find the volume knob, then fit 45 of them on one record. A year and a half later a van axle broke on Interstate 10 and the band was over.

33e09dd8-a998-4e1a-9e69-1a6567a3803d.name: fIREHOSE
33e09dd8-a998-4e1a-9e69-1a6567a3803d.label: SST
33e09dd8-a998-4e1a-9e69-1a6567a3803d.lede: Mike Watt and George Hurley lost D. Boon in December 1985 and weren't planning a sequel. Then a 21-year-old from Ohio kept phoning, and by the end the three had played about 980 gigs.

5c4c90a4-539f-4101-83cf-301bc6a94e06.name: Hüsker Dü
5c4c90a4-539f-4101-83cf-301bc6a94e06.label: SST
5c4c90a4-539f-4101-83cf-301bc6a94e06.lede: Bob Mould, Grant Hart and Greg Norton started in St. Paul in 1979, outran every band in the Midwest, then wrote a double album that gave hardcore a plot and a tune. Nine years in, they were done.

3df040ee-2b8b-446b-937a-3f86f4b2cabf.name: Meat Puppets
3df040ee-2b8b-446b-937a-3f86f4b2cabf.label: SST
3df040ee-2b8b-446b-937a-3f86f4b2cabf.lede: Two brothers and a drummer from Phoenix got sick of hardcore and played desert country on acid, until Kurt Cobain put three of their songs on MTV. After a long collapse, the same trio made a record together again in 2019.

0bd450a7-32dd-496f-a0d4-1f71a2226add.name: Saccharine Trust
0bd450a7-32dd-496f-a0d4-1f71a2226add.label: SST
0bd450a7-32dd-496f-a0d4-1f71a2226add.lede: Jack Brewer preached from the mic and Joe Baiza, who still doesn't think of himself as a guitar player, ran jazz through punk a floor above D. Boon. SST treated them as the label's odd one out, and Kurt Cobain put Paganicons in his top 50.

f035837e-4117-438d-a524-cacf43500e68.name: Descendents
f035837e-4117-438d-a524-cacf43500e68.label: SST
f035837e-4117-438d-a524-cacf43500e68.lede: A teenage fisherman, a 34-year-old bassist headed for the post office and a shy biology student in glasses built pop-punk's blueprint in a South Bay rehearsal room, then kept pausing it for graduate school.

77c167d2-4965-4421-830a-9815e4956475.name: Dinosaur Jr.
77c167d2-4965-4421-830a-9815e4956475.label: SST
77c167d2-4965-4421-830a-9815e4956475.lede: Three kids from Amherst, Massachusetts got banned from nearly every club around for volume, made to add a "Jr." by a band of ex-Grateful Dead and Jefferson Airplane members, and fell out so badly that Lou Barlow wrote about it for years. Then J Mascis and Barlow reunited, and the second run made more albums than the first.

78c1866f-92d8-4180-98ea-fe88121aa195.name: Negativland
78c1866f-92d8-4180-98ea-fe88121aa195.label: SST
78c1866f-92d8-4180-98ea-fe88121aa195.lede: Two Concord teenagers started cutting up tape in 1979. Four decades on, Negativland has faked a murder link to dodge a tour, been sued by U2's label and then by its own, and shipped a longtime member's ashes with a CD.

e919b253-da5b-4aae-a444-6a368376a2d6.name: Bad Brains
e919b253-da5b-4aae-a444-6a368376a2d6.label: SST
e919b253-da5b-4aae-a444-6a368376a2d6.lede: Four D.C. jazz-fusion players heard the Ramones, outran everyone in town and got barred from the clubs, and the teenagers trailing them into basements and galleries went on to start Dischord.

707d26d5-51ee-42b2-9bc4-19884689d51c.name: Saint Vitus
707d26d5-51ee-42b2-9bc4-19884689d51c.label: SST
707d26d5-51ee-42b2-9bc4-19884689d51c.lede: Too slow for Los Angeles metal, Saint Vitus found a home when Black Flag's label signed them, and the punks threw things at them anyway. They kept playing doom through new singers, a breakup and a reunion.

bc5e6e42-73ba-44fa-a41e-3379402f0429.name: Screaming Trees
bc5e6e42-73ba-44fa-a41e-3379402f0429.label: SST
bc5e6e42-73ba-44fa-a41e-3379402f0429.lede: Two brawling brothers rehearsed in their parents' video store in Ellensburg, Washington, with a singer whose voice sounded like a burnt church. Seattle's boom put them on Epic and Letterman, and the band still ended without a goodbye.

e675295a-1efe-4247-aa3b-53b78d0cdffc.name: Mudhoney
e675295a-1efe-4247-aa3b-53b78d0cdffc.label: Sub Pop
e675295a-1efe-4247-aa3b-53b78d0cdffc.lede: They took their name from a Russ Meyer movie none of them had seen, put two fuzz pedals on a Sub Pop single, and were still making records for the label in their fourth decade.

78f56916-fe11-4110-8f10-d553ddf8de7b.name: Green River
78f56916-fe11-4110-8f10-d553ddf8de7b.label: Sub Pop
78f56916-fe11-4110-8f10-d553ddf8de7b.lede: Green River lasted three years, put out two EPs and one album, and split on Halloween 1987. The pieces became Mudhoney, Mother Love Bone and, eventually, Pearl Jam.

867d3fb7-9cd1-47a4-a8f0-de29cdca2004.name: Tad
867d3fb7-9cd1-47a4-a8f0-de29cdca2004.label: Sub Pop
867d3fb7-9cd1-47a4-a8f0-de29cdca2004.lede: Tad Doyle was a butcher from Idaho with a three-song demo. Sub Pop made him a lumberjack, sent him across Europe in a van with Nirvana, and let him make some of the heaviest records out of Seattle.

5b11f4ce-a62d-471e-81fc-a69a8278c7da.name: Nirvana
5b11f4ce-a62d-471e-81fc-a69a8278c7da.label: Sub Pop
5b11f4ce-a62d-471e-81fc-a69a8278c7da.lede: Kurt Cobain and Krist Novoselic recorded Bleach for $606.17, and three years later Nevermind was No. 1 on the Billboard 200. Cobain died in April 1994, seven years after the band's first show.

153c9281-268f-4cf3-8938-f5a4593e5df4.name: Soundgarden
153c9281-268f-4cf3-8938-f5a4593e5df4.label: Sub Pop
153c9281-268f-4cf3-8938-f5a4593e5df4.lede: A sculpture that moans in the wind gave them their name, and one night at the Rainbow Tavern gave Sub Pop its first backer. They were the first Seattle band signed to a major label, split in 1997 after a bass went flying in Honolulu, and are still finishing the last songs Chris Cornell sang on.

762e1e6d-ba12-4946-b8ee-dfa0cf9a2655.name: Dwarves
762e1e6d-ba12-4946-b8ee-dfa0cf9a2655.label: Sub Pop
762e1e6d-ba12-4946-b8ee-dfa0cf9a2655.lede: The Dwarves played fifteen-minute sets, sent a masked guitarist onstage in studded leather underpants, and put out a press release announcing his murder. Sub Pop dropped them over it, and they're still going.

2feb192c-2363-46d6-b476-1c88a25cb294.name: The Afghan Whigs
2feb192c-2363-46d6-b476-1c88a25cb294.label: Sub Pop
2feb192c-2363-46d6-b476-1c88a25cb294.lede: Greg Dulli wanted a band that sounded like the Temptations, the Band and Neil Young at once. He got it in Cincinnati, took it to a Seattle grunge label, and he's still at it forty years later.

cecd5f91-cfdd-45d1-879f-3920c7c76e58.name: Codeine
cecd5f91-cfdd-45d1-879f-3920c7c76e58.label: Sub Pop
cecd5f91-cfdd-45d1-879f-3920c7c76e58.lede: Codeine played so slowly that Sub Pop, the grunge label, asked them to fly to Seattle and add fuzz. They declined, and made three records before they quit in 1994.

d98c8149-0c01-4151-93e1-48fdc3d5027f.name: Sebadoh
d98c8149-0c01-4151-93e1-48fdc3d5027f.label: Sub Pop
d98c8149-0c01-4151-93e1-48fdc3d5027f.lede: Thrown out of Dinosaur Jr., Lou Barlow turned his home cassettes into a band with Eric Gaffney and Jason Loewenstein. Three songwriters, one four-track, then a major label that gave them five weeks in Los Angeles and dropped them within weeks of the record.

86b24e8f-a4d9-4c84-83ee-fde0d14ad9fa.name: Sunny Day Real Estate
86b24e8f-a4d9-4c84-83ee-fde0d14ad9fa.label: Sub Pop
86b24e8f-a4d9-4c84-83ee-fde0d14ad9fa.lede: Sunny Day Real Estate cut Diary in Chicago, gave out one interview and one photo to promote it, and split before the follow-up reached stores. Three reunions later, they're still on the road with it.

6c8b9855-ba8b-48f9-ac1d-42167f7f7b18.name: The Shins
6c8b9855-ba8b-48f9-ac1d-42167f7f7b18.label: Sub Pop
6c8b9855-ba8b-48f9-ac1d-42167f7f7b18.lede: A side project from an Albuquerque basement ended up in a McDonald's ad, a Natalie Portman scene and No. 2 on the Billboard 200. Then James Mercer rebuilt the band around himself.

fa97dd36-1b82-43d7-a6e4-2adeafd59cef.name: Fleet Foxes
fa97dd36-1b82-43d7-a6e4-2adeafd59cef.label: Sub Pop
fa97dd36-1b82-43d7-a6e4-2adeafd59cef.lede: Robin Pecknold and Skyler Skjelset started a band in Kirkland, recorded a debut in a parents' basement and put five-part harmonies at the top of 2008's year-end lists. Then the drummer left to become Father John Misty, and Pecknold went back to college.

a506f761-2c22-4b2f-8a94-bd748c2c8f75.name: Neutral Milk Hotel
a506f761-2c22-4b2f-8a94-bd748c2c8f75.label: Merge
a506f761-2c22-4b2f-8a94-bd748c2c8f75.lede: Jeff Mangum made two albums as Neutral Milk Hotel, stopped touring them in 1998 without announcing it, and spent fifteen years out of sight while In the Aeroplane Over the Sea found its audience. By 2013 it had sold more than 393,000 copies without once reaching the Billboard 200.

3ff72a59-f39d-411d-9f93-2d4a86413013.name: The Magnetic Fields
3ff72a59-f39d-411d-9f93-2d4a86413013.label: Merge
3ff72a59-f39d-411d-9f93-2d4a86413013.lede: Stephin Merritt wrote sixty-nine love songs mostly in a Manhattan bar, then fifty songs about his own life, and has kept the shows quiet for the sake of his left ear.

f75150f0-d80d-4c34-903b-6acfb47b63ee.name: Lambchop
f75150f0-d80d-4c34-903b-6acfb47b63ee.label: Merge
f75150f0-d80d-4c34-903b-6acfb47b63ee.lede: Kurt Wagner kept laying hardwood floors in Nashville while his oversized band picked up a name from a lawyer's letter and its first big audience in Europe.

52074ba6-e495-4ef3-9bb4-0703888a9f68.name: Arcade Fire
52074ba6-e495-4ef3-9bb4-0703888a9f68.label: Merge
52074ba6-e495-4ef3-9bb4-0703888a9f68.lede: Arcade Fire made Funeral in a Montreal studio while relatives died, got a 9.7 from Pitchfork, sang with Bowie, took Album of the Year from Eminem, and went disco with James Murphy.

a57e5515-555a-42d6-a92a-465deac3fdd1.name: Polvo
a57e5515-555a-42d6-a92a-465deac3fdd1.label: Merge
a57e5515-555a-42d6-a92a-465deac3fdd1.lede: Ash Bowie and Dave Brylawski met in a Spanish class at UNC and named their band after the Spanish word for dust. Bowie broke strings and kept playing, and Polvo's records got stranger from there, though Bowie says it was never as complicated as people think.

9639cd52-c351-4a17-9797-58880e95a7ef.name: The Mountain Goats
9639cd52-c351-4a17-9797-58880e95a7ef.label: Merge
9639cd52-c351-4a17-9797-58880e95a7ef.lede: John Darnielle started out taping songs into a Panasonic boombox while working a psych-ward job in Southern California. Thirty-odd years on, the Mountain Goats are a four-piece playing rooms where the crowd sings back songs about wrestlers, goths, Dungeons & Dragons and his stepfather.

61604b45-8a91-4e33-a1b6-45d7b1fec4e5.name: Destroyer
61604b45-8a91-4e33-a1b6-45d7b1fec4e5.label: Merge
61604b45-8a91-4e33-a1b6-45d7b1fec4e5.lede: Dan Bejar named his band Destroyer in Vancouver in 1995, not knowing Kiss had an album by that name. Fourteen albums later he's still writing the wordiest songs on Merge, and the saxophones showed up around 2011.

d935bec6-cab7-46cc-bf8b-ca089563b985.name: Crooked Fingers
d935bec6-cab7-46cc-bf8b-ca089563b985.label: Merge
d935bec6-cab7-46cc-bf8b-ca089563b985.lede: Eric Bachmann walked out of the noise of Archers of Loaf and into a band named for his grandfather's CB-radio handle, then wrote slow, dark songs from a Seattle cargo van, between sandwich orders in Denver and from a classroom in Taipei.

3c8ff4c9-b5b9-4e78-ad9d-5157c323de24.name: Wye Oak
3c8ff4c9-b5b9-4e78-ad9d-5157c323de24.label: Merge
3c8ff4c9-b5b9-4e78-ad9d-5157c323de24.lede: Wye Oak took their name from Maryland's state tree, which a storm had flattened four years earlier. Jenn Wasner's guitar was the band's calling card, and in 2013 she announced she was putting it down.

ea8aba9a-0163-439b-91ff-fe02e9d67663.name: The Spinanes
ea8aba9a-0163-439b-91ff-fe02e9d67663.label: Merge
ea8aba9a-0163-439b-91ff-fe02e9d67663.lede: Rebecca Gates and Scott Plouf made a Portland duo out of one guitar and one drum kit, and it handed Sub Pop its first No. 1 on college radio. Then Plouf took a second job drumming for Built to Spill, and Gates moved to Chicago.

44d766e3-fc4a-4c19-9cdc-cd69966de1d8.name: Palace
44d766e3-fc4a-4c19-9cdc-cd69966de1d8.label: Drag City
44d766e3-fc4a-4c19-9cdc-cd69966de1d8.lede: Will Oldham started as a teenage movie actor in Louisville, cut country records with Slint members and his own brothers under a new band name almost every time, and wrote a song Johnny Cash ended up singing.

87e27246-8c40-407f-bfb3-5dc416557eeb.name: Royal Trux
87e27246-8c40-407f-bfb3-5dc416557eeb.label: Drag City
87e27246-8c40-407f-bfb3-5dc416557eeb.lede: Neil Hagerty left Pussy Galore's day job for a band with Jennifer Herrema, cut a double LP in San Francisco, gave Drag City its first record, and took more than $1 million from Virgin. Years after splitting, a Guardian interview ended the reunion.

1bc2d696-c0e2-480d-87ed-17b2a82d7983.name: Silver Jews
1bc2d696-c0e2-480d-87ed-17b2a82d7983.label: Drag City
1bc2d696-c0e2-480d-87ed-17b2a82d7983.lede: David Berman and two college friends taped noise in a Hoboken apartment, and the project became the home for his songs. He avoided the stage until 2006, then ended the band in 2009 in a Tennessee cave.

89af9575-4d72-4345-8eba-e9de3d36ac34.name: Smog
89af9575-4d72-4345-8eba-e9de3d36ac34.label: Drag City
89af9575-4d72-4345-8eba-e9de3d36ac34.lede: Bill Callahan taped the first Smog songs in the late 1980s on machines he could afford, signed to Drag City, and spent seventeen years getting from hiss to some of the plainest songs in American indie. Then he dropped the name.

8f54d90b-f322-4e5d-a0fd-bdc960f2d20f.name: Gastr del Sol
8f54d90b-f322-4e5d-a0fd-bdc960f2d20f.label: Drag City
8f54d90b-f322-4e5d-a0fd-bdc960f2d20f.lede: [[David Grubbs]] started in Louisville hardcore and moved to Chicago for graduate school. He named his next band half for his old one and half for a Derby winner, then spent five years taking rock songs apart with [[Jim O'Rourke]] until the two stopped working together.

f1df0431-9250-4ec8-95d8-f19ce7cf7fb6.name: Stereolab
f1df0431-9250-4ec8-95d8-f19ce7cf7fb6.label: Drag City
f1df0431-9250-4ec8-95d8-f19ce7cf7fb6.lede: Stereolab took its name from a hi-fi demonstration record and spent two decades setting Lætitia Sadier's French vocals and Marxist-flavored lyrics against Farfisa drones. By one count they sold 300,000 albums in America without once pretending to be a rock band.

cb69e1f1-bc76-4df5-93c9-cf97dd8a3b5c.name: Joanna Newsom
cb69e1f1-bc76-4df5-93c9-cf97dd8a3b5c.label: Drag City
cb69e1f1-bc76-4df5-93c9-cf97dd8a3b5c.lede: Joanna Newsom plays a pedal harp and sings in a voice critics argued over, and in six years she goes from a twelve-song debut to an 18-song triple album.

07a17571-81fc-4cf8-a634-98f0d926d313.name: Ty Segall
07a17571-81fc-4cf8-a634-98f0d926d313.label: Drag City
07a17571-81fc-4cf8-a634-98f0d926d313.lede: Ty Segall grew up surfing in Laguna Beach and put out three albums in 2012 alone. Since then he's toured in a baby mask, sung from behind the drums in Fuzz, and kept releasing records nearly every year.

f0303341-cd61-4a2c-a0dc-edae98853a06.name: Sun City Girls
f0303341-cd61-4a2c-a0dc-edae98853a06.label: Drag City
f0303341-cd61-4a2c-a0dc-edae98853a06.lede: Two half-Lebanese brothers named their band after an Arizona retirement town, played it to punk crowds who threw sandwiches, and stopped for good when drummer Charles Gocher died in 2007.

5e521e8c-0ab2-44c4-8fd8-14d8d3321265.name: Isis
5e521e8c-0ab2-44c4-8fd8-14d8d3321265.label: Hydra Head
5e521e8c-0ab2-44c4-8fd8-14d8d3321265.lede: Aaron Turner started Isis in Boston with his roommate Jeff Caxide while already running Hydra Head Records. Five albums later the band ended where it began, in Montreal, and came back once, in 2018, for a benefit.

f3c95ad4-215b-4519-8660-84c9f467da05.name: Cave In
f3c95ad4-215b-4519-8660-84c9f467da05.label: Hydra Head
f3c95ad4-215b-4519-8660-84c9f467da05.lede: Cave In started as metallic hardcore in Methuen, turned toward space rock, signed to RCA, and went back to Hydra Head with the heavy songs the label wouldn't release. Bassist Caleb Scofield died in 2018; the band finished the record he'd played on and kept going.

72448406-ba82-43a7-9e13-d9a47ff333f4.name: Botch
72448406-ba82-43a7-9e13-d9a47ff333f4.label: Hydra Head
72448406-ba82-43a7-9e13-d9a47ff333f4.lede: Four Tacoma high schoolers named their band out of a dictionary, made two albums for Hydra Head, and quit at the Showbox in 2002. In 2024, after a reunion, they quit there again, on purpose.

75a97901-0051-4b67-a79b-9ebf2400d1d9.name: Old Man Gloom
75a97901-0051-4b67-a79b-9ebf2400d1d9.label: Hydra Head
75a97901-0051-4b67-a79b-9ebf2400d1d9.lede: Aaron Turner and Santos Montano started it in Santa Fe in 1999. Boston's Nate Newton and Caleb Scofield made it a four-man pile-up, and it has gone on for 25 years without saying when the joke ends.

019f73df-915e-477b-b026-a2a2740df534.name: Khanate
019f73df-915e-477b-b026-a2a2740df534.label: Hydra Head
019f73df-915e-477b-b026-a2a2740df534.lede: Alan Dubin screams over riffs played at a crawl, in a band put together from OLD, Burning Witch, Sunn O))) and Blind Idiot God. Khanate makes four albums by 2009, goes quiet, then releases a fifth in 2023 with no warning.

300c0909-19cc-4ca2-bee2-82a355d4ac81.name: Harkonen
300c0909-19cc-4ca2-bee2-82a355d4ac81.label: Hydra Head
300c0909-19cc-4ca2-bee2-82a355d4ac81.lede: Harkonen started in Tacoma in 1997 as a five-piece hardcore band, lost members until three were left, cut two records for Hydra Head and played its last show at Bumbershoot in 2005.

ae69d81f-552d-4013-8dfc-4778d8f38742.name: Jesu
ae69d81f-552d-4013-8dfc-4778d8f38742.label: Hydra Head
ae69d81f-552d-4013-8dfc-4778d8f38742.lede: Justin Broadrick ended Godflesh with a song called "Jesu", kept the name for his next band, and spent twenty years slowing metal down until it sounded like a lullaby.

3d722ad8-1986-4ce0-bc98-d0864ef625f2.name: Coalesce
3d722ad8-1986-4ce0-bc98-d0864ef625f2.label: Hydra Head
3d722ad8-1986-4ce0-bc98-d0864ef625f2.lede: Sean Ingram and Jes Steineger came out of Kansas City's straight edge scene, broke the band up in 1996, 1999 and 2010, and keep getting named by metal bands as where they started.

fa31e7d4-a03a-4110-98fc-f8826e95ec25.name: Converge
fa31e7d4-a03a-4110-98fc-f8826e95ec25.label: Deathwish
fa31e7d4-a03a-4110-98fc-f8826e95ec25.lede: Jacob Bannon and Kurt Ballou started Converge in Salem, Massachusetts, as teenagers with a four-track. Thirty-five years on they run their own label and their own studio, draw their own covers, and still make the most carefully built noise in hardcore.

1bfdbf9d-e241-4ad7-8283-a3a7904bb6ca.name: Modern Life Is War
1bfdbf9d-e241-4ad7-8283-a3a7904bb6ca.label: Deathwish
1bfdbf9d-e241-4ad7-8283-a3a7904bb6ca.lede: Five friends from Marshalltown, Iowa, mailed out 100 copies of a 7-inch to book their own tour, put an 1896 photo of their Main Street on the cover of Witness, quit in 2008, and came back to write another record in a basement.

00330ad2-6d94-4957-b3b0-7ca1ea6f6fd6.name: Blacklisted
00330ad2-6d94-4957-b3b0-7ca1ea6f6fd6.label: Deathwish
00330ad2-6d94-4957-b3b0-7ca1ea6f6fd6.lede: [[George Hirsch]] kept quitting Blacklisted and kept coming back. The Philadelphia band tunes down to C and rarely runs past twenty minutes a record.

3039780c-6db4-499a-8b22-ddd0bb7da0af.name: Trash Talk
3039780c-6db4-499a-8b22-ddd0bb7da0af.label: Deathwish
3039780c-6db4-499a-8b22-ddd0bb7da0af.lede: Trash Talk started in Sacramento in 2005 and kept moving: Steve Albini mixed the second record, Keith Morris guested on a single, and Odd Future Records signed them in 2012. Through all of it the band ran its own label.

ea367e3c-4c74-460b-8a99-bbbb9b1ad5cf.name: Touché Amoré
ea367e3c-4c74-460b-8a99-bbbb9b1ad5cf.label: Deathwish
ea367e3c-4c74-460b-8a99-bbbb9b1ad5cf.lede: Jeremy Bolm ran a fan site for Thursday, then started a band in Los Angeles whose debut lasts eighteen minutes. Nine years later he turned his mother's death into the record that became its most popular.

f4ccf6c5-ad41-4f8f-bb9e-6e2c6ad23302.name: Deafheaven
f4ccf6c5-ad41-4f8f-bb9e-6e2c6ad23302.label: Deathwish
f4ccf6c5-ad41-4f8f-bb9e-6e2c6ad23302.lede: George Clarke and Kerry McCoy met in a Modesto rainstorm, recorded a $500 demo, and three years later had a pink album cover that got black metal argued about in places that never cover it.

968bf044-8703-459d-a349-17d15af2ac74.name: The Hope Conspiracy
968bf044-8703-459d-a349-17d15af2ac74.label: Deathwish
968bf044-8703-459d-a349-17d15af2ac74.lede: Boston hardcore with a snarl and a reading list. Four albums in twenty-five years, most of them cut at Kurt Ballou's Godcity, and Kevin Baker is still angry on the newest one.

16d6213e-2138-4a41-8ba5-acf8bd8fc69a.name: Cursed
16d6213e-2138-4a41-8ba5-acf8bd8fc69a.label: Deathwish
16d6213e-2138-4a41-8ba5-acf8bd8fc69a.lede: Chris Colohan finished with the Swarm and built Cursed across Montreal and Ontario, then made three albums loud enough that he got electrocuted on a video shoot. The last European tour ended with the passports and tour money stolen and one show left, in Amsterdam.

582fee78-d934-4603-9f5c-1729e0ca36b7.name: Helmet
582fee78-d934-4603-9f5c-1729e0ca36b7.label: AmRep
582fee78-d934-4603-9f5c-1729e0ca36b7.lede: Page Hamilton left Band of Susans, started a band with short hair and no solos, and cut a $2,500 record that kept Amphetamine Reptile going through the 1990s. Interscope won the bidding war, Meantime went gold, and after the 1998 split Hamilton brought the name back in 2004 and hasn't put it down.

d4b064a0-5567-4930-a359-16fadfa7941b.name: Cows
d4b064a0-5567-4930-a359-16fadfa7941b.label: AmRep
d4b064a0-5567-4930-a359-16fadfa7941b.lede: Cows came out of Minneapolis in 1986 with a front man who played bugle and dressed in shaving cream, mousetraps and stuffed animals. They made nine albums, eight of them on [[Amphetamine Reptile Records]], and ended with one produced by the Melvins' Buzz Osborne.

db9cbc9e-65b6-4221-a847-75981feb1c6b.name: Unsane
db9cbc9e-65b6-4221-a847-75981feb1c6b.label: AmRep
db9cbc9e-65b6-4221-a847-75981feb1c6b.lede: Chris Spencer, Pete Shore and Charlie Ondras put a decapitated subway corpse on the first Unsane cover, lost their drummer to an overdose, and then got a skateboard-wipeout video that cost a couple hundred dollars onto MTV.

9ccfbc94-a4f4-42f7-b6f5-d903ab77cccb.name: Melvins
9ccfbc94-a4f4-42f7-b6f5-d903ab77cccb.label: AmRep
9ccfbc94-a4f4-42f7-b6f5-d903ab77cccb.lede: Three Montesano high schoolers took their name from a Thriftway supervisor, and Kurt Cobain said watching them made him a punk. Four decades on, the band has outlasted Atlantic Records, put out a record under a mirror-written name and played with two drum kits pushed together.

ea15533d-5ea7-4605-85d5-7634c38a6258.name: Hammerhead
ea15533d-5ea7-4605-85d5-7634c38a6258.label: AmRep
ea15533d-5ea7-4605-85d5-7634c38a6258.lede: Three men from Fargo and Moorhead moved to Minneapolis and made three albums for [[Amphetamine Reptile Records]] before [[Paul Sanders]] left for college. They came back in 2010 for the label's 25th anniversary and kept going.

c5790c27-5808-42a2-b409-5395b56c209f.name: Today Is the Day
c5790c27-5808-42a2-b409-5395b56c209f.label: AmRep
c5790c27-5808-42a2-b409-5395b56c209f.lede: Steve Austin taught himself to record on a Fostex four-track at twelve, and he has run Today Is the Day his own way since 1992. Two future Mastodon members passed through in the middle.

e7680f97-5a8b-48d4-8c36-a0e1f01bf239.name: Chokebore
e7680f97-5a8b-48d4-8c36-a0e1f01bf239.label: AmRep
e7680f97-5a8b-48d4-8c36-a0e1f01bf239.lede: Chokebore started in Honolulu, signed to Amphetamine Reptile off a demo tape, and ended up spending seven or eight months a year touring Europe, where the crowds were.

ca210542-af7d-4119-9952-38959029d06f.name: God Bullies
ca210542-af7d-4119-9952-38959029d06f.label: AmRep
ca210542-af7d-4119-9952-38959029d06f.lede: Mike Corso and Mike Hard started God Bullies in a Kalamazoo basement in 1986. Three years later they were making records for Amphetamine Reptile, and in 2024 the survivors finished an album for two bandmates who didn't get to hear it.

1397d045-1603-41fc-80b9-712c18360145.name: Bikini Kill
1397d045-1603-41fc-80b9-712c18360145.label: Kill Rock Stars
1397d045-1603-41fc-80b9-712c18360145.lede: [[Kathleen Hanna]] scrawled a deodorant joke on Kurt Cobain's wall, and Nirvana turned it into the title of their biggest song. Her own band, four people from Olympia, put out three records inside a year.

03ad1736-b7c9-412a-b442-82536d63a5c4.name: Elliott Smith
03ad1736-b7c9-412a-b442-82536d63a5c4.label: Kill Rock Stars
03ad1736-b7c9-412a-b442-82536d63a5c4.lede: Elliott Smith meant a four-track tape from a Portland basement for a seven-inch single. It ended up getting him a Kill Rock Stars deal, an Oscar nomination and a DreamWorks contract.

8716a313-c6df-440c-9b74-370e8d79728e.name: Heavens to Betsy
8716a313-c6df-440c-9b74-370e8d79728e.label: Kill Rock Stars
8716a313-c6df-440c-9b74-370e8d79728e.lede: Corin Tucker and Tracy Sawyer played the 1991 International Pop Underground Convention with, by Tucker's account, hardly a song written. They made one album, quit in 1994, and in 2026 played again after 32 years.

9434776a-bdd7-4f58-b719-b5d95b9d2a11.name: Unwound
9434776a-bdd7-4f58-b719-b5d95b9d2a11.label: Kill Rock Stars
9434776a-bdd7-4f58-b719-b5d95b9d2a11.lede: Justin Trosper, Vern Rumsey and Brandt Sandeno started out playing Hüsker Dü covers in Tumwater. With Sara Lund on drums they made seven albums, each stranger than the last, quit on April Fool's Day 2002, and came back two years after Rumsey died.

d6dfbc0b-d737-49df-be8e-517b85985bcb.name: Bratmobile
d6dfbc0b-d737-49df-be8e-517b85985bcb.label: Kill Rock Stars
d6dfbc0b-d737-49df-be8e-517b85985bcb.lede: Two dorm neighbors in Eugene started a zine, then a band that didn't have instruments yet. They broke up mid-show in New York in 1994, then came back for two more records.

11eabe0c-2638-4808-92f9-1dbd9c453429.name: Deerhoof
11eabe0c-2638-4808-92f9-1dbd9c453429.label: Kill Rock Stars
11eabe0c-2638-4808-92f9-1dbd9c453429.lede: Rob Fisk started Deerhoof with a bass and a harmonica in San Francisco, a drummer showed up a week later, and three decades on the band has opened for Radiohead, played the Large Hadron Collider and pulled its catalog from Spotify.

97b1142f-c71e-4971-8736-4a8ceaf6b4c3.name: The Decemberists
97b1142f-c71e-4971-8736-4a8ceaf6b4c3.label: Kill Rock Stars
97b1142f-c71e-4971-8736-4a8ceaf6b4c3.lede: [[Colin Meloy]] moved from Montana to Portland, wrote songs about sailors and ghosts, watched thieves haul off the band's gear, sent guitarist Chris Funk to duel [[Stephen Colbert]] on TV, and ended up with a number one record made in a barn.

9cf16514-25d6-46c2-8cc8-a8e857e7a3f2.name: Huggy Bear
9cf16514-25d6-46c2-8cc8-a8e857e7a3f2.label: Kill Rock Stars
9cf16514-25d6-46c2-8cc8-a8e857e7a3f2.lede: Five people from Brighton promised to last three years, then turned down the major labels, the photographs and most of the interviews, and split on schedule.

149e6720-4e4a-41a4-afca-6d29083fc091.name: Bad Religion
149e6720-4e4a-41a4-afca-6d29083fc091.label: Epitaph
149e6720-4e4a-41a4-afca-6d29083fc091.lede: Four high schoolers play hardcore in three-part harmony, and one of them starts a label to press the records. Epitaph is still his forty years on.

dcaa4f81-bfb7-44eb-8594-4e74f004b6e4.name: NOFX
dcaa4f81-bfb7-44eb-8594-4e74f004b6e4.label: Epitaph
dcaa4f81-bfb7-44eb-8594-4e74f004b6e4.lede: Three Los Angeles punks turned down every major label, kept their video off MTV, and after 41 years said goodbye over three nights at home in San Pedro.

24f8d8a5-269b-475c-a1cb-792990b0b2ee.name: Rancid
24f8d8a5-269b-475c-a1cb-792990b0b2ee.label: Epitaph
24f8d8a5-269b-475c-a1cb-792990b0b2ee.lede: Tim Armstrong and Matt Freeman buried Operation Ivy at Gilman Street, started over sober, said no to Madonna's label, and ended up on MTV.

5c210861-2ce2-4be3-9307-bbcfc361cc01.name: Pennywise
5c210861-2ce2-4be3-9307-bbcfc361cc01.label: Epitaph
5c210861-2ce2-4be3-9307-bbcfc361cc01.lede: Four Hermosa Beach kids who played backyard parties wrote a song for three dead friends. Its writer died in 1996, the singer quit and came back, and the band kept going for thirty-plus years.

23a03e33-a603-404e-bcbf-2c00159d7067.name: The Offspring
23a03e33-a603-404e-bcbf-2c00159d7067.label: Epitaph
23a03e33-a603-404e-bcbf-2c00159d7067.lede: A $20,000 record, a janitor's day job and a KROQ DJ's hunch make Smash the best-selling independent-label album ever. Then the band walks out on the label that made it.

42884e27-dfb8-453d-990f-2ffd90bc2d1a.name: Refused
42884e27-dfb8-453d-990f-2ffd90bc2d1a.label: Epitaph
42884e27-dfb8-453d-990f-2ffd90bc2d1a.lede: Refused ended in 1998 with police shutting down a basement show in Virginia and a written promise never to play together again. They kept it for 14 years, then turned up at Coachella.

a11aacf5-fcbe-47f9-b065-75f4466c00ae.name: Millencolin
a11aacf5-fcbe-47f9-b065-75f4466c00ae.label: Epitaph
a11aacf5-fcbe-47f9-b065-75f4466c00ae.lede: Three skate rats from Örebro named a band after a trick, signed with a label from their own town and then with Brett Gurewitz's Epitaph. Thirty years on, the four-piece hasn't changed.

7d990fa3-e1a0-4d6e-b266-222a66bd3f83.name: Down by Law
7d990fa3-e1a0-4d6e-b266-222a66bd3f83.label: Epitaph
7d990fa3-e1a0-4d6e-b266-222a66bd3f83.lede: [[Dave Smalley]] had already sung for [[DYS]], [[Dag Nasty]] and [[ALL]] when he started a fourth band in Los Angeles. [[Brett Gurewitz]] signed it after a talk in his car, and a punk take on a Proclaimers hit got it onto MTV.

931e1d1f-6b2f-4ff8-9f70-aa537210cd46.name: Operation Ivy
931e1d1f-6b2f-4ff8-9f70-aa537210cd46.label: Lookout!
931e1d1f-6b2f-4ff8-9f70-aa537210cd46.lede: A Gilman Street band that lasted two years, played about 185 shows and made one album, Operation Ivy ended up behind Rancid and a good share of third-wave ska.

084308bd-1654-436f-ba03-df6697104e19.name: Green Day
084308bd-1654-436f-ba03-df6697104e19.label: Lookout!
084308bd-1654-436f-ba03-df6697104e19.lede: Billie Joe Armstrong and Mike Dirnt were fifteen when they started a band in a Rodeo garage. Their first album cost $675 to make, and by 2024 Wikipedia counts roughly 75 million records sold worldwide.

e4a135d0-1948-4620-bc07-b0217d09ccc1.name: Screeching Weasel
e4a135d0-1948-4620-bc07-b0217d09ccc1.label: Lookout!
e4a135d0-1948-4620-bc07-b0217d09ccc1.lede: Ben Weasel and Jughead started a band in the Chicago suburbs in 1986, ended it three times, and wrote the Ramones-and-bubblegum songs a generation of pop-punk bands learned from. Weasel still fronts it.

79c3a221-4cf6-4594-8181-eb1539d9860f.name: The Mr. T Experience
79c3a221-4cf6-4594-8181-eb1539d9860f.label: Lookout!
79c3a221-4cf6-4594-8181-eb1539d9860f.lede: In 1985 Frank Portman started a Berkeley band named after Mr. T's merchandise. Ten other members came and went, the band spent the 1990s and early 2000s on Lookout!, and in 2006 Portman published a novel.

16615a4c-ccb6-4ea8-9617-e3e0d71f51a9.name: Crimpshrine
16615a4c-ccb6-4ea8-9617-e3e0d71f51a9.label: Lookout!
16615a4c-ccb6-4ea8-9617-e3e0d71f51a9.lede: Two 13-year-olds started S.A.G. in 1982 with one drum and a three-string guitar. By 1989 the band, by then Crimpshrine, had a Lookout! EP, a US tour that came apart in Florida and a regular spot at 924 Gilman Street.

28fd67e8-573c-4cdd-a37d-8b74af74109c.name: The Queers
28fd67e8-573c-4cdd-a37d-8b74af74109c.label: Lookout!
28fd67e8-573c-4cdd-a37d-8b74af74109c.lede: Joe King kept writing Ramones songs for forty years. A drunk but well-rehearsed two days in Indiana gave him the best-selling record of the bunch, and a fight over an Epitaph deal cost him his rhythm section.

a7c3f0e1-027a-4f1f-800a-c115422f96f3.name: Pansy Division
a7c3f0e1-027a-4f1f-800a-c115422f96f3.label: Lookout!
a7c3f0e1-027a-4f1f-800a-c115422f96f3.lede: Jon Ginoli ran a want ad for gay musicians into the Ramones and Buzzcocks, and Chris Freeman answered. A thousand shows later, they're still the loud, funny, unapologetic gay band rock never had.

d70416d3-c006-4a8b-aebd-91a4f198591f.name: The Donnas
d70416d3-c006-4a8b-aebd-91a4f198591f.label: Lookout!
d70416d3-c006-4a8b-aebd-91a4f198591f.lede: Four Palo Alto thirteen-year-olds started a joke band in a garage, took the same last name, and ended up on Letterman with a Kiss cover in the catalog.

fea43e99-c4d5-4dac-9c27-868e864c6dc2.name: Tsunami
fea43e99-c4d5-4dac-9c27-868e864c6dc2.label: Simple Machines
fea43e99-c4d5-4dac-9c27-868e864c6dc2.lede: Jenny Toomey and Kristin Thomson ran a record label from their Arlington living room, started a band for a New Year's party, and toured it for seven years. They closed both in 1998; a box set pulled Tsunami back out of the archive 26 years later.

19c960a1-703e-48e4-8286-37b3aee7a09c.name: Ida
19c960a1-703e-48e4-8286-37b3aee7a09c.label: Simple Machines
19c960a1-703e-48e4-8286-37b3aee7a09c.lede: Daniel Littleton left Annapolis hardcore behind and started singing quietly with Elizabeth Mitchell, and Simple Machines put out the tapes. Three albums later, Ida was the label's gentlest band.

666db644-8738-4362-8754-8f66791de43d.name: Grenadine
666db644-8738-4362-8754-8f66791de43d.label: Simple Machines
666db644-8738-4362-8754-8f66791de43d.lede: Two label owners and a trombonist set down their day bands and made crooning, cocktail-hour pop built around Goya foods.

c5e3744d-b321-4cc9-976a-4d4d9d0ee73a.name: Scrawl
c5e3744d-b321-4cc9-976a-4d4d9d0ee73a.label: Simple Machines
c5e3744d-b321-4cc9-976a-4d4d9d0ee73a.lede: Scrawl bought back its own master tapes at auction, got dropped by Elektra over a fax, and is still playing out of Columbus forty years after Marcy Mays and Sue Harshe started it.

398e10c3-ed3c-424d-a607-3c346b31afa2.name: Retsin
398e10c3-ed3c-424d-a607-3c346b31afa2.label: Simple Machines
398e10c3-ed3c-424d-a607-3c346b31afa2.lede: Tara Jane O'Neil and Cynthia Nelson met on the road in 1993, each in a different touring band. Two years later they were on Simple Machines with an 8-track record, and by 2001 they'd swapped electric guitars for banjo, flute and toy piano.

44a38273-7da3-433e-8213-554452f6f9bd.name: The Hated
44a38273-7da3-433e-8213-554452f6f9bd.label: Simple Machines
44a38273-7da3-433e-8213-554452f6f9bd.lede: Two St. John's College faculty kids in Annapolis name a band from a kibbutz, play church basements and a school playground for five years, then plug back in about 35 years later.

f2578144-0644-4dbc-ae93-e6237aaf9cd4.name: The Mommyheads
f2578144-0644-4dbc-ae93-e6237aaf9cd4.label: Simple Machines
f2578144-0644-4dbc-ae93-e6237aaf9cd4.lede: Adam Cohen started the Mommyheads in 1987, still in high school in New York. A decade later Geffen signed them, barely marketed the record and let them go; they reunited in 2008 and have been releasing records ever since.

f444dc7d-59c1-4ed6-beb7-f90b6d85366c.name: Unrest
f444dc7d-59c1-4ed6-beb7-f90b6d85366c.label: Simple Machines
f444dc7d-59c1-4ed6-beb7-f90b6d85366c.lede: Mark Robinson started a record label in high school, made his band its house act, and by 1993 had a 4AD box set of 7-inches to show for a rule about never playing the same song twice.

1d3da898-4fb4-4445-b704-cd7315e01789.name: Sunn O)))
1d3da898-4fb4-4445-b704-cd7315e01789.label: Southern Lord
1d3da898-4fb4-4445-b704-cd7315e01789.lede: Stephen O'Malley and Greg Anderson stack Sunn amps as a tribute to Earth, then spend 25 years turning the hum into cathedral sets, a Scott Walker album and a self-titled record on Sub Pop.

60dd41cf-8f9d-46d8-bc19-dc7e5acb24c8.name: Earth
60dd41cf-8f9d-46d8-bc19-dc7e5acb24c8.label: Southern Lord
60dd41cf-8f9d-46d8-bc19-dc7e5acb24c8.lede: Dylan Carlson took heavy metal riffs, slowed them to a crawl and made a 73-minute record with no drums. Then he vanished for years and came back playing western noir.

57652bf8-cfe8-42e7-b9a7-5572a7080d8d.name: Boris
57652bf8-cfe8-42e7-b9a7-5572a7080d8d.label: Southern Lord
57652bf8-cfe8-42e7-b9a7-5572a7080d8d.lede: A Tokyo band took its name from a Melvins song, released an hour-long track and called it a single, and has spent three decades declining to repeat itself.

ae720a02-629e-4e9b-98e7-d1f637bd5a49.name: Goatsnake
ae720a02-629e-4e9b-98e7-d1f637bd5a49.label: Southern Lord
ae720a02-629e-4e9b-98e7-d1f637bd5a49.lede: Greg Anderson left Seattle for Los Angeles with a pile of Sabbath-slow riffs, borrowed a rhythm section from the Obsessed and hired a hardcore singer who sounds like soul music.

e5d4491d-1496-4efa-a5b9-e7be001b9f6a.name: Burning Witch
e5d4491d-1496-4efa-a5b9-e7be001b9f6a.label: Southern Lord
e5d4491d-1496-4efa-a5b9-e7be001b9f6a.lede: Burning Witch lasted about three years, played to rooms that emptied by the second song, and cut two EPs, one with Steve Albini at the board. Sunn O))), Goatsnake and Khanate all trace back to it.

e9452446-7702-4853-96ce-5dfe6748d3fb.name: Wolves in the Throne Room
e9452446-7702-4853-96ce-5dfe6748d3fb.label: Southern Lord
e9452446-7702-4853-96ce-5dfe6748d3fb.lede: Brothers Nathan and Aaron Weaver took black metal to an abandoned farm outside Olympia, played it by firelight, and kept saying no to the rock and roll machine.

a7d9c5f6-751d-4ea5-bf6d-39f1751d44a1.name: Nails
a7d9c5f6-751d-4ea5-bf6d-39f1751d44a1.label: Southern Lord
a7d9c5f6-751d-4ea5-bf6d-39f1751d44a1.lede: Todd Jones spent years in other people's hardcore bands, then started one where most songs run under two minutes. Kurt Ballou has recorded all four albums.

e9df4e93-6f7a-448a-a5ac-d30c27a6d22c.name: Black Breath
e9df4e93-6f7a-448a-a5ac-d30c27a6d22c.label: Southern Lord
e9df4e93-6f7a-448a-a5ac-d30c27a6d22c.lede: Two Bellingham friends buy Boss HM-2 pedals, run Swedish death metal through a hardcore band, and end up on Southern Lord with Kurt Ballou at the board for all three albums. Then the band goes quiet, and the story gets sadder before it gets a coda.

39cb09fb-0a41-4f76-a616-62d1d65304c9.name: Antietam
39cb09fb-0a41-4f76-a616-62d1d65304c9.label: Homestead
39cb09fb-0a41-4f76-a616-62d1d65304c9.lede: Tara Key and Tim Harris left Louisville punk for New York, borrowed a name from the Civil War, and have kept Antietam going, with one long gap, for over forty years.

41593aa1-dda6-4a5a-af87-0eebf93e3775.name: Babes in Toyland
41593aa1-dda6-4a5a-af87-0eebf93e3775.label: Twin/Tone
41593aa1-dda6-4a5a-af87-0eebf93e3775.lede: Kat Bjelland told Soul Asylum's singer her band would beat his before she had a band. A drummer who had never played, a BBC DJ who kept playing the records and a Reprise contract followed, then a bass chair that never sat still.

449e44cb-bcae-4c48-a1af-5d8df0f81456.name: Beat Happening
449e44cb-bcae-4c48-a1af-5d8df0f81456.label: K
449e44cb-bcae-4c48-a1af-5d8df0f81456.lede: Calvin Johnson, Heather Lewis and Bret Lunsford started with no bass player, a borrowed drum kit and a label run out of a kitchen. A few years later Johnson and his label partner threw a six-day festival that SPIN called the true Woodstock of the '90s.

0ec95aa0-d79b-4d02-946c-bf8867f7e054.name: Big Dipper
0ec95aa0-d79b-4d02-946c-bf8867f7e054.label: Homestead
0ec95aa0-d79b-4d02-946c-bf8867f7e054.lede: Bill Goffrier and Gary Waleik started on a Boston porch with songs left over from two broken-up bands, painted UFOs on their sleeves, and made one Epic album, Slam, with a cover they hated.

37c78aeb-d196-42b5-b991-6afb4fc9bc2e.name: Dead Kennedys
37c78aeb-d196-42b5-b991-6afb4fc9bc2e.label: Alternative Tentacles
37c78aeb-d196-42b5-b991-6afb4fc9bc2e.lede: Jello Biafra ran for mayor of San Francisco, a Giger poster put him in a Los Angeles courtroom, and when the band split in 1986 the fights moved on to who owns the songs.

1cf41bc8-6033-4294-8e45-68613a80aae4.name: The Dicks
1cf41bc8-6033-4294-8e45-68613a80aae4.label: Alternative Tentacles
1cf41bc8-6033-4294-8e45-68613a80aae4.lede: Gary Floyd put up flyers in Austin for a band that didn't exist, then had to find one; Mudhoney and the Jesus Lizard later covered its songs.

0f0b2f97-a073-4a92-ab99-ff7980ad7fca.name: D.O.A.
0f0b2f97-a073-4a92-ab99-ff7980ad7fca.label: Alternative Tentacles
0f0b2f97-a073-4a92-ab99-ff7980ad7fca.lede: Joe Keithley, who calls himself Joey Shithead, put "hardcore" on an album in 1981, kept touring it for four decades and in 2018 won a seat on Burnaby city council.

35968888-6cfb-4590-8f70-60886d0be91a.name: Dub Narcotic Sound System
35968888-6cfb-4590-8f70-60886d0be91a.label: K
35968888-6cfb-4590-8f70-60886d0be91a.lede: Calvin Johnson took the melodica out of Beat Happening, ran it through a dub echo, and made party records in the basement studio at his own label. In 1997 the Jon Spencer Blues Explosion drove to Olympia to pay off a debt and found a room with a microphone and not much else.

974b1bfe-dc7a-419a-94f4-f387a193e273.name: Golden Smog
974b1bfe-dc7a-419a-94f4-f387a193e273.label: Twin/Tone
974b1bfe-dc7a-419a-94f4-f387a193e273.lede: Dan Murphy and Dave Pirner dressed up as the Eagles to annoy a hardcore crowd, and the joke grew into a band named after a Flintstones gag. Jeff Tweedy turned up in Murphy's basement in 1994, and the side project has kept coming back since.

337c6e9f-4d6a-49ae-907e-78af6a52a6ee.name: Great Plains
337c6e9f-4d6a-49ae-907e-78af6a52a6ee.label: Homestead
337c6e9f-4d6a-49ae-907e-78af6a52a6ee.lede: Ron House fronted a Columbus band that wrote about Rutherford B. Hayes, Lincoln Logs and record-store clerks, and put it all out on Homestead, a label with a name for unpaid royalties.

859c297a-f739-45f2-ac58-401eeb2d017f.name: The Halo Benders
859c297a-f739-45f2-ac58-401eeb2d017f.label: K
859c297a-f739-45f2-ac58-401eeb2d017f.lede: Calvin Johnson ran K Records, Doug Martsch fronted Built to Spill, and together they made three albums in which neither singer read the other's lyrics. A drug stop in Utah ended up on television.

24ed5b09-02b1-47fe-bd83-6fa5270039b0.name: The Jayhawks
24ed5b09-02b1-47fe-bd83-6fa5270039b0.label: Twin/Tone
24ed5b09-02b1-47fe-bd83-6fa5270039b0.lede: Two Minneapolis rockabilly guitarists started a country-rock band in a punk town, finished a record from demos, and got signed because a producer overheard it through a phone call.

50f50c49-6cca-45b7-8717-0af54a6ad469.name: Karp
50f50c49-6cca-45b7-8717-0af54a6ad469.label: K
50f50c49-6cca-45b7-8717-0af54a6ad469.lede: Three Tumwater classmates named their band after a zine with a very rude title, put out three albums on K Records, and got picked by Beck as an opening act.

4430600b-0fdb-43a1-be52-c81aa7ab1682.name: Lard
4430600b-0fdb-43a1-be52-c81aa7ab1682.label: Alternative Tentacles
4430600b-0fdb-43a1-be52-c81aa7ab1682.lede: Jello Biafra showed up at Chicago Trax with newspaper clippings instead of lyrics, and [[Al Jourgensen]] and [[Paul Barker]] turned them into songs. Lard has never officially toured, and it keeps getting announced anyway.

cb712405-f411-4ba7-b687-f6ecafad0f65.name: Live Skull
cb712405-f411-4ba7-b687-f6ecafad0f65.label: Homestead
cb712405-f411-4ba7-b687-f6ecafad0f65.lede: Mark C. and Tom Paine left San Francisco for downtown New York, split the singing three ways and made a band loud enough for Gowanus. In 1987 Thalia Zedek, whose band Uzi had just ended, took over the lead vocal.

65e1b41c-c719-4237-9f72-c2f07ea19355.name: Lync
65e1b41c-c719-4237-9f72-c2f07ea19355.label: K
65e1b41c-c719-4237-9f72-c2f07ea19355.lede: Three Olympia kids put out four 7-inches and one album on K Records in about two years, then just stopped playing. The members scattered into Beck's records, Built to Spill's touring band and Love as Laughter.

16c8fd0a-6fe9-43c7-8255-eb1b6790e1db.name: Mecca Normal
16c8fd0a-6fe9-43c7-8255-eb1b6790e1db.label: K
16c8fd0a-6fe9-43c7-8255-eb1b6790e1db.lede: [[Jean Smith]] sings, [[David Lester]] plays guitar, and nobody else is invited; [[Kathleen Hanna]] says she wouldn't be in a band if she hadn't heard of Smith.

85d2e30c-92fd-4c7f-a2dc-f988a70e234d.name: Naked Raygun
85d2e30c-92fd-4c7f-a2dc-f988a70e234d.label: Homestead
85d2e30c-92fd-4c7f-a2dc-f988a70e234d.lede: Naked Raygun began at a Chicago bar in 1980, lent two members to Big Black, split in 1992, came back at Riot Fest in 2006, and in 2015 opened for the Foo Fighters at Wrigley Field.

a9416fb3-4d28-4575-abae-f0d160be83ed.name: Neurosis
a9416fb3-4d28-4575-abae-f0d160be83ed.label: Alternative Tentacles
a9416fb3-4d28-4575-abae-f0d160be83ed.lede: In 1985 three Oakland punks decided their band would have keyboards and a slide projector. Four decades on, the records are still getting heavier.

37e9d7b2-7779-41b2-b2eb-3685351caad3.name: NoMeansNo
37e9d7b2-7779-41b2-b2eb-3685351caad3.label: Alternative Tentacles
37e9d7b2-7779-41b2-b2eb-3685351caad3.lede: Two brothers in Victoria couldn't find a guitarist, so a bass and a drum kit did the job. Thirty-seven years later, in 2016, John Wright announced the retirement.

dc0d05ce-2f47-4962-b4fa-8631a0a51987.name: The Replacements
dc0d05ce-2f47-4962-b4fa-8631a0a51987.label: Twin/Tone
dc0d05ce-2f47-4962-b4fa-8631a0a51987.lede: A janitor with a notebook walks in on two teenage brothers and a drummer in a Minneapolis basement, and over twelve years they write Let It Be and Pleased to Meet Me and just as dependably wreck the shows meant to sell them.

b10db9ad-b4c3-47f3-a7a4-37864b134f65.name: Soul Asylum
b10db9ad-b4c3-47f3-a7a4-37864b134f65.label: Twin/Tone
b10db9ad-b4c3-47f3-a7a4-37864b134f65.lede: Dave Pirner's band started as Loud Fast Rules, put out three records in 1986 for Twin/Tone, then took a ballad written on a napkin to No. 5 and a Grammy. After Karl Mueller died in 2005, Pirner kept the name going.

5dbf117b-c076-4d3b-b7ae-13517c25b2cf.name: Squirrel Bait
5dbf117b-c076-4d3b-b7ae-13517c25b2cf.label: Homestead
5dbf117b-c076-4d3b-b7ae-13517c25b2cf.lede: Five Louisville high schoolers played roughly two dozen shows, made one EP and one LP, and split up before most of them could legally buy a drink. Slint, Bastro and Gastr del Sol grew out of the wreckage.

aad33feb-a3bc-482e-8269-4c7d853fe181.name: The Suburbs
aad33feb-a3bc-482e-8269-4c7d853fe181.label: Twin/Tone
aad33feb-a3bc-482e-8269-4c7d853fe181.lede: Nine songs on red vinyl in 1978 were the first record Twin/Tone ever pressed. Sixteen years on, a live album by the same band was the last.

3285dc48-9505-469d-ad8a-bdf2d3dba632.name: Swans
3285dc48-9505-469d-ad8a-bdf2d3dba632.label: Homestead
3285dc48-9505-469d-ad8a-bdf2d3dba632.lede: Michael Gira started Swans to make a room hurt, taught the band to sing, shut it down in 1997, and brought it back in 2010 with records that run two hours.

6f2f87e7-3ce9-4f1c-81dd-6f068a78cf26.name: The Microphones
6f2f87e7-3ce9-4f1c-81dd-6f068a78cf26.label: K
6f2f87e7-3ce9-4f1c-81dd-6f068a78cf26.lede: Phil Elverum recorded his first Microphones tapes in the back room of an Anacortes record store, then took them to Olympia and K Records. He ran a guitar through a thrift-store cassette deck, made The Glow Pt. 2, and dropped the name in 2003. In 2020 he picked it back up for one 44-minute song.

7903b54d-b1ce-4061-91ef-4e8b25fbdc33.name: Tiger Trap
7903b54d-b1ce-4061-91ef-4e8b25fbdc33.label: K
7903b54d-b1ce-4061-91ef-4e8b25fbdc33.lede: Rose Melberg started Tiger Trap in Sacramento in 1992 and had it finished by January 1994. In between came one album that outsold anything K Records had released to that point.

c807804d-c5fe-49bc-a3dd-ece614b9d8c8.name: Trip Shakespeare
c807804d-c5fe-49bc-a3dd-ece614b9d8c8.label: Twin/Tone
c807804d-c5fe-49bc-a3dd-ece614b9d8c8.lede: Two Harvard kids and a Minnesota bassist started a trio in Minneapolis, the city of Hüsker Dü and Prince, then added the older brother and signed to A&M. Then came Nirvana, and the label stopped knowing what to do with them.

3bf93ae1-bb48-4cb5-989a-b179987d03d2.name: Victims Family
3bf93ae1-bb48-4cb5-989a-b179987d03d2.label: Alternative Tentacles
3bf93ae1-bb48-4cb5-989a-b179987d03d2.lede: Two Santa Rosa teenagers started a trio in 1984, drew a one-year Canadian ban, and landed a Dutch radio hit. At home, Green Day and Mr. Bungle were the openers.

4837e8d3-a13f-4670-9684-82970411f4bc.name: Volcano Suns
4837e8d3-a13f-4670-9684-82970411f4bc.label: Homestead
4837e8d3-a13f-4670-9684-82970411f4bc.lede: Mission of Burma ended because Roger Miller's ears gave out, and its drummer Peter Prescott started another loud band the following spring. Four guitarists and three bassists later, Steve Albini was behind the desk for the last record.

c0eee88b-47f2-4cd2-ac48-a045e902a432.name: Ween
c0eee88b-47f2-4cd2-ac48-a045e902a432.label: Twin/Tone
c0eee88b-47f2-4cd2-ac48-a045e902a432.lede: Two guys and a DAT machine out of New Hope, Pennsylvania, made a soul record, a country record and a sea record, and nobody ever worked out when they were joking.

4a48f534-9b66-495c-a934-b775beda1ca7.name: Zeni Geva
4a48f534-9b66-495c-a934-b775beda1ca7.label: Alternative Tentacles
4a48f534-9b66-495c-a934-b775beda1ca7.lede: KK Null named his Tokyo band for money and violence, then flew it to Chicago in 1991 to be recorded by Steve Albini. Albini ended up working on five of their records.

91d06612-5c1e-4278-b40b-b6ce22dc9bb4.name: 7 Year Bitch
91d06612-5c1e-4278-b40b-b6ce22dc9bb4.label: C/Z
91d06612-5c1e-4278-b40b-b6ce22dc9bb4.lede: Four women from Seattle's Capitol Hill lost their guitarist weeks before their first album and named the second for a friend murdered a year later. Atlantic signed them, and in 1997, seven years after they began, they stopped.

7cf05db3-24e7-4534-84bf-65006cd0cc82.name: Archers of Loaf
7cf05db3-24e7-4534-84bf-65006cd0cc82.label: Alias
7cf05db3-24e7-4534-84bf-65006cd0cc82.lede: Four friends from Asheville made a $5,000 debut, got a Beavis and Butt-Head cameo, and turned down a major-label offer because of who else was on the roster.

3ac482b8-1494-4071-a0e9-f192f9d2c2b0.name: Built to Spill
3ac482b8-1494-4071-a0e9-f192f9d2c2b0.label: Up Records
3ac482b8-1494-4071-a0e9-f192f9d2c2b0.lede: Doug Martsch wrote long songs so radio would ignore him, kept swapping bandmates, and still landed three records on Pitchfork's list of the 1990s.

1131e5da-dfdf-46c9-b6ff-b7ac552c2a3c.name: The Dismemberment Plan
1131e5da-dfdf-46c9-b6ff-b7ac552c2a3c.label: DeSoto
1131e5da-dfdf-46c9-b6ff-b7ac552c2a3c.lede: A D.C. band records its best-known album on Interscope's money, gets dropped in the merger, and watches DeSoto, the label two Jawbox alumni run, put it out anyway.

608c9da7-d3ef-4661-828b-24bb6ae20cd6.name: Drive Like Jehu
608c9da7-d3ef-4661-828b-24bb6ae20cd6.label: Headhunter
608c9da7-d3ef-4661-828b-24bb6ae20cd6.lede: Drive Like Jehu made two albums, split without telling anyone, and came back 19 years later for a free afternoon in front of a pipe organ in Balboa Park.

4de3cfed-b459-42bd-bfbb-7a843fbc73df.name: Galaxie 500
4de3cfed-b459-42bd-bfbb-7a843fbc73df.label: Rough Trade
4de3cfed-b459-42bd-bfbb-7a843fbc73df.lede: Three Harvard kids made three albums in three years with one producer. Then Dean Wareham told Damon Krukowski not to buy the plane tickets to Japan.

b916a410-ee27-4f15-92ce-1ce2b60e7697.name: The Gits
b916a410-ee27-4f15-92ce-1ce2b60e7697.label: C/Z
b916a410-ee27-4f15-92ce-1ce2b60e7697.lede: Four Antioch College friends moved into a Capitol Hill house called the Rathouse and made two of Seattle's fastest, tightest punk records. Then Mia Zapata was killed, and the band's story turned into the story of the case.

dfa0e21c-ee3e-44da-81d5-58e3c1218a9f.name: Hot Snakes
dfa0e21c-ee3e-44da-81d5-58e3c1218a9f.label: Swami
dfa0e21c-ee3e-44da-81d5-58e3c1218a9f.lede: Hot Snakes made three records in five years in whatever weeks four calendars overlapped, with a singer in New York and a drummer in Philadelphia. A 2011 reunion brought a fourth album, and a fifth was very near done when Rick Froberg died in 2023.

ec88cdc3-0517-4951-b5ef-7323e7316db0.name: Jawbreaker
ec88cdc3-0517-4951-b5ef-7323e7316db0.label: Tupelo
ec88cdc3-0517-4951-b5ef-7323e7316db0.lede: Three Santa Monica kids who swore off major labels signed to DGC for a reported $1 million, then played to fans who sat down on the floor. Twenty-one years after the split, a festival put them back on a stage.

56f3de75-2c88-4054-a1df-65c661f4ee0f.name: June of 44
56f3de75-2c88-4054-a1df-65c661f4ee0f.label: Quarterstick
56f3de75-2c88-4054-a1df-65c661f4ee0f.lede: Jeff Mueller, Sean Meadows, Fred Erskine and Doug Scharin came from four cities and four bands, cut a record in Brooklyn in four days, then spent five years stretching the template into dub, strings and a fifteen-minute closer.

57111f1f-9829-45ea-bb4e-a5aba37cd1d1.name: L7
57111f1f-9829-45ea-bb4e-a5aba37cd1d1.label: Sub Pop
57111f1f-9829-45ea-bb4e-a5aba37cd1d1.lede: Donita Sparks and Suzi Gardner named their band after slang for square. Then came riffs a wrestler used for his entrance music, a Prodigy cover, and the night Sparks dropped her jeans on British TV.

2d67239c-aa40-4ad5-a807-9052b66857a6.name: Le Tigre
2d67239c-aa40-4ad5-a807-9052b66857a6.label: Mr. Lady
2d67239c-aa40-4ad5-a807-9052b66857a6.lede: Kathleen Hanna named Le Tigre in 1994, four years before it had a member. When Bikini Kill ended, she finally put a band behind the name, and it played dance floors for the next quarter century.

e297ecdf-64ec-4e34-899d-80380f5b0c2a.name: Rocket from the Crypt
e297ecdf-64ec-4e34-899d-80380f5b0c2a.label: Headhunter
e297ecdf-64ec-4e34-899d-80380f5b0c2a.lede: Six people in matching outfits let a game show wheel pick the setlist, and anyone with the logo tattooed on their body gets in free for life.

1e9250c4-46d2-48f1-b7c7-5f1c0a6b1abd.name: Rodan
1e9250c4-46d2-48f1-b7c7-5f1c0a6b1abd.label: Quarterstick
1e9250c4-46d2-48f1-b7c7-5f1c0a6b1abd.lede: Rodan made one album in four weeks, played its last show in September 1994, and sent four members off to start Shipping News, June of 44, Rachel's, Retsin and the Sonora Pine.

b506d0b1-fd16-4ba0-a3dc-a20095c93024.name: Team Dresch
b506d0b1-fd16-4ba0-a3dc-a20095c93024.label: Chainsaw
b506d0b1-fd16-4ba0-a3dc-a20095c93024.lede: A zine, two labels and one 16-year-old's letter turned into a queercore band that booked its first tour over AOL and printed Mariel Hemingway, mid-hurdle, on its T-shirts.

65aac2dc-216c-4b1a-8501-45567c901c0e.name: Wipers
65aac2dc-216c-4b1a-8501-45567c901c0e.label: Park Avenue
65aac2dc-216c-4b1a-8501-45567c901c0e.lede: Greg Sage taped punk records on a four-track in Portland and sold almost none of them for a decade. Then Kurt Cobain started telling anyone who asked that Nirvana learned everything from the Wipers.

1d779dfd-d292-48b5-b232-a09687b9881a.name: Aldous Harding
1d779dfd-d292-48b5-b232-a09687b9881a.label: 4AD
1d779dfd-d292-48b5-b232-a09687b9881a.lede: Aldous Harding busked her way out of Lyttelton, sings in about six different voices, keeps her lyrics to herself, and has made three of her five albums at the same Welsh studio with the same producer.

535b5de2-6673-4810-b952-6930879fb064.name: Ana Roxanne
535b5de2-6673-4810-b952-6930879fb064.label: Kranky
535b5de2-6673-4810-b952-6930879fb064.lede: Ana Roxanne Recto wanted to be Alicia Keys, then studied jazz in Iowa and Hindustani singing in India before landing at Mills College with a room of analog synthesizers. Six years after her Kranky debut, she took the tape haze off her voice.

69158f97-4c07-4c4e-baf8-4e4ab1ed666e.name: Boards of Canada
69158f97-4c07-4c4e-baf8-4e4ab1ed666e.label: Warp
69158f97-4c07-4c4e-baf8-4e4ab1ed666e.lede: Two brothers from the Pentland Hills, Michael Sandison and Marcus Eoin, make music that sounds like a home video someone taped over. In 2013 they announced an album by hiding six-digit codes in a 12-inch, a radio playlist and a cartoon ad.

260b6184-8828-48eb-945c-bc4cb6fc34ca.name: Charli xcx
260b6184-8828-48eb-945c-bc4cb6fc34ca.label: Atlantic
260b6184-8828-48eb-945c-bc4cb6fc34ca.lede: She writes a No. 1 for someone else, spends two years making pop her own label doesn't know what to do with, then gives a whole summer her name.

96c1edac-1011-4cb8-882c-27248de35071.name: The Cramps
96c1edac-1011-4cb8-882c-27248de35071.label: Vengeance
96c1edac-1011-4cb8-882c-27248de35071.lede: Two record collectors moved from Sacramento to New York, played CBGB with no bass player and recorded in Memphis with Alex Chilton. The tapes from that 1977 session finally came out in 2026, through Henry Rollins and Ian MacKaye.

9018ba16-a391-4a08-af8c-21cdc52672c2.name: Gilla Band
9018ba16-a391-4a08-af8c-21cdc52672c2.label: Rough Trade
9018ba16-a391-4a08-af8c-21cdc52672c2.lede: Three school friends who wanted to be the Strokes added a drummer, a Rough Trade deal and a singer with a breakdown to write about. Girl Band became Gilla Band, and Pugnello, their fourth album, picked up five stars from the Guardian.

ee232ef6-4bfd-49c8-a135-b7f82b564531.name: Grace Ives
ee232ef6-4bfd-49c8-a135-b7f82b564531.label: True Panther Sounds
ee232ef6-4bfd-49c8-a135-b7f82b564531.lede: Grace Ives wrote her first songs on a used Roland in a dorm at SUNY Purchase. Since then: three albums, one pink dye job, and a Pitchfork 8.4 for the record she made sober.

b6799f5e-77dc-456a-b456-9177b92b195c.name: Lex Walton
b6799f5e-77dc-456a-b456-9177b92b195c.label: Sub Pop
b6799f5e-77dc-456a-b456-9177b92b195c.lede: Lex Walton wrote a pop manifesto on the night shift as a security guard at Boston's Museum of Fine Arts, self-released a catalog that Sub Pop counts at a dozen or so records and Album of the Year counts at 36, and ended up on Sub Pop with Wolf Parade's Dan Boeckner producing.

76970ff5-1330-4e08-9aa2-f896109660ce.name: L'Rain
76970ff5-1330-4e08-9aa2-f896109660ce.label: Mexican Summer
76970ff5-1330-4e08-9aa2-f896109660ce.lede: Taja Cheek ran a radio station out of a pink Cadillac, booked a basement venue under her own apartment and curated at MoMA PS1, then took her mother's name for a band. Pitchfork gave her fourth record as L'Rain an 8.2.

9ed67b68-9fa7-471a-99eb-483139293274.name: Mandy, Indiana
9ed67b68-9fa7-471a-99eb-483139293274.label: Sacred Bones
9ed67b68-9fa7-471a-99eb-483139293274.lede: Mandy, Indiana started in Manchester as Gary, Indiana, recorded a debut in a cave and a crypt, then drew its best reviews yet for URGH, an album with billy woods on it.

d296518f-e5e3-4ba9-a026-560916dcbc2f.name: My New Band Believe
d296518f-e5e3-4ba9-a026-560916dcbc2f.label: Rough Trade
d296518f-e5e3-4ba9-a026-560916dcbc2f.lede: Cameron Picton wrote a band name down in a food-poisoning haze on a black midi tour of China, then built an acoustic record on Rough Trade that Pitchfork scored 8.4, with a lineup that changes from song to song.

5efbd5c9-5cb1-4166-b121-e79d16aebad4.name: Nino Paid
5efbd5c9-5cb1-4166-b121-e79d16aebad4.label: Signal Records
5efbd5c9-5cb1-4166-b121-e79d16aebad4.lede: Jacquan Andrews wrote his first songs at eight, spent years in foster care, quit rapping, and came back in 2022 as Nino Paid. One sad-song video later he had a Columbia-backed deal, and two years after that an XXL Freshman cover.

e913c999-cee5-4722-867c-0f4b08562e27.name: Nirosta Steel
e913c999-cee5-4722-867c-0f4b08562e27.label: ULYSSA
e913c999-cee5-4722-867c-0f4b08562e27.lede: Steven Hall sang harmonies for Arthur Russell in the '70s, then kept his own tapes for forty years. At 69 a double LP built from them gets a 9.0 from Pitchfork.

6925db17-f35e-42f3-a4eb-84ee6bf5d4b0.name: Olivia Rodrigo
6925db17-f35e-42f3-a4eb-84ee6bf5d4b0.label: Geffen
6925db17-f35e-42f3-a4eb-84ee6bf5d4b0.lede: Olivia Rodrigo wrote a Disney+ song in three days, signed a record deal off it, and has since opened every album cycle with a number one single.

96855c21-b832-4366-ba12-0d2330c36a86.name: Phoebe Bridgers
96855c21-b832-4366-ba12-0d2330c36a86.label: Dead Oceans
96855c21-b832-4366-ba12-0d2330c36a86.lede: Phoebe Bridgers wrote a debut about grief, smashed a guitar on Saturday Night Live, formed two bands with famous friends, and put out a third album that Pitchfork scored 8.4.

7c52dc5d-9c3e-4abc-a313-5ed9977d3476.name: Picture
7c52dc5d-9c3e-4abc-a313-5ed9977d3476.label: Short Span
7c52dc5d-9c3e-4abc-a313-5ed9977d3476.lede: Natal Zaks made sunlit house in Aarhus for a decade under other names. In 2026 he put out two double LPs of dub techno as Picture, and the second drew an 8.2 from Pitchfork.

423a85de-66ba-4113-abdc-ba2678ee89ba.name: Ratboys
423a85de-66ba-4113-abdc-ba2678ee89ba.label: New West
423a85de-66ba-4113-abdc-ba2678ee89ba.lede: Julia Steiner and Dave Sagan met in a Notre Dame Facebook group in 2010, went through nine drummers on the way to a four-piece, and in 2026 made a record about talking to an empty chair.

5b8f4a81-8103-4583-9c24-7ad5496f1476.name: Sideshow
5b8f4a81-8103-4583-9c24-7ad5496f1476.label: 10K
5b8f4a81-8103-4583-9c24-7ad5496f1476.lede: Sideshow, born in Tigray and raised in the DMV, spent six years putting out short, murky tapes from LA. Then came 32 tracks across four discs and an 8.4 from Pitchfork.

96949f2e-dc5f-4493-bd65-02d52cb88f78.name: Starker
96949f2e-dc5f-4493-bd65-02d52cb88f78.label: RRR Music Group
96949f2e-dc5f-4493-bd65-02d52cb88f78.lede: Starker draws a cartoon dog for Westside Gunn, owns Polo pieces the company's own offices lack, and in 2026 takes an 8.4 from Pitchfork for a 32-minute tape about a Brooklyn that's mostly gone.

ab1a3f85-e0ea-470a-af5c-175447ae774c.name: underscores
ab1a3f85-e0ea-470a-af5c-175447ae774c.label: Mom + Pop
ab1a3f85-e0ea-470a-af5c-175447ae774c.lede: She started posting dubstep at 13, taught herself guitar to make a debut, then wrote her best-reviewed record on escalators and in airports. underscores now opens arenas for Charli XCX.

155cfd40-dcde-471e-acc0-32179916165c.name: xaviersobased
155cfd40-dcde-471e-acc0-32179916165c.label: Atlantic
155cfd40-dcde-471e-acc0-32179916165c.lede: A Manhattan kid trades a gaming headset for a microphone, uploads 'patchmade', and ends up on Atlantic with a debut album that Pitchfork scored 8.3.

60f5cb67-691a-412b-b6ef-18372ac45e7b.name: Los Thuthanaka
60f5cb67-691a-412b-b6ef-18372ac45e7b.label: Self-released
60f5cb67-691a-412b-b6ef-18372ac45e7b.lede: Two Aymara siblings put a 61-minute record on Bandcamp with no warning, and Pitchfork ranked it first among the albums of 2025.

cceea21d-f3ec-4586-be7a-d2e939c15c78.name: Dijon
cceea21d-f3ec-4586-be7a-d2e939c15c78.label: R&R / Warner
cceea21d-f3ec-4586-be7a-d2e939c15c78.lede: Dijon Duenas grew up on military bases, cut his first records with a college friend in Maryland, and spent years as a name in other people's credits. Then he made an album for his newborn son, and Pitchfork put it at No. 2 for 2025.

79c6b6f4-cb92-4f03-a1ef-82e7aa4eddbb.name: Cameron Winter
79c6b6f4-cb92-4f03-a1ef-82e7aa4eddbb.label: Partisan
79c6b6f4-cb92-4f03-a1ef-82e7aa4eddbb.lede: Cameron Winter quit hockey after concussions, took up the piano, and made a baritone record his own label doubted could pay his rent. Pitchfork put it third on its 2025 albums list.

13e2db47-3010-48b8-a8b9-667551f37119.name: Oklou
13e2db47-3010-48b8-a8b9-667551f37119.label: Because Music
13e2db47-3010-48b8-a8b9-667551f37119.lede: Marylou Mayniel trained as a cellist in Poitiers, spent a decade in Paris DJ crews and laptop cassettes, and then made the debut album Pitchfork ranked fourth in the world for 2025.

89aa5ecb-59ad-46f5-b3eb-2d424e941f19.name: Bad Bunny
89aa5ecb-59ad-46f5-b3eb-2d424e941f19.label: Rimas Entertainment
89aa5ecb-59ad-46f5-b3eb-2d424e941f19.lede: He bagged groceries in Vega Baja, posted one song to SoundCloud, and in February 2026 played the Super Bowl halftime show mostly in Spanish, behind an album Pitchfork ranked No. 5 of 2025.

9833b455-0da2-40b5-8e63-37816c910604.name: Wednesday
9833b455-0da2-40b5-8e63-37816c910604.label: Dead Oceans
9833b455-0da2-40b5-8e63-37816c910604.lede: Karly Hartzman started Wednesday as a solo project while still a photography student in Asheville, and named it after a British jangle-pop band. Eight years on, the five-piece with the pedal steel and the feedback has Pitchfork's No. 6 album of 2025.

e0c97a4d-c392-41a9-a374-57af3e3eeab3.name: Geese
e0c97a4d-c392-41a9-a374-57af3e3eeab3.label: Partisan Records
e0c97a4d-c392-41a9-a374-57af3e3eeab3.lede: Geese started as schoolmates running through a Tame Impala cover in a Fort Greene basement. Nine years later the New Yorker and NME both put Getting Killed at the top of their 2025 lists.

daf06c03-68bc-4619-80e1-519b5fc67424.name: Joanne Robertson
daf06c03-68bc-4619-80e1-519b5fc67424.label: AD 93
daf06c03-68bc-4619-80e1-519b5fc67424.lede: Joanne Robertson trained as a painter, sang on two of Dean Blunt's albums, and spent nearly twenty years making diary-like records of her own. In 2025 one of them, Blurrr, landed at No. 8 on Pitchfork's year-end list.

6420dd6b-8232-42db-9cb9-90bec8f40e91.name: Nourished by Time
6420dd6b-8232-42db-9cb9-90bec8f40e91.label: XL Recordings
6420dd6b-8232-42db-9cb9-90bec8f40e91.lede: Marcus Brown stocked shelves at a Koreatown Whole Foods, recorded Erotic Probiotic 2 in his parents' Baltimore basement for zero dollars, and landed on Pitchfork's year-end top ten twice, at No. 5 in 2023 and No. 9 in 2025.

29fab96f-c3a2-4251-80f6-7ccda50da706.name: Amaarae
29fab96f-c3a2-4251-80f6-7ccda50da706.label: Interscope
29fab96f-c3a2-4251-80f6-7ccda50da706.lede: Amaarae grew up between the Bronx, Atlanta and Accra, kept getting told she didn't fit a genre, and made a Pitchfork top-ten album out of the mismatch.

4b913922-5cc8-4d9a-bbd8-19d7f9fa0cd5.name: Smerz
4b913922-5cc8-4d9a-bbd8-19d7f9fa0cd5.label: Escho
4b913922-5cc8-4d9a-bbd8-19d7f9fa0cd5.lede: Two Oslo friends moved to Copenhagen, wrote a K-pop closer and a choir piece, and in 2025 made the record Pitchfork ranked No. 11.

610b71d9-fa78-47d6-9073-083922e73840.name: Addison Rae
610b71d9-fa78-47d6-9073-083922e73840.label: Columbia
610b71d9-fa78-47d6-9073-083922e73840.lede: Addison Rae went from TikTok dance videos to a shelved first album, a leaked demo Charli xcx wanted a verse on, and a 2025 debut Pitchfork put at No. 12 for the year.

6ce5eca0-4ad6-49e0-a5ab-e11482d85324.name: Sudan Archives
6ce5eca0-4ad6-49e0-a5ab-e11482d85324.label: Stones Throw
6ce5eca0-4ad6-49e0-a5ab-e11482d85324.lede: Brittney Parks left a pop duo her stepfather had planned, taught herself beats on an iPad, and taught the violin to share a stage with a drum machine. Pitchfork has put her on its year-end list three times.

5c555e44-94b7-4aa3-8d21-63a935e3806e.name: Barker
5c555e44-94b7-4aa3-8d21-63a935e3806e.label: Smalltown Supersound
5c555e44-94b7-4aa3-8d21-63a935e3806e.lede: Sam Barker found a Pro-One in his school studio in 1996, booked other people's tours in Berlin for about a decade, then took the kick drum out of techno. His 2025 album Stochastic Drift landed at No. 14 on Pitchfork's year-end list.

8b22acd6-20e6-4463-a75c-c14b5cfdb666.name: Earl Sweatshirt
8b22acd6-20e6-4463-a75c-c14b5cfdb666.label: Warner Records
8b22acd6-20e6-4463-a75c-c14b5cfdb666.lede: Earl Sweatshirt starts out as a sixteen-year-old MySpace rapper in Odd Future, disappears to Samoa, comes back, and spends a decade making records that get quieter, stranger and better. The latest, a fatherhood album, is Pitchfork's No. 15 of 2025.

25f3abd9-63b5-471a-bd25-feb9672dfa11.name: Rosalía
25f3abd9-63b5-471a-bd25-feb9672dfa11.label: Columbia
25f3abd9-63b5-471a-bd25-feb9672dfa11.lede: Rosalía won the one flamenco-singing seat at a Barcelona conservatory, then spent a decade refusing to make the same record twice. The latest, Lux, is an orchestral album about saints, sung in 14 languages.

09f91305-e193-48af-92e3-252b3dd5e718.name: Water From Your Eyes
09f91305-e193-48af-92e3-252b3dd5e718.label: Matador
09f91305-e193-48af-92e3-252b3dd5e718.lede: Rachel Brown and Nate Amos started out wanting to write New Order songs. By 2024 they were opening for Interpol in front of about 160,000 people, and in 2025 they landed a record in Pitchfork's top 20.

7441014f-f8f5-494f-81db-ff166fbc078d.name: PinkPantheress
7441014f-f8f5-494f-81db-ff166fbc078d.label: Warner Records
7441014f-f8f5-494f-81db-ff166fbc078d.lede: She posted a song a day because she had nothing else to do, and four years later a mixtape with a crown on the cover landed on the year-end lists.

827cef10-eff0-4794-866e-d6b7f2ee874d.name: Titanic
827cef10-eff0-4794-866e-d6b7f2ee874d.label: Unheard of Hope
827cef10-eff0-4794-866e-d6b7f2ee874d.lede: Mabe Fratti, a Guatemalan cellist, and Héctor Tosta, a Mexico City guitarist-producer, make records the way other people renovate a house, room by room: pop in one, black metal in the next.

03d1ff41-771f-46fc-85c2-921ebb4561cf.name: Nick León
03d1ff41-771f-46fc-85c2-921ebb4561cf.label: TraTraTrax
03d1ff41-771f-46fc-85c2-921ebb4561cf.lede: A Fruity Loops kid from Fort Lauderdale sold beats to Miami rappers, burned out on the European festival circuit, and came home to make the record Pitchfork called a dembow pop album for muggy, electric nights.

f30fea51-fa9c-4067-bc49-fc43236e89ba.name: billy woods
f30fea51-fa9c-4067-bc49-fc43236e89ba.label: Backwoodz Studioz
f30fea51-fa9c-4067-bc49-fc43236e89ba.lede: billy woods, born in D.C. and raised in Zimbabwe, keeps his face out of the pictures, runs his own label, and spent two decades in New York's underground before Pitchfork ranked GOLLIWOG No. 21 of 2025.

23f02e95-84fe-44bf-a173-f30e5c18e24d.name: aya
23f02e95-84fe-44bf-a173-f30e5c18e24d.label: Hyperdub
23f02e95-84fe-44bf-a173-f30e5c18e24d.lede: A Huddersfield kid who grew up under a TV mast spent a decade making club music as LOFT, got sober, and then made hexed!, an album that treats addiction as a horror film and that Pitchfork scored 9.0.

7df4c4de-3181-4a69-bd36-9d663970cebb.name: Alex G
7df4c4de-3181-4a69-bd36-9d663970cebb.label: RCA
7df4c4de-3181-4a69-bd36-9d663970cebb.lede: Alex Giannascoli was 17 when he started putting albums on Bandcamp from Havertown, Pennsylvania. Frank Ocean emailed, Domino signed him, and in 2024 RCA did too; on Headlights, his tenth album, he still plays most of the instruments himself.

3d254f1e-7d18-431b-baeb-68e57695dfdb.name: Blood Orange
3d254f1e-7d18-431b-baeb-68e57695dfdb.label: RCA / Domino
3d254f1e-7d18-431b-baeb-68e57695dfdb.lede: Dev Hynes was 18 and screaming in Test Icicles, then a folk singer called Lightspeed Champion, then Blood Orange, writing for Solange, Carly Rae Jepsen and Blondie. In 2025 Pitchfork put his grief record Essex Honey at No. 24 of the year.

0e0d5912-4026-47ef-be1c-c876c7108dd2.name: Rochelle Jordan
0e0d5912-4026-47ef-be1c-c876c7108dd2.label: Empire
0e0d5912-4026-47ef-be1c-c876c7108dd2.lede: Rochelle Jordan posts R&B covers on YouTube, gets ten DMs from a Virginia Beach producer, loses seven years to a bad deal, and comes back with a 17-track house album that Pitchfork ranks No. 25 for 2025.

763cb144-afdb-471e-bd86-d4f5b9b58641.name: Adrianne Lenker
763cb144-afdb-471e-bd86-d4f5b9b58641.label: 4AD
763cb144-afdb-471e-bd86-d4f5b9b58641.lede: Adrianne Lenker wrote her first song at eight and made four Big Thief albums in four years. Then she set up in a woodland studio with a few friends, no drums and no screens.

12d0b276-b102-4779-ac35-6939c584d9da.name: Arooj Aftab
12d0b276-b102-4779-ac35-6939c584d9da.label: Verve
12d0b276-b102-4779-ac35-6939c584d9da.lede: Arooj Aftab's acoustic "Hallelujah" went around Lahore by file-sharing, and fifteen years on she was the first Pakistani artist to win a Grammy. Then she made a record about the night, and Elvis Costello played Wurlitzer on it.

bc6af694-5880-4770-bdf1-82d03fea43f4.name: Astrid Sonne
bc6af694-5880-4770-bdf1-82d03fea43f4.label: Escho
bc6af694-5880-4770-bdf1-82d03fea43f4.lede: Astrid Sonne left the classical track at 18, taught herself Ableton by trial and error, and years of instrumentals later sang her own songs on Great Doubt, which Pitchfork ranked No. 9 on its year-end 50.

cd689e77-dfdd-4f81-b50c-5e5a3f5e38a4.name: Bladee
cd689e77-dfdd-4f81-b50c-5e5a3f5e38a4.label: Trash Island
