cd689e77-dfdd-4f81-b50c-5e5a3f5e38a4.lede: Benjamin Reichwald wanted to be a painter, sang through Auto-Tune instead, and in 2024 left his label and put out the album Pitchfork ranked No. 8 of the year.

a7537f5b-ef6f-424e-9f4d-9b990cb8866f.name: Cindy Lee
a7537f5b-ef6f-424e-9f4d-9b990cb8866f.label: Realistik
a7537f5b-ef6f-424e-9f4d-9b990cb8866f.lede: Women fell apart mid-set in Victoria in 2010. [[Patrick Flegel]] spent the next decade making drag-pop records as Cindy Lee that almost nobody could find, then put a 32-song album on YouTube and a GeoCities-style site, and Pitchfork gave it a 9.1.

d786f59b-1836-4ddb-8393-ab753edbe984.name: Clairo
d786f59b-1836-4ddb-8393-ab753edbe984.label: Clairo Records
d786f59b-1836-4ddb-8393-ab753edbe984.lede: Claire Cottrill filmed herself lip-syncing on a laptop in thirty minutes, on a day she felt at her worst. Eight years later she was on the Coachella main stage with an album cut live to tape.

e66411bb-9429-4be3-9d53-be407d3a182c.name: DORIS
e66411bb-9429-4be3-9d53-be407d3a182c.label: Janine Records
e66411bb-9429-4be3-9d53-be407d3a182c.lede: Frank Dorrey, a Linden, New Jersey kid, built a name making surreal portraits on an iPhone, then put out a 50-song, pitched-up sample diary that Pitchfork ranked No. 16 for 2024.

1a331805-47cc-4f30-a123-94d820dbca31.name: Jessica Pratt
1a331805-47cc-4f30-a123-94d820dbca31.label: Mexican Summer
1a331805-47cc-4f30-a123-94d820dbca31.lede: Jessica Pratt recorded her first songs on analogue tape in 2007 and left them unreleased for five years. By 2024 she was closing a Chanel couture show, playing Colbert and singing on an A$AP Rocky single.

b6cfaa6e-71cf-4431-81e6-515a4b23a425.name: Jlin
b6cfaa6e-71cf-4431-81e6-515a4b23a425.label: Planet Mu
b6cfaa6e-71cf-4431-81e6-515a4b23a425.lede: Jerrilynn Patton taught herself footwork online in Gary, Indiana, kept a steel-mill job while she did it, and as Jlin ended up with Björk, Philip Glass and the Kronos Quartet on one album.

e7d4f00b-2938-4049-aa44-e69a59a7b3da.name: Ka
e7d4f00b-2938-4049-aa44-e69a59a7b3da.label: Iron Works
e7d4f00b-2938-4049-aa44-e69a59a7b3da.lede: Kaseem Ryan quit rap, spent 20 years in the FDNY, and came back in his thirties with records built on almost no drums. He sold one on the sidewalk outside a closed record store, and his last album came out two months before he died in 2024.

19301485-ac9c-4dad-885b-cd8e8c8b4184.name: Kim Gordon
19301485-ac9c-4dad-885b-cd8e8c8b4184.label: Matador
19301485-ac9c-4dad-885b-cd8e8c8b4184.lede: Kim Gordon had never played an instrument when she joined her first band at 27. She went on to co-found Sonic Youth, and at 70 she made a record on trap beats that Pitchfork ranked No. 10 for 2024.

ddefada4-c07e-43d3-9837-318805f37776.name: Mabe Fratti
ddefada4-c07e-43d3-9837-318805f37776.label: Unheard of Hope
ddefada4-c07e-43d3-9837-318805f37776.lede: Mabe Fratti learned cello in a Guatemalan church orchestra, took a three-month residency in Mexico and never really left. In 2024 Pitchfork ranked Sentir Que No Sabes No. 20 on its albums of the year.

68c261d5-48c8-4ea9-9466-9fc908dc79bb.name: Magdalena Bay
68c261d5-48c8-4ea9-9466-9fc908dc79bb.label: Mom + Pop
68c261d5-48c8-4ea9-9466-9fc908dc79bb.lede: Two Miami prog-rock kids swapped Rush for Grimes, taught themselves pop off YouTube, and ended up with a concept album about a girl whose body rejects a CD.

e160f589-dbe6-4b8f-88b5-f528ff4443b4.name: Mannequin Pussy
e160f589-dbe6-4b8f-88b5-f528ff4443b4.label: Epitaph
e160f589-dbe6-4b8f-88b5-f528ff4443b4.lede: Marisa Dabice and Athanasios Paul started Mannequin Pussy as a two-piece in Connecticut, and fourteen years later Pitchfork gave the band's fourth album an 8.8 and Best New Music.

4f52595e-652d-4894-95ea-f925234629fc.name: MJ Lenderman
4f52595e-652d-4894-95ea-f925234629fc.label: Anti-
4f52595e-652d-4894-95ea-f925234629fc.lede: MJ Lenderman scooped ice cream in Asheville, played lead guitar for Wednesday, and put out the record Pitchfork ranked No. 4 of 2024.

262cf0ce-2af2-4686-a8cc-d6b33e97336d.name: Mk.gee
262cf0ce-2af2-4686-a8cc-d6b33e97336d.label: R&R
262cf0ce-2af2-4686-a8cc-d6b33e97336d.lede: Michael Gordon grew up in Linwood, New Jersey, recording on cracked software and cheap gear, then spent years putting his guitar on other people's records. In 2024 his own debut, Two Star & the Dream Police, runs 33 minutes and gets argued over everywhere.

e5306b29-16c0-4520-bb05-6b21f041b2f0.name: Mount Eerie
e5306b29-16c0-4520-bb05-6b21f041b2f0.label: P.W. Elverum & Sun
e5306b29-16c0-4520-bb05-6b21f041b2f0.lede: Phil Elverum shut down the Microphones in 2003, took the name of the mountain above his hometown and has released almost everything since on a label he runs himself. After his wife Geneviève Castrée died in 2016, the albums he made about it became the best-known of his career.

46a4b150-be30-44b3-a337-e06a72657d33.name: Nala Sinephro
46a4b150-be30-44b3-a337-e06a72657d33.label: Warp
46a4b150-be30-44b3-a337-e06a72657d33.lede: Nala Sinephro plays pedal harp through modular synths and makes jazz that doesn't follow jazz's rules. Her second album, Endlessness, is ten pieces all called "Continuum", and Pitchfork ranked it fifth of 2024.

4173ee0d-e003-496a-98eb-a2eaa90cb3f7.name: Nilüfer Yanya
4173ee0d-e003-496a-98eb-a2eaa90cb3f7.label: Ninja Tune
4173ee0d-e003-496a-98eb-a2eaa90cb3f7.lede: Nilüfer Yanya grew up in Chelsea with a saz-playing father, put out three EPs, and opened for Adele in Hyde Park. Her third album, My Method Actor, landed at No. 13 on Pitchfork's 2024 list.

9398dc7b-c0a3-4f4c-adea-7434f1b5ea2c.name: Rafael Toral
9398dc7b-c0a3-4f4c-adea-7434f1b5ea2c.label: Drag City
9398dc7b-c0a3-4f4c-adea-7434f1b5ea2c.lede: Rafael Toral drummed in Lisbon, spent over a decade building his own electronic instruments, then picked the guitar back up and landed at No. 14 on Pitchfork's best of 2024.

43810b53-144a-4f6a-925e-66987a10b098.name: skaiwater
43810b53-144a-4f6a-925e-66987a10b098.label: Capitol
43810b53-144a-4f6a-925e-66987a10b098.lede: Tyler Brooks started on GarageBand in Nottingham at 10, posted a Jersey club loop that TikTok ran with, and moved to Los Angeles. The album that followed, #gigi, finished No. 1 on The FADER's 2024 list.

af826aa8-df24-453b-b429-21b8dc39ae6c.name: Still House Plants
af826aa8-df24-453b-b429-21b8dc39ae6c.label: Bison
af826aa8-df24-453b-b429-21b8dc39ae6c.lede: Finlay Clark, Jess Hickie-Kallenbach and David Kennedy met at the Glasgow School of Art and started playing in front of a wall of houseplants. Guitar, voice and drums, taken apart and rebuilt as they play, got them from a tenement flat to Pitchfork's Best New Music.

45425c84-9092-4e2c-b732-e1d0280b580a.name: Tyla
45425c84-9092-4e2c-b732-e1d0280b580a.label: FAX / Epic
45425c84-9092-4e2c-b732-e1d0280b580a.lede: She heard a log drum at 14, sang over one at 17, and at 21 became the first South African soloist on the Hot 100 in over 55 years, with a song about a body in motion and a dance that ends in a pour.

42321e24-42b6-4f08-b0d9-8325ee887a20.name: Waxahatchee
42321e24-42b6-4f08-b0d9-8325ee887a20.label: Anti-
42321e24-42b6-4f08-b0d9-8325ee887a20.lede: Katie Crutchfield named a cassette after a creek near her Alabama home, and twelve years later Pitchfork ranked her sixth album No. 6 of 2024.

d6d45dda-2377-4faa-947b-e071efa085c0.name: 100 gecs
d6d45dda-2377-4faa-947b-e071efa085c0.label: Dog Show / Atlantic
d6d45dda-2377-4faa-947b-e071efa085c0.lede: Two St. Louis friends swapped Logic files between Chicago and Los Angeles, and the closet-recorded album they made turned a pine tree in a Des Plaines office park into a pilgrimage site.

90cc2464-234e-4da0-b39b-576f36e633bc.name: Anohni
90cc2464-234e-4da0-b39b-576f36e633bc.label: Secretly Canadian
90cc2464-234e-4da0-b39b-576f36e633bc.lede: ANOHNI sang over cassettes in after-hours bars, named her band for a woman she met days before that woman died, and won the Mercury Prize with an album that jumped 119 places on the UK chart in a week.

f91ec397-c4be-4672-8faa-2d2983682b1c.name: Avalon Emerson
f91ec397-c4be-4672-8faa-2d2983682b1c.label: Another Dove
f91ec397-c4be-4672-8faa-2d2983682b1c.lede: Avalon Emerson wrote software by day and threw SoMa warehouse parties by night, learned to DJ at Panorama Bar, then turned up at a London pub with a cellist, a guitarist and a debut album she sang herself.

3ceeddbd-fba5-4bdb-99f7-2d028ed5afda.name: boygenius
3ceeddbd-fba5-4bdb-99f7-2d028ed5afda.label: Interscope
3ceeddbd-fba5-4bdb-99f7-2d028ed5afda.lede: Julien Baker, Phoebe Bridgers and Lucy Dacus booked a tour before they had a song and cut six in four days at Sound City. Four years later they made The Record in one month at Rick Rubin's studio, and it went No. 1 in the U.K.

d8f43dc5-4613-48ac-8c23-a62b82f8c67a.name: Caroline Polachek
d8f43dc5-4613-48ac-8c23-a62b82f8c67a.label: Perpetual Novice
d8f43dc5-4613-48ac-8c23-a62b82f8c67a.lede: A haunted-house idea in Boulder turned into a band, a Beyoncé credit and an iPod ad, and then Caroline Polachek made the album Pitchfork ranked No. 2 of 2023.

f7df5df4-4dfa-459d-972b-1ba051c15ddc.name: Fever Ray
f7df5df4-4dfa-459d-972b-1ba051c15ddc.label: Rabid Records / Mute
f7df5df4-4dfa-459d-972b-1ba051c15ddc.lede: Karin Dreijer fronted a Gothenburg guitar band, started The Knife with brother Olof, then stepped out alone in a mask as Fever Ray. In 2023 they made an album about love that Pitchfork ranked No. 8 for the year.

03a47c9d-f4d8-4445-b229-920285d7a1af.name: HiTech
03a47c9d-f4d8-4445-b229-920285d7a1af.label: FXHE Records
03a47c9d-f4d8-4445-b229-920285d7a1af.lede: Three Detroit rappers put out 15 CDs, handed one to Omar S at his storefront, and were on a Coachella stage by 2025.

6f2c949d-9540-4421-bf02-27ae27e00e33.name: Ice Spice
6f2c949d-9540-4421-bf02-27ae27e00e33.label: 10K Projects / Capitol
6f2c949d-9540-4421-bf02-27ae27e00e33.lede: Ice Spice made six songs in 13 minutes, landed at No. 32 on Pitchfork's 2023 list, and spent the rest of that year on Taylor Swift's and Nicki Minaj's records. A year earlier she was a Bronx student with a Wendy's name tag.

8ff2bf9c-d1b6-4134-ae14-b837913c3dfd.name: Jaimie Branch
8ff2bf9c-d1b6-4134-ae14-b837913c3dfd.label: International Anthem
8ff2bf9c-d1b6-4134-ae14-b837913c3dfd.lede: Jaimie Branch went to hear improvised music at Chicago's Velvet Lounge as a teenager, rebuilt her life in Brooklyn, and led Fly or Die, a quartet whose first album made NPR Music's Top 50 of 2017. Her last one, a Pitchfork Best New Album, came out a year after she died.

6ed40778-8d03-4a5c-ad35-93cf814627c9.name: Jessie Ware
6ed40778-8d03-4a5c-ad35-93cf814627c9.label: EMI / Interscope
6ed40778-8d03-4a5c-ad35-93cf814627c9.lede: Jessie Ware went from newsroom desks and backing vocals to a Mercury shortlisting, nearly quit after her third album, then built a second act out of a podcast with her mum and a disco record.

8f9f14be-6364-40da-9d82-984acdd66f27.name: Joanna Sternberg
8f9f14be-6364-40da-9d82-984acdd66f27.label: Fat Possum
8f9f14be-6364-40da-9d82-984acdd66f27.lede: Joanna Sternberg didn't write a song until their early twenties. Twelve of them got cut in six days after a pandemic on the 40th floor, and Pitchfork put the record at No. 34 for 2023.

4266bddb-2a59-445c-9b90-29f84dfffff6.name: Julie Byrne
4266bddb-2a59-445c-9b90-29f84dfffff6.label: Ghostly International
4266bddb-2a59-445c-9b90-29f84dfffff6.lede: Julie Byrne learned guitar at seventeen on her father's instrument and later patrolled Central Park as a ranger. Six years after Not Even Happiness, The Greater Wings won Pitchfork's Best New Music and landed at No. 21 on its 2023 year-end list.

0c3fe1fa-edd0-471c-b6a1-87472da86167.name: Kara Jackson
0c3fe1fa-edd0-471c-b6a1-87472da86167.label: September Recordings
0c3fe1fa-edd0-471c-b6a1-87472da86167.lede: Kara Jackson was a slam poet from Oak Park when she was named U.S. National Youth Poet Laureate. Four years later came a folk debut that asks the question most folk records dodge.

045494aa-e913-4e62-bf4e-dcc276e0075a.name: Kelela
045494aa-e913-4e62-bf4e-dcc276e0075a.label: Warp
045494aa-e913-4e62-bf4e-dcc276e0075a.lede: She quit telemarketing in 2012 with two songs recorded and gave her first mixtape away free. A decade later, a mostly Berlin-made album landed at No. 17 on Pitchfork's 50 Best Albums of 2023.

b7539c32-53e7-4908-bda3-81449c367da6.name: Lana Del Rey
b7539c32-53e7-4908-bda3-81449c367da6.label: Interscope / Polydor
b7539c32-53e7-4908-bda3-81449c367da6.lede: Elizabeth Grant made one album as Lizzy Grant and watched her label pull it, then put a self-edited webcam video online and came back as Lana Del Rey. Her ninth album, Ocean Blvd, ranked No. 11 on Pitchfork's 2023 list.

cb5704af-3ef1-485f-bb7f-e43cf40170a7.name: Laurel Halo
cb5704af-3ef1-485f-bb7f-e43cf40170a7.label: Awe
cb5704af-3ef1-485f-bb7f-e43cf40170a7.lede: Laurel Halo went from a freeform radio booth in Ann Arbor to Hyperdub, sang on her debut album, then stopped, scored runways and a documentary, and started a label called Awe. Its first release, the piano record Atlas, landed at No. 26 on Pitchfork's 2023 list.

fa58cf24-0e44-421d-8519-8bf461dcfaa5.name: Mitski
fa58cf24-0e44-421d-8519-8bf461dcfaa5.label: Dead Oceans
fa58cf24-0e44-421d-8519-8bf461dcfaa5.lede: Mitski grew up in 13 countries, studied at Purchase College and, eight albums in, writes the songs people quote back to themselves.

1b6bd9dc-c944-4937-94ec-b2276141fa36.name: Model/Actriz
1b6bd9dc-c944-4937-94ec-b2276141fa36.label: True Panther
1b6bd9dc-c944-4937-94ec-b2276141fa36.lede: Two Berklee kids found a singer at a basement show, lost him to a breakup, and got him back with a bassist who had walked runways in Milan. Dogsbody took Best New Music and a Coachella slot followed.

1395c84b-2e84-4f25-9962-f1c0d5aa31ed.name: Noname
1395c84b-2e84-4f25-9962-f1c0d5aa31ed.label: Self-released
1395c84b-2e84-4f25-9962-f1c0d5aa31ed.lede: Fatimah Warner grew up around her mother's Bronzeville bookstore, finished her first mixtape in two rented Airbnbs, built a book club that ships to prisons, and put out her second album herself in 2023.

2f8d2007-7666-45af-89d4-dec4921dce04.name: Sofia Kourtesis
2f8d2007-7666-45af-89d4-dec4921dce04.label: Ninja Tune
2f8d2007-7666-45af-89d4-dec4921dce04.lede: Sofia Kourtesis left Lima for Germany at 17 and, by her own account, rapped badly in Hamburg. Years later she made Madres while her mother was being treated for cancer, and it landed on Pitchfork's 2023 year-end list.

01d3c51b-9b98-418a-8d8e-37f6fab59d8c.name: Sufjan Stevens
01d3c51b-9b98-418a-8d8e-37f6fab59d8c.label: Asthmatic Kitty
01d3c51b-9b98-418a-8d8e-37f6fab59d8c.lede: Sufjan Stevens announced an album for every US state, made two, and spent the next two decades doing everything else, nearly all of it on Asthmatic Kitty, the label he started with his stepfather, Lowell Brams. His latest, Javelin, was Pitchfork's No. 6 record of 2023.

272989c8-5535-492d-a25c-9f58803e027f.name: SZA
272989c8-5535-492d-a25c-9f58803e027f.label: Top Dawg Entertainment / RCA
272989c8-5535-492d-a25c-9f58803e027f.lede: A marine biology dropout who built her first EP on beats she found online, then made fans wait five years for the follow-up to Ctrl. When SOS finally arrived, Pitchfork put it at No. 1 for 2023.

2d781050-032a-4a4f-b0a9-7b4bc99449e1.name: Yaeji
2d781050-032a-4a4f-b0a9-7b4bc99449e1.label: XL Recordings
2d781050-032a-4a4f-b0a9-7b4bc99449e1.lede: Kathy Yaeji Lee grew up between Queens, Atlanta and Seoul, whispered her way onto dance floors with a Drake remix, then spent a pandemic writing an album about what she wanted to hit with a sledgehammer.

31da7b06-bc30-4a1f-9f4a-c2ac1a84167f.name: yeule
31da7b06-bc30-4a1f-9f4a-c2ac1a84167f.label: Ninja Tune
31da7b06-bc30-4a1f-9f4a-c2ac1a84167f.lede: yeule took a name from a Final Fantasy character at 14, hid behind it online from Singapore, and ended up with a Best New Music score for a fuzzy album about comforting their younger self.

b675f327-4738-4af4-bb83-1adb0003f2d3.name: Yves Tumor
b675f327-4738-4af4-bb83-1adb0003f2d3.label: Warp
b675f327-4738-4af4-bb83-1adb0003f2d3.lede: Yves Tumor spent two and a half years on the road with Mykki Blanco, put out a record on Berlin's PAN, then signed to Warp and started getting compared to Prince.

859d0860-d480-4efd-970c-c05d5f1776b8.name: Beyoncé
859d0860-d480-4efd-970c-c05d5f1776b8.label: Parkwood/Columbia
859d0860-d480-4efd-970c-c05d5f1776b8.lede: Houston talent shows led to a record deal that Elektra dropped before an album came out. Beyoncé has since had eight straight No. 1 debuts, moving from soul to house to country.

99450990-b24e-4132-bb68-235f8c3e2564.name: Alvvays
99450990-b24e-4132-bb68-235f8c3e2564.label: Polyvinyl
99450990-b24e-4132-bb68-235f8c3e2564.lede: Molly Rankin wrote 'Adult Diversion' behind a smoothie shop counter, buried a snowmobile outside a PEI farmhouse, lost her demo recorder to a thief, and still ended up with Pitchfork's No. 3 album of 2022.

cb0a7ee8-69fe-409c-85ae-820e3f1e46d4.name: Special Interest
cb0a7ee8-69fe-409c-85ae-820e3f1e46d4.label: Rough Trade
cb0a7ee8-69fe-409c-85ae-820e3f1e46d4.lede: None of the four came to New Orleans for Katrina. A Casio SK1 run through cheap pedals started the sound, and by 2022 Pitchfork had Endure at No. 4 for the year.

9f81247f-7f57-42f3-a8ba-75bef554e591.name: Big Thief
9f81247f-7f57-42f3-a8ba-75bef554e591.label: 4AD
9f81247f-7f57-42f3-a8ba-75bef554e591.lede: Two Berklee alumni and two friends lived on the road for years, then recorded an 80-minute double album in five studios during lockdown. Pitchfork ranked it No. 7 of 2022.

245f7a1a-b799-40f1-a11a-6b379dbe0fa1.name: Lucrecia Dalt
245f7a1a-b799-40f1-a11a-6b379dbe0fa1.label: RVNG Intl.
245f7a1a-b799-40f1-a11a-6b379dbe0fa1.lede: Lucrecia Dalt started as a Colombian soil engineer with a side hobby in electronics and ended up a Berlin voice artist. In 2022 she made a Spanish-language bolero record about an alien, and Pitchfork ranked it No. 8 of the year.

f55859c9-0642-47dc-8c68-4aa2db484b23.name: Yaya Bey
f55859c9-0642-47dc-8c68-4aa2db484b23.label: Big Dada
f55859c9-0642-47dc-8c68-4aa2db484b23.lede: Her father told her not to sing. Yaya Bey put out three albums on Elevated anyway, signed to Big Dada, and ended 2022 at No. 9 on Pitchfork's year-end list.

c8b03190-306c-4120-bb0b-6f2ebfc06ea9.name: The Weeknd
c8b03190-306c-4120-bb0b-6f2ebfc06ea9.label: XO/Republic
c8b03190-306c-4120-bb0b-6f2ebfc06ea9.lede: He posted three songs under a username with no face, folded shirts at American Apparel, and ended up with a song that held a Hot 100 top-ten spot for a full year.

87c5dedd-371d-4a53-9f7f-80522fb7f3cb.name: Björk
87c5dedd-371d-4a53-9f7f-80522fb7f3cb.label: One Little Independent
87c5dedd-371d-4a53-9f7f-80522fb7f3cb.lede: She cut an LP at eleven, opened for Crass at seventeen, started Iceland's biggest rock band at twenty, and has spent every album since refusing to make the last one again.

381086ea-f511-4aba-bdf9-71c753dc5077.name: Kendrick Lamar
381086ea-f511-4aba-bdf9-71c753dc5077.label: pgLang / Top Dawg / Aftermath / Interscope
381086ea-f511-4aba-bdf9-71c753dc5077.lede: A stuttering kid from Compton freestyled for two hours to get signed, then won a Pulitzer, played a Super Bowl halftime show and made a double album that opens in a therapist's chair.

7230b2f8-96da-4242-8d57-2a8c1c3d71e4.name: Jockstrap
7230b2f8-96da-4242-8d57-2a8c1c3d71e4.label: Rough Trade
7230b2f8-96da-4242-8d57-2a8c1c3d71e4.lede: Georgia Ellery brought poems and a jazz violin; Taylor Skye brought a laptop and a habit of not leaving a sound alone. They picked the name Jockstrap for shock value, then went on to a 21-piece student string section, a Mercury Prize shortlist and one laptop that nearly left a restaurant without them.

59476fae-d0c9-4ebd-b03c-c38b19b30dff.name: Makaya McCraven
59476fae-d0c9-4ebd-b03c-c38b19b30dff.label: International Anthem
59476fae-d0c9-4ebd-b03c-c38b19b30dff.lede: McCraven records his band live, then takes the tapes home and cuts them up the way a hip-hop producer cuts samples. In These Times took seven years of that.

f2393e49-b791-46da-a6d7-1e9e60743405.name: Cate Le Bon
f2393e49-b791-46da-a6d7-1e9e60743405.label: Mexican Summer
f2393e49-b791-46da-a6d7-1e9e60743405.lede: Cate Le Bon grew up on a Welsh farm, sang on a Gruff Rhys tour, built herself a chair, and now gets the call from Wilco, Deerhunter and St. Vincent when they want to sound less like themselves.

9055fca5-69bc-4d47-b569-ab2012a19565.name: The Smile
9055fca5-69bc-4d47-b569-ab2012a19565.label: XL
9055fca5-69bc-4d47-b569-ab2012a19565.lede: Thom Yorke and Jonny Greenwood of Radiohead, plus Tom Skinner of Sons of Kemet, turned up on a Glastonbury livestream in May 2021 as a band nobody knew existed. Their first album got Pitchfork's 8.6 and Best New Music.

602d121e-b374-405d-9d06-164be173eddd.name: Charlotte Adigéry & Bolis Pupul
602d121e-b374-405d-9d06-164be173eddd.label: DEEWEE
602d121e-b374-405d-9d06-164be173eddd.lede: Charlotte Adigéry and Bolis Pupul knew each other from around Ghent for years before Soulwax's Dewaele brothers put them in a room together. A week later they had an EP's worth of songs, and three records on they had an album about microaggressions you can dance to.

214d84a5-e9e5-4432-af95-8c84da7ba4c0.name: Beth Orton
214d84a5-e9e5-4432-af95-8c84da7ba4c0.label: Partisan
214d84a5-e9e5-4432-af95-8c84da7ba4c0.lede: A drama-school kid from Norfolk made a record that only came out in Japan, sang on three Chemical Brothers tracks, and spent years being filed under folktronica. Then she bought a £300 piano in Camden Market and made Weather Alive, the album Pitchfork called the best work of her career.

1e4e9db7-5068-4a9c-bdd0-5777e47172c8.name: FKA twigs
1e4e9db7-5068-4a9c-bdd0-5777e47172c8.label: Young/Atlantic
1e4e9db7-5068-4a9c-bdd0-5777e47172c8.lede: Tahliah Barnett spent her early twenties dancing behind Jessie J and Kylie Minogue, then released a video of her own face that 16 million people watched. Years later she won a Grammy for a techno-leaning record made after she moved to Prague.

859216c4-5d01-479b-b6c3-e20cc591a86a.name: Daphni
859216c4-5d01-479b-b6c3-e20cc591a86a.label: Jiaolong
859216c4-5d01-479b-b6c3-e20cc591a86a.lede: Dan Snaith finished a maths PhD, won a Polaris Prize and started a label so his club tracks had somewhere to go. Daphni is the dancefloor side of Caribou, who was Manitoba until a punk singer threatened to sue.

c4ff10e0-ae5a-467d-a409-6e0b4bf241eb.name: Perfume Genius
c4ff10e0-ae5a-467d-a409-6e0b4bf241eb.label: Matador
c4ff10e0-ae5a-467d-a409-6e0b4bf241eb.lede: Mike Hadreas left a Seattle-area high school in his senior year and put piano songs on Myspace. Matador put out the record, he played Letterman, and a dance score with a saxophonist and a string arranger became his sixth album.

9c12ec84-c547-45dc-a198-7b9dd9b2b0c7.name: Florist
9c12ec84-c547-45dc-a198-7b9dd9b2b0c7.label: Double Double Whammy
9c12ec84-c547-45dc-a198-7b9dd9b2b0c7.lede: Florist recorded one album on a screened-in porch with birdsong on tape, and Emily Sprague made another by herself in Los Angeles under the same name.

397832c9-bd43-4023-9f54-05c4d2ef1d56.name: Rachika Nayar
397832c9-bd43-4023-9f54-05c4d2ef1d56.label: NNA Tapes
397832c9-bd43-4023-9f54-05c4d2ef1d56.lede: Rachika Nayar rescored an anime as Rachika S, spent four years on a debut of looped guitar, then put a trance kick drum under her second record and landed at No. 29 on Pitchfork's 2022 year-end list.

b539e453-c4fe-47e3-8a07-8517eac74429.name: Hikaru Utada
b539e453-c4fe-47e3-8a07-8517eac74429.label: Epic Records Japan
b539e453-c4fe-47e3-8a07-8517eac74429.lede: At thirteen she cut an R&B record that went nowhere. At sixteen she made the best-selling album in Japanese history. Then she took on America, walked away, and came back with songs about her mother and a video game.

94c64122-dbd4-4927-b2fa-f204b0b4b0c2.name: Ravyn Lenae
94c64122-dbd4-4927-b2fa-f204b0b4b0c2.label: Atlantic
94c64122-dbd4-4927-b2fa-f204b0b4b0c2.lede: She paid $300 for her first studio session as a high school sophomore, signed to Atlantic at 16, and then made everyone wait until she was 23 for the album.

5b6ebfe0-f72b-4902-bba9-74c8af0f1af0.name: The 1975
5b6ebfe0-f72b-4902-bba9-74c8af0f1af0.label: Dirty Hit
5b6ebfe0-f72b-4902-bba9-74c8af0f1af0.lede: Four school friends from Wilmslow went through a run of band names, signed to a label for £20, and kept making the records they wanted: long ones, strange ones, and in 2022 a short, plain one that Pitchfork ranked No. 33 of the year.

175a1b69-7a19-4881-b1ca-fe6b84ff3a2d.name: Mavi
175a1b69-7a19-4881-b1ca-fe6b84ff3a2d.label: Mavi 4 Mayor Music
175a1b69-7a19-4881-b1ca-fe6b84ff3a2d.lede: Omavi Minder starts rapping at 14 in Charlotte, makes a debut at Howard that Earl Sweatshirt co-signs, then watches a finished second album die in sample clearance. The record he makes after that, about grief, lands at No. 34 on Pitchfork's 2022 list.

d10d6441-dcc1-4202-93bf-0c0acf72913a.name: Soul Glo
d10d6441-dcc1-4202-93bf-0c0acf72913a.label: Epitaph
d10d6441-dcc1-4202-93bf-0c0acf72913a.lede: Soul Glo started in Philadelphia for kids who fit neither the city's punk shows nor its hardcore ones. Now the band has a Pitchfork 8.5, a Coachella set and a bass slot that keeps changing hands.

365b5b7f-e9e5-4054-892b-2322e9519efe.name: Dungbeetle
365b5b7f-e9e5-4054-892b-2322e9519efe.label: Widesound
365b5b7f-e9e5-4054-892b-2322e9519efe.lede: Two Brown graduates started a band in Providence in the summer of 1990 and took it to the Lower East Side, where their singer wore a cape, called himself Sam Shit and never once winked. They left one 7-inch and a soundtrack song, then played again exactly once, in 2014.

c71fe634-2eab-4e3d-8b1c-473374b64301.name: The Grace Period
c71fe634-2eab-4e3d-8b1c-473374b64301.label: Audio Dregs
c71fe634-2eab-4e3d-8b1c-473374b64301.lede: Chris Ott was a Boston drummer and a Pitchfork critic, and the Grace Period was the loop music he made, from an Audio Dregs cassette in the '90s to zip files on a blog.

9bfdd332-bfe5-4333-bb59-0882b5253b5c.name: The Capital Suite
9bfdd332-bfe5-4333-bb59-0882b5253b5c.label: Old Colony Recordings
9bfdd332-bfe5-4333-bb59-0882b5253b5c.lede: Four Skidmore students from three class years made one album, Bekampa Tramset, at a studio down an Amherst dirt road. Twenty-four years later a Cape Cod label put it back out.

b0d6108a-3dd5-479d-b518-803f54b3ba45.name: 1 Mile North
b0d6108a-3dd5-479d-b518-803f54b3ba45.label: Ba Da Bing!
b0d6108a-3dd5-479d-b518-803f54b3ba45.lede: Jon Hills made the first 1 Mile North album with the natural reverb of the dilapidated Brooklyn sweater factory he lived in. The second got a 9.0 from Pitchfork; then came ten years off and three more albums, made on his own.

ms-creepy-woods.name: Creepy Woods
ms-creepy-woods.label: Endless Records
ms-creepy-woods.lede: Three Skidmore sophomores debuted at a benefit for their own zine in November 1994, and within five months a student critic named Chris Ott was hearing Slint in them. Ott also played drums in the band. They left a 7-inch, a few compilation tracks and a demo tape.

9a58fda3-f4ed-4080-a3a5-f457aac9fcdd.name: Joy Division
9a58fda3-f4ed-4080-a3a5-f457aac9fcdd.label: Factory Records
9a58fda3-f4ed-4080-a3a5-f457aac9fcdd.lede: Four lads from Salford and Macclesfield saw the Sex Pistols, bought instruments, and in under three years made two albums that Factory Records was built on. Then their singer died the night before their first American tour, and the other three kept going under a new name.

f1106b17-dcbb-45f6-b938-199ccfab50cc.name: New Order
f1106b17-dcbb-45f6-b938-199ccfab50cc.label: Factory Records
f1106b17-dcbb-45f6-b938-199ccfab50cc.lede: Three survivors of Joy Division learned to sing, play synths and program drum machines in public, then made the best-selling 12-inch single ever and spent the money on a nightclub. Thirty years later they were in court over the name.

aaddb5e3-f8a5-4a9d-8674-f885112ecf0e.name: The Durutti Column
aaddb5e3-f8a5-4a9d-8674-f885112ecf0e.label: Factory Records
aaddb5e3-f8a5-4a9d-8674-f885112ecf0e.lede: Tony Wilson built a punk band around a guitarist from Manchester, the punks left, and Vini Reilly stayed on Factory for the label's whole life, playing guitar that sounded like nothing else on it.

73577e86-4da8-4d76-949d-34c757e053be.name: A Certain Ratio
73577e86-4da8-4d76-949d-34c757e053be.label: Factory Records
73577e86-4da8-4d76-949d-34c757e053be.lede: A Certain Ratio gave Factory its first single by a lone band, played funk in army-surplus shorts, cut a cover for £50 and once had Madonna as the opening act. Kerr, Moscrop and Johnson are still at it.

01f4fb92-6bf0-4de5-83dc-3fe194e763bf.name: Happy Mondays
01f4fb92-6bf0-4de5-83dc-3fe194e763bf.label: Factory Records
01f4fb92-6bf0-4de5-83dc-3fe194e763bf.lede: Six lads from Salford came last in a battle of the bands at the Haçienda, made a platinum record with Bez dancing out front, then went £230,000 over budget in Barbados the year Factory went under.

82e26f64-813d-4b22-a442-44d182f7f9eb.name: Section 25
82e26f64-813d-4b22-a442-44d182f7f9eb.label: Factory Records
82e26f64-813d-4b22-a442-44d182f7f9eb.lede: Ian Curtis produced their first single, Peter Saville wrapped their first album in waxed card, and Bernard Sumner helped them make "Looking from a Hilltop," the Blackpool electro record that New York clubs picked up.

c27b14ec-2d19-4fe2-b7dc-06bdaadfedc2.name: Quando Quango
c27b14ec-2d19-4fe2-b7dc-06bdaadfedc2.label: Factory Records
c27b14ec-2d19-4fe2-b7dc-06bdaadfedc2.lede: A Haçienda booker and a Dutch synth player made a handful of Factory twelve-inches that Larry Levan played at the Paradise Garage, and that a Chicago teenager heard before house music had a name.

3cdb360e-d0a2-459f-92f6-f0f28e62127d.name: Electronic
3cdb360e-d0a2-459f-92f6-f0f28e62127d.label: Factory Records
3cdb360e-d0a2-459f-92f6-f0f28e62127d.lede: New Order's singer and the Smiths' guitarist meant to put out anonymous white labels; instead they gave a collapsing Factory one of its last hit albums and kept going, on and off, for a decade.

a2accb58-6099-4cb5-a3c8-f6332f364db5.name: James
a2accb58-6099-4cb5-a3c8-f6332f364db5.label: Factory Records
a2accb58-6099-4cb5-a3c8-f6332f364db5.lede: James turned down a Factory album, toured with the Smiths, lived on T-shirt money for years, and had to wait 42 years for a No. 1 studio album.

555ac13e-6428-4a1a-8284-5c18d4e29330.name: Biting Tongues
555ac13e-6428-4a1a-8284-5c18d4e29330.label: Factory Records
555ac13e-6428-4a1a-8284-5c18d4e29330.lede: Biting Tongues started as live music for a silent film at Tony Wilson's Factory club, never played the same set twice, and ended in the same studio sessions that gave birth to 808 State.

3420e6bc-8551-4c6c-86ca-c13a3115edd3.name: Crispy Ambulance
3420e6bc-8551-4c6c-86ca-c13a3115edd3.label: Factory Records
3420e6bc-8551-4c6c-86ca-c13a3115edd3.lede: Four South Manchester teenagers who started out covering Hawkwind ended up with Rob Gretton in their corner, Martin Hannett at the desk, and their singer fronting Joy Division for one chaotic night in Bury.

e1033f2d-04db-4fd8-827a-fbb2ef07a11d.name: Stockholm Monsters
e1033f2d-04db-4fd8-827a-fbb2ef07a11d.label: Factory Records
e1033f2d-04db-4fd8-827a-fbb2ef07a11d.lede: Peter Hook produced nearly everything they made, the Burnage teenagers who'd turn into Oasis grew up watching them, and Stockholm Monsters were gone two years before Madchester arrived.

c2314623-e863-4fde-af8c-d6e00fec5f2c.name: The Wake
c2314623-e863-4fde-af8c-d6e00fec5f2c.label: Factory Records
c2314623-e863-4fde-af8c-d6e00fec5f2c.lede: Caesar walked out of Altered Images just before the hits, sent a Glasgow single to Rob Gretton, and spent the next six years on Factory opening for New Order, with Bobby Gillespie on bass for the first stretch.

ffd81d6b-fe65-44a9-be51-a1c4f6285df0.name: Kalima
ffd81d6b-fe65-44a9-be51-a1c4f6285df0.label: Factory Records
ffd81d6b-fe65-44a9-be51-a1c4f6285df0.lede: Six Manchester teenagers rehearsed next to Joy Division as Swamp Children, borrowed most of A Certain Ratio, renamed themselves after an Elvin Jones tune and ended up as regulars at Gilles Peterson's Sunday sessions.

68142098-e3b3-4f76-a8cc-8898713fcf58.name: Minny Pops
68142098-e3b3-4f76-a8cc-8898713fcf58.label: Factory Records
68142098-e3b3-4f76-a8cc-8898713fcf58.lede: A very tall Amsterdammer named his band after a Korg drum box, planned three gigs and an EP, and instead got signed in a Joy Division dressing room and became the first Dutch band to record a Peel session.

fa291018-ac66-454f-a42b-8fbcfb24d0b3.name: Revenge
fa291018-ac66-454f-a42b-8fbcfb24d0b3.label: Factory Records
fa291018-ac66-454f-a42b-8fbcfb24d0b3.lede: When New Order stalled in 1989, Peter Hook went to his own studio in Rochdale, took the lead vocal and made a dance-rock record with a glamour photographer's shot on the sleeve.

4ef07b86-b2a2-4ab1-9d10-bf86a397e24e.name: Northside
4ef07b86-b2a2-4ab1-9d10-bf86a397e24e.label: Factory Records
4ef07b86-b2a2-4ab1-9d10-bf86a397e24e.lede: Four lads from Blackley and Moston sold out their first gig by word of mouth, got signed by Tony Wilson from the back of the room, and saw their first single banned by the BBC.

8bbbbdb3-544d-447a-b22c-327550e157b3.name: The Names
8bbbbdb3-544d-447a-b22c-327550e157b3.label: Factory Records
8bbbbdb3-544d-447a-b22c-327550e157b3.lede: A band of Brussels students handed Joy Division's manager a single at a gig, shook hands with Tony Wilson on a deal, and made their records with Martin Hannett, a toy xylophone included.

ff59a833-6f7e-48c6-9048-3097943c81d0.name: The Railway Children
ff59a833-6f7e-48c6-9048-3097943c81d0.label: Factory Records
ff59a833-6f7e-48c6-9048-3097943c81d0.lede: Four Wigan teenagers made a Factory record, topped the indie chart, signed to Virgin and had an American radio No. 1. Then EMI bought Virgin.

ad289e3d-ad4d-4f5d-922c-b49bdb436c03.name: 52nd Street
ad289e3d-ad4d-4f5d-922c-b49bdb436c03.label: Factory Records
ad289e3d-ad4d-4f5d-922c-b49bdb436c03.lede: A Manchester jazz-funk band got a New Order production, a Jellybean remix and a New York club hit out of Factory, then walked out on the label and took an R&B single to No. 8 in America.

97e4323f-b28a-4742-a7b9-d8d21ff3d8ba.name: Cath Carroll
97e4323f-b28a-4742-a7b9-d8d21ff3d8ba.label: Factory Records
97e4323f-b28a-4742-a7b9-d8d21ff3d8ba.lede: A Manchester fanzine editor turned NME writer turned Factory singer spent two years and four studios on one album, recorded in Sheffield, São Paulo, London and Chicago, then moved to Chicago for good.

0950961b-75e3-4c1b-a506-48231d40bdef.name: The Wendys
0950961b-75e3-4c1b-a506-48231d40bdef.label: Factory Records
0950961b-75e3-4c1b-a506-48231d40bdef.lede: Four engineering graduates from Edinburgh supported the Happy Mondays, got a Factory deal at a Factory party, and made one Ian Broudie album before the label went under around them.

8ca01f46-53ac-4af2-8516-55a909c0905e.name: My Bloody Valentine
8ca01f46-53ac-4af2-8516-55a909c0905e.label: Creation Records
8ca01f46-53ac-4af2-8516-55a909c0905e.lede: Two Dublin teenagers who met at a karate tournament spent a decade finding their sound, then took Creation through two and a half years and nineteen studios to make Loveless. The next album took another twenty-two.

e938a15c-b17e-4e7a-9f68-ff0d536cab44.name: The Jesus and Mary Chain
e938a15c-b17e-4e7a-9f68-ff0d536cab44.label: Creation Records
e938a15c-b17e-4e7a-9f68-ff0d536cab44.lede: Two brothers from East Kilbride spent their dad's redundancy money on a four-track, played twenty-minute sets with their backs to the crowd, and gave Creation its first hit. They split on a Los Angeles stage in 1998 and came back nine years later at Coachella.

55704c38-224f-4b75-b29f-d43653f8bc9a.name: Primal Scream
55704c38-224f-4b75-b29f-d43653f8bc9a.label: Creation Records
55704c38-224f-4b75-b29f-d43653f8bc9a.lede: Bobby Gillespie quit the drum stool in the Jesus and Mary Chain to keep a jangly Glasgow band going, then handed one of its songs to a rave DJ who was told to destroy it. Four decades on, the band is still on stage, still picking fights.

6999f790-25f4-44a3-b745-1e3e01fde0f5.name: Felt
6999f790-25f4-44a3-b745-1e3e01fde0f5.label: Creation Records
6999f790-25f4-44a3-b745-1e3e01fde0f5.lede: Lawrence decided Felt would make ten albums and ten singles in ten years, went through guitarists and bassists on the way, and ended the band on schedule in 1989.

3f575ecd-627d-4f08-a89f-abd46d469c7e.name: Ride
3f575ecd-627d-4f08-a89f-abd46d469c7e.label: Creation Records
3f575ecd-627d-4f08-a89f-abd46d469c7e.lede: Four Oxford art students were signed to Creation within a year of their first gig and were 18 to 20 when they made Nowhere. Six years later the two songwriters wouldn't share a side of a record.

a16371b9-7d36-497a-a9d4-42b0a0440c5e.name: Slowdive
a16371b9-7d36-497a-a9d4-42b0a0440c5e.label: Creation Records
a16371b9-7d36-497a-a9d4-42b0a0440c5e.lede: Five Reading teenagers signed to Creation, got told by the British music press that they were finished, got dropped a week after their third album, and came back twenty years later to bigger crowds than they'd ever had.

39ab1aed-75e0-4140-bd47-540276886b60.name: Oasis
39ab1aed-75e0-4140-bd47-540276886b60.label: Creation Records
39ab1aed-75e0-4140-bd47-540276886b60.lede: A Burnage band that had to blag its way onto a Glasgow bill ended up as the biggest thing Creation Records ever had, sold out Knebworth twice over, split in a Paris dressing-room fight, and came back sixteen years later to stadiums full of people who weren't born the first time.

c5f5dc27-3059-49c0-ae45-5009a01bb9ec.name: Super Furry Animals
c5f5dc27-3059-49c0-ae45-5009a01bb9ec.label: Creation Records
c5f5dc27-3059-49c0-ae45-5009a01bb9ec.lede: Five Welshmen who started out playing techno with a Hollywood actor on vocals, put a drug smuggler on their first album cover, drove a blue tank to festivals, and made the biggest-selling Welsh-language album there is.

cbaf677b-4f80-4663-8c2c-9197ec9d214a.name: The House of Love
cbaf677b-4f80-4663-8c2c-9197ec9d214a.label: Creation Records
cbaf677b-4f80-4663-8c2c-9197ec9d214a.lede: Guy Chadwick built a band out of a Melody Maker ad and gave Creation an indie No. 1 with 'Christine'. Then came a major label, four producers and Terry Bickers setting fire to the band's money in the tour van.

1b5189d8-28fd-4c97-a04a-37c49b1ccfa6.name: The Boo Radleys
1b5189d8-28fd-4c97-a04a-37c49b1ccfa6.label: Creation Records
1b5189d8-28fd-4c97-a04a-37c49b1ccfa6.lede: A band from Wallasey named after a recluse in a novel went from shoegaze to Giant Steps, then to a No. 1 album led by a song Martin Carr wrote after a night on acid.

fa6c7999-ff65-486b-9e18-bcb59d6db2f0.name: Swervedriver
fa6c7999-ff65-486b-9e18-bcb59d6db2f0.label: Creation Records
fa6c7999-ff65-486b-9e18-bcb59d6db2f0.lede: Two Oxford schoolmates raised near a car plant put muscle-car riffs under shoegaze noise, then lost a drummer to a sandwich run at the Canadian border and their best-reviewed album to a label that dropped them a week after release.

e3347fbd-2595-480e-926d-278566debf9d.name: Sugar
e3347fbd-2595-480e-926d-278566debf9d.label: Creation Records
e3347fbd-2595-480e-926d-278566debf9d.lede: Bob Mould was done with Virgin and wanted a band again. He built one in Athens, Georgia, named it after a sugar packet at a Waffle House, and made the NME's album of the year before the band was a year old.

4fd4170a-f958-4666-87f2-f0f168b20aed.name: Biff Bang Pow!
4fd4170a-f958-4666-87f2-f0f168b20aed.label: Creation Records
4fd4170a-f958-4666-87f2-f0f168b20aed.lede: Alan McGee's label gave the world the Jesus and Mary Chain, My Bloody Valentine and Oasis. It also gave his own band half a dozen albums, most of them cut in a few days, with two of the label's co-founders in the line-up.

9d6108ad-dbc2-4bf1-a746-edc1044d2749.name: The Pastels
9d6108ad-dbc2-4bf1-a746-edc1044d2749.label: Creation Records
9d6108ad-dbc2-4bf1-a746-edc1044d2749.lede: Stephen McRobbie started the Pastels in Glasgow in 1981, cut three of Creation's first singles, and never moved the band out of Glasgow.

eec6108a-240e-4dc2-89d7-a6e1c3ff14e4.name: The Loft
eec6108a-240e-4dc2-89d7-a6e1c3ff14e4.label: Creation Records
eec6108a-240e-4dc2-89d7-a6e1c3ff14e4.lede: Alan McGee heard 'Why Does the Rain' at his own club and wanted it as a single. Two Creation releases later the Loft broke up mid-set at the Hammersmith Palais, and it took them forty years to make an album.

8bd0e8b7-081a-4b32-b855-b38134074b35.name: The Weather Prophets
8bd0e8b7-081a-4b32-b855-b38134074b35.label: Creation Records
8bd0e8b7-081a-4b32-b855-b38134074b35.lede: Pete Astor went from the Loft's on-stage split straight into a new band, with Alan McGee briefly on bass. Then McGee put them on his new Warners imprint in the same month Warners released Prince.

c3552faf-9c1c-46ba-af13-653fe2fdcf9c.name: The Jasmine Minks
c3552faf-9c1c-46ba-af13-653fe2fdcf9c.label: Creation Records
c3552faf-9c1c-46ba-af13-653fe2fdcf9c.lede: An Aberdeen band mailed a demo to Melody Maker and ended up as Creation single No. 4, recorded for £50. McGee then sent them busking across London, eight gigs in a day, and signed them again seventeen years later.

e304fa8b-8de2-4089-b43b-bd24ca40800f.name: The Telescopes
e304fa8b-8de2-4089-b43b-bd24ca40800f.label: Creation
e304fa8b-8de2-4089-b43b-bd24ca40800f.lede: Stephen Lawrie started the Telescopes in Burton upon Trent as a feedback machine, turned it into something gentler on Creation, and has kept the name going under shifting line-ups ever since.

869f504d-2119-466b-8a3c-ff44cd8abcd0.name: The Jazz Butcher
869f504d-2119-466b-8a3c-ff44cd8abcd0.label: Creation
869f504d-2119-466b-8a3c-ff44cd8abcd0.lede: Pat Fish started the Jazz Butcher as a one-night joke at his Oxford college in 1982, then kept it going through a fistfight with his co-founder, a Bauhaus rhythm section and the Oasis years at Creation, until his death in 2021.

ff9c106f-e342-4543-a376-776e08121f69.name: Momus
ff9c106f-e342-4543-a376-776e08121f69.label: Creation
ff9c106f-e342-4543-a376-776e08121f69.lede: Nick Currie named himself after the Greek god of mockery, made five albums of clever, filthy synth-pop for Creation, got sued by a tyre company and a synthesizer pioneer, and wrote the line about everyone being famous for fifteen people.

dadd10f1-9db4-4a35-b939-9469029deab5.name: Velvet Crush
dadd10f1-9db4-4a35-b939-9469029deab5.label: Creation Records
dadd10f1-9db4-4a35-b939-9469029deab5.lede: Ric Menck and Paul Chastain left Chicago for Providence, cut their first album on Matthew Sweet's home eight-track, and got it released in Britain by Creation.

3a369807-6de5-42ea-bbaa-37524ad6989c.name: BMX Bandits
3a369807-6de5-42ea-bbaa-37524ad6989c.label: Creation Records
3a369807-6de5-42ea-bbaa-37524ad6989c.lede: Duglas T. Stewart named his Bellshill band thinking it would split in a week. Forty years on he's still the only constant, and half of Glasgow's guitar pop has passed through.

87788c91-a97e-40a8-860b-3d9a3956af5e.name: Hurricane #1
87788c91-a97e-40a8-860b-3d9a3956af5e.label: Creation Records
87788c91-a97e-40a8-860b-3d9a3956af5e.lede: Andy Bell wrote the songs after Ride, Alex Lowe sang them, and Creation got two albums before Bell left to play bass in Oasis. Fifteen years later, Alan McGee talked Lowe into bringing it back.

4023f80b-9693-424e-888f-411031fdda66.name: 3 Colours Red
4023f80b-9693-424e-888f-411031fdda66.label: Creation Records
4023f80b-9693-424e-888f-411031fdda66.lede: Alan McGee called them the second best band in Britain, and in three years they had two Top 20 albums, a No. 11 single and a US tour with Aerosmith. Then they announced the split and played out the summer at Reading and Leeds.

a174af65-40ee-4a04-8efd-0e9538205af8.name: 18 Wheeler
a174af65-40ee-4a04-8efd-0e9538205af8.label: Creation Records
a174af65-40ee-4a04-8efd-0e9538205af8.lede: Oasis got signed on 18 Wheeler's bill at King Tut's. 18 Wheeler went on to make three albums for the same label, the last with a Sex Pistol on bass.

000fc734-b7e1-4a01-92d1-f544261b43f5.name: Cocteau Twins
000fc734-b7e1-4a01-92d1-f544261b43f5.label: 4AD
000fc734-b7e1-4a01-92d1-f544261b43f5.lede: A guitarist with a box of effects pedals and a singer who wouldn't sing words people could make out left a refinery town in Scotland and gave 4AD its sound for the next decade.

b6b2bb8d-54a9-491f-9607-7b546023b433.name: Pixies
b6b2bb8d-54a9-491f-9607-7b546023b433.label: 4AD
b6b2bb8d-54a9-491f-9607-7b546023b433.lede: Black Francis wanted a bass player who liked Hüsker Dü and Peter, Paul and Mary, and Kim Deal answered the ad without owning a bass. Five records later he ended the band on the radio, and since 2004 they've been back for twice as long as they were gone.

ccda046a-2674-4f7d-97e6-f23d6c156432.name: Dead Can Dance
ccda046a-2674-4f7d-97e6-f23d6c156432.label: 4AD
ccda046a-2674-4f7d-97e6-f23d6c156432.lede: Two Melbourne post-punks moved to London, dropped the guitars for cello, hurdy-gurdy and a Chinese hammered dulcimer, and became the biggest-selling act on 4AD. Lisa Gerrard sang in a language she made up; Brendan Perry built a studio in an Irish church.

0688add2-c282-4ee2-ba61-223ffdb3c201.name: Bauhaus
0688add2-c282-4ee2-ba61-223ffdb3c201.label: 4AD
0688add2-c282-4ee2-ba61-223ffdb3c201.lede: Four art-school and factory kids from Northampton cut a nine-minute single about a dead horror actor six weeks after they started, and goth historians still call it the genre's first record. They quit at the top in 1983, then kept coming back, once upside down.

cbcd4d49-e892-4fc6-a313-35f275a153d2.name: The Birthday Party
cbcd4d49-e892-4fc6-a313-35f275a153d2.label: 4AD
cbcd4d49-e892-4fc6-a313-35f275a153d2.lede: Five Caulfield Grammar boys took a Melbourne ballroom residency to London, then Berlin, and made noise so ugly and exact that the band couldn't survive it. What walked out of the wreckage was Nick Cave and the Bad Seeds.

60ef8ddb-7676-4056-a357-9a8c228d03a6.name: This Mortal Coil
60ef8ddb-7676-4056-a357-9a8c228d03a6.label: 4AD
60ef8ddb-7676-4056-a357-9a8c228d03a6.lede: Ivo Watts-Russell ran 4AD and wanted to hear his favorite songs played by his own artists, so he made a band with no fixed members and three albums. One Tim Buckley cover outlived all of it.

b1b9d5cc-7975-43e5-960e-670583da7bc8.name: Throwing Muses
b1b9d5cc-7975-43e5-960e-670583da7bc8.label: 4AD
b1b9d5cc-7975-43e5-960e-670583da7bc8.lede: Two step-sisters from Newport, Rhode Island started a band as high school freshmen and became the first Americans on 4AD. Kristin Hersh is still making Muses records forty-odd years later.

667e856e-f3a7-42e9-8244-95422ef31321.name: The Breeders
667e856e-f3a7-42e9-8244-95422ef31321.label: 4AD
667e856e-f3a7-42e9-8244-95422ef31321.lede: Kim Deal started a side project on a Pixies tour, handed lead guitar to a twin sister who had never played one, and wrote Cannonball. Thirty years on, the Last Splash four were opening for Olivia Rodrigo at Madison Square Garden.

6746c384-b67b-4eb7-a986-e2b6f4140cee.name: Colourbox
6746c384-b67b-4eb7-a986-e2b6f4140cee.label: 4AD
6746c384-b67b-4eb7-a986-e2b6f4140cee.lede: Two brothers from London made one album of reggae, soul covers and sample-splattered noise for 4AD, then lent their drum machines to Pump Up the Volume, a UK No. 1 that started a sampling lawsuit before it reached the top.

06e59c30-5e21-4318-96e8-7a5f7e309af1.name: Red House Painters
06e59c30-5e21-4318-96e8-7a5f7e309af1.label: 4AD
06e59c30-5e21-4318-96e8-7a5f7e309af1.lede: Mark Kozelek's band got signed off a 90-minute demo tape, made four long, slow records for 4AD, then left the label and got caught in Island's merger. Its final album sat on a shelf for three years before Kozelek bought it back.

99524243-dc2e-4bf3-82c0-72395391d21f.name: Scott Walker
99524243-dc2e-4bf3-82c0-72395391d21f.label: 4AD
99524243-dc2e-4bf3-82c0-72395391d21f.lede: Noel Scott Engel had a teen-idol fan club bigger than the Beatles' at 23, spent a decade singing other people's songs to get out of contracts, and finished on 4AD with a percussionist punching a side of pork.

697801d1-68b2-4413-a7e4-0ef507d21cc1.name: Lush
697801d1-68b2-4413-a7e4-0ef507d21cc1.label: 4AD
697801d1-68b2-4413-a7e4-0ef507d21cc1.lede: Two school friends who couldn't play when they started got a 4AD deal, a Cocteau Twin producing, a Lollapalooza slot and a Britpop top ten, then lost their drummer a month after their last show.

78605d0c-7454-456d-934c-51eb46122566.name: Modern English
78605d0c-7454-456d-934c-51eb46122566.label: 4AD
78605d0c-7454-456d-934c-51eb46122566.lede: A Colchester art-school band that started out as the Lepers wrote a love song about the bomb dropping, and three years later it was closing out Valley Girl and giving 4AD its first American hit.

eb872766-98f6-453d-883f-2ae908a18315.name: TV on the Radio
eb872766-98f6-453d-883f-2ae908a18315.label: 4AD
eb872766-98f6-453d-883f-2ae908a18315.lede: An animator and a painter turned a $100-a-month Williamsburg loft into a studio after 9/11, and the records that came out of it ran doo-wop, post-punk and noise through the same wires, with David Bowie singing on one of them.

664c3e0e-42d8-48c1-b209-1efca19c0325.name: The National
664c3e0e-42d8-48c1-b209-1efca19c0325.label: 4AD
664c3e0e-42d8-48c1-b209-1efca19c0325.lede: Five Ohioans in Brooklyn pooled $15,000 for a debut, kept their day jobs through two records, then quit them. Two decades on they win Grammys, and their guitarist worked on most of Taylor Swift's Folklore.

1584532a-62ed-4cbe-ad95-6def0af7df35.name: Pale Saints
1584532a-62ed-4cbe-ad95-6def0af7df35.label: 4AD
1584532a-62ed-4cbe-ad95-6def0af7df35.lede: Ivo Watts-Russell heard a Leeds trio's demo, saw one London show and signed them. Pale Saints made three albums for 4AD, and the singer on the last one had started out fronting Lush.

84e4c923-0b83-49d3-9a89-a71a3339edcb.name: The Wolfgang Press
84e4c923-0b83-49d3-9a89-a71a3339edcb.label: 4AD
84e4c923-0b83-49d3-9a89-a71a3339edcb.lede: Three refugees from 4AD's earliest bands made what John Peel called the most morose record he'd ever heard, then discovered De La Soul, scored a US hit with A Girl Like You and watched Tom Jones cover it.

45b675bb-83f5-40e9-bbd4-a597fd9fc6c8.name: His Name Is Alive
45b675bb-83f5-40e9-bbd4-a597fd9fc6c8.label: 4AD
45b675bb-83f5-40e9-bbd4-a597fd9fc6c8.lede: A Michigan teenager taped songs in his parents' basement, mailed them to 4AD until Ivo Watts-Russell said yes, and cried when he heard what Ivo did with them. Decades later Warren Defever is still the only constant in His Name Is Alive.

1fc54353-dcd0-47b1-bb59-7bd2974df829.name: Clan of Xymox
1fc54353-dcd0-47b1-bb59-7bd2974df829.label: 4AD
1fc54353-dcd0-47b1-bb59-7bd2974df829.lede: Two Nijmegen students with a Korg and a drum machine got a Dead Can Dance tour, two albums on 4AD and a John Peel session, then shortened their name and put a song on MTV. Ronny Moorings has kept Clan of Xymox going for four decades since.

c118bc97-11a7-41dc-a55e-48c3bcf22ac2.name: Belly
c118bc97-11a7-41dc-a55e-48c3bcf22ac2.label: 4AD
c118bc97-11a7-41dc-a55e-48c3bcf22ac2.lede: Tanya Donelly left her stepsister's band, called three friends from Aquidneck Island, and within two years had a gold record, two Grammy nominations and the cover of Rolling Stone. Then they stopped talking to each other for twenty years.

0b461f11-c7af-4ddb-a30e-5cb0aabb3e7f.name: Kristin Hersh
0b461f11-c7af-4ddb-a30e-5cb0aabb3e7f.label: 4AD
0b461f11-c7af-4ddb-a30e-5cb0aabb3e7f.lede: She never meant to have a solo career: a tape of leftover acoustic songs got to Michael Stipe, he phoned, and three decades later she's still making records in a Rhode Island studio, alongside Throwing Muses, a loud trio and a shelf of books.

7e5a2a59-6d9f-4a17-b7c2-e1eedb7bd222.name: Grimes
7e5a2a59-6d9f-4a17-b7c2-e1eedb7bd222.label: 4AD
7e5a2a59-6d9f-4a17-b7c2-e1eedb7bd222.lede: Claire Boucher made a Dune concept album on cassette, locked herself in a blacked-out Montreal room with GarageBand to make Visions, and has insisted on producing every part of Grimes herself ever since.

6821bf3f-5d5b-4b0f-8fa4-79d2ab2d9219.name: Blonde Redhead
6821bf3f-5d5b-4b0f-8fa4-79d2ab2d9219.label: 4AD
6821bf3f-5d5b-4b0f-8fa4-79d2ab2d9219.lede: A Japanese art student and two Italian jazz-school twins took their name from a no wave song, made five noisy records for Smells Like and Touch and Go, then remade themselves on 4AD after a horse nearly took Kazu Makino's face.

437a0e49-c6ae-42f6-a6c1-84f25ed366bc.name: Bon Iver
437a0e49-c6ae-42f6-a6c1-84f25ed366bc.label: 4AD
437a0e49-c6ae-42f6-a6c1-84f25ed366bc.lede: Justin Vernon went to his father's hunting cabin to get over a band, a breakup and a sick liver, came back with nine songs he called demos, and ended up on Kanye West records, Taylor Swift records and the Grammy stage.

abf74786-2f3e-47e0-ae68-69a55c13909a.name: Mojave 3
abf74786-2f3e-47e0-ae68-69a55c13909a.label: 4AD
abf74786-2f3e-47e0-ae68-69a55c13909a.lede: Creation dropped Slowdive a week after their third album, so three of them sent Ivo Watts-Russell a cassette of quiet acoustic songs and became a country-tinged 4AD band in the middle of Britpop.

40f5d9e4-2de7-4f2d-ad41-e31a9a9fea27.name: The Smiths
40f5d9e4-2de7-4f2d-ad41-e31a9a9fea27.label: Rough Trade
40f5d9e4-2de7-4f2d-ad41-e31a9a9fea27.lede: A 14-year-old guitarist knocked on a stranger's door in Stretford, and five years later the Smiths had made four studio albums, rewritten British guitar pop and broken up before the last one came out. The arguing over the money took longer.

439a29ad-f4ef-4857-a7cd-3d4a551056c8.name: Cabaret Voltaire
439a29ad-f4ef-4857-a7cd-3d4a551056c8.label: Rough Trade
439a29ad-f4ef-4857-a7cd-3d4a551056c8.lede: Three Sheffield friends played tape loops of steam hammers out of the back of a van, got beaten up at their first gig, and spent the next twenty years turning that noise into music people could dance to.

42201355-08b7-43b6-a7b8-866f612e1600.name: The Raincoats
42201355-08b7-43b6-a7b8-866f612e1600.label: Rough Trade
42201355-08b7-43b6-a7b8-866f612e1600.lede: Two art students saw the Slits, picked up instruments they barely knew how to play, and made a record so unlike anything around it that Kurt Cobain traipsed across London looking for a copy thirteen years later.

3d113367-769f-4200-9ff8-e19d47def451.name: Young Marble Giants
3d113367-769f-4200-9ff8-e19d47def451.label: Rough Trade
3d113367-769f-4200-9ff8-e19d47def451.lede: Two brothers and a singer from Cardiff made one album with a drum machine played off a cassette, toured America, and split. Kurt Cobain, Courtney Love and Belle and Sebastian spent the next decades covering it.

5a54b72e-bfb3-4ca6-944a-e17261399965.name: Pere Ubu
5a54b72e-bfb3-4ca6-944a-e17261399965.label: Rough Trade
5a54b72e-bfb3-4ca6-944a-e17261399965.lede: David Thomas wanted one Cleveland single to turn up in a thrift-store bin someday. He kept the band going for fifty years instead, through 21 musicians, Rough Trade, MTV and a stage version of the play it's named after.

378c0556-fce5-4c1a-8360-5c48ca3e26c5.name: Swell Maps
378c0556-fce5-4c1a-8360-5c48ca3e26c5.label: Rough Trade
378c0556-fce5-4c1a-8360-5c48ca3e26c5.lede: Solihull teenagers who'd been taping songs in each other's bedrooms since 1972 pressed an 87-second single, got John Peel to play it ten times, and made two albums with vacuum cleaners and balloons on them. Thurston Moore said they had a lot to do with his upbringing.

a2588b38-6532-4186-b0c8-9aff306d56f5.name: Scritti Politti
a2588b38-6532-4186-b0c8-9aff306d56f5.label: Rough Trade
a2588b38-6532-4186-b0c8-9aff306d56f5.lede: Green Gartside started out printing his pressing costs and his squat's address on the sleeve, ended up with Miles Davis and Arif Mardin in the credits, and then didn't play a gig for 26 years.

4c9f194e-6235-475a-bf7b-2fd54a0879ec.name: The Pop Group
4c9f194e-6235-475a-bf7b-2fd54a0879ec.label: Rough Trade
4c9f194e-6235-475a-bf7b-2fd54a0879ec.lede: Five Bristol teenagers wanted to be a pop group, hired a dub producer, shouted over free jazz and played their last show to half a million people in Trafalgar Square. They were finished barely out of their teens.

9f041c61-f382-4048-a1f1-33105124bb99.name: Robert Wyatt
9f041c61-f382-4048-a1f1-33105124bb99.label: Rough Trade
9f041c61-f382-4048-a1f1-33105124bb99.lede: Robert Wyatt drummed and sang in the Soft Machine, fell from a fourth-floor window in 1973, and made his comeback on Rough Trade with a run of cover singles that ended in "Shipbuilding".

022865bc-84c9-4002-b6c1-d5fc6e12b7d8.name: Stiff Little Fingers
022865bc-84c9-4002-b6c1-d5fc6e12b7d8.label: Rough Trade
022865bc-84c9-4002-b6c1-d5fc6e12b7d8.lede: Four Belfast schoolboys swapped Deep Purple covers for songs about the Troubles, packaged their first single like a bomb, and made the first independent album to reach the UK Top 20.

83bae41e-e95e-4540-8dfa-2254563858dc.name: LiliPUT
83bae41e-e95e-4540-8dfa-2254563858dc.label: Rough Trade
83bae41e-e95e-4540-8dfa-2254563858dc.lede: Two Zurich artists learned their instruments in a bunker, got a guitarist at their first encore, and were famous enough in Britain by 1979 for Kleenex's lawyers to come calling.

62c2cd94-30a8-43ed-9d06-8f689111c69c.name: Television Personalities
62c2cd94-30a8-43ed-9d06-8f689111c69c.label: Rough Trade
62c2cd94-30a8-43ed-9d06-8f689111c69c.lede: Dan Treacy cut a four-song EP for £22, named it after a TV host punk had embarrassed, and spent the next four decades writing songs that Alan McGee, Kurt Cobain and MGMT all fell for.

53578264-7436-437b-87a0-3b034a3661f0.name: Aztec Camera
53578264-7436-437b-87a0-3b034a3661f0.label: Rough Trade
53578264-7436-437b-87a0-3b034a3661f0.lede: Roddy Frame was 16 when Postcard signed his band and 18 when Rough Trade put out High Land, Hard Rain. He spent the next twelve years under the Aztec Camera name chasing Knopfler, Jam and Lewis, Mick Jones and Ryuichi Sakamoto, and never made the same record twice.

2fb4db11-8349-47ab-b1a6-f04f011699ff.name: The Go-Betweens
2fb4db11-8349-47ab-b1a6-f04f011699ff.label: Rough Trade
2fb4db11-8349-47ab-b1a6-f04f011699ff.lede: Two University of Queensland theatre students named their band after an L.P. Hartley novel, wrote their way through Glasgow, London and Sydney, and never had a Top 50 single. Brisbane named a bridge after them anyway.

16cb5325-3458-4845-b8d6-5933a2ec3166.name: Virgin Prunes
16cb5325-3458-4845-b8d6-5933a2ec3166.label: Rough Trade
16cb5325-3458-4845-b8d6-5933a2ec3166.lede: Lypton Village in north Dublin produced two bands. One became U2; the other wore dresses and plastic suits, got pulled off a Clash support slot and talked Rough Trade into a record that came as a 7-inch, a 10-inch, a 12-inch, a cassette, a book and a film.

ca8ac7f8-fc63-43a9-9761-46c253e66ac3.name: Microdisney
ca8ac7f8-fc63-43a9-9761-46c253e66ac3.label: Rough Trade
ca8ac7f8-fc63-43a9-9761-46c253e66ac3.lede: Two Cork kids met at a New Year's Eve party, stuck record labels on other bands' sleeves at Rough Trade, and made pop songs so sweet that it took a minute to notice how hard Cathal Coughlan's words were biting.

9df32318-47d5-4df7-bc68-3ed9e15eb0f6.name: The Sundays
9df32318-47d5-4df7-bc68-3ed9e15eb0f6.label: Rough Trade
9df32318-47d5-4df7-bc68-3ed9e15eb0f6.lede: Harriet Wheeler and David Gavurin wrote songs in a boiler room, got a bidding war from their first gig, watched their label go bankrupt under their debut, and after three albums simply stopped putting records out.

c48d4327-8122-4286-af66-05e1ee6ac4d8.name: Mazzy Star
c48d4327-8122-4286-af66-05e1ee6ac4d8.label: Rough Trade
c48d4327-8122-4286-af66-05e1ee6ac4d8.lede: A Paisley Underground guitarist and a teenage folk singer from East LA turned a contract-filler for a dead band into Mazzy Star, had a platinum record by accident, and found interviews and stages equally hard going.

f181961b-20f7-459e-89de-920ef03c7ed0.name: The Strokes
f181961b-20f7-459e-89de-920ef03c7ed0.label: Rough Trade
f181961b-20f7-459e-89de-920ef03c7ed0.lede: Rough Trade heard ten seconds of a $600 demo down a phone line and signed it. Twenty-five years on, the five New Yorkers on that tape are still the only lineup the Strokes have had.

82b304c0-7da4-45d3-896a-0767c7ae1141.name: The Libertines
82b304c0-7da4-45d3-896a-0767c7ae1141.label: Rough Trade
82b304c0-7da4-45d3-896a-0767c7ae1141.lede: Two songwriters who couldn't stand each other and couldn't do without each other made two albums for Rough Trade, broke up by way of a burglary, and somehow ended up running a hotel together in Margate.

8830afec-83b3-4213-aad0-f6377f1d73ac.name: British Sea Power
8830afec-83b3-4213-aad0-f6377f1d73ac.label: Rough Trade
8830afec-83b3-4213-aad0-f6377f1d73ac.lede: Rough Trade signed a Brighton band who decorated stages with branches, gave journalists grid references and played a slate mine, a ferry and the highest pub in Britain. Twenty years later they won a Bafta for a video game and dropped the "British."

cf82a38f-9413-4333-bacb-ca5b6db95794.name: Warpaint
cf82a38f-9413-4333-bacb-ca5b6db95794.label: Rough Trade
cf82a38f-9413-4333-bacb-ca5b6db95794.lede: Two choir-class friends from Oregon and two sisters from Nevada started a band in Los Angeles on Valentine's Day 2004, went through five drummers in five years, and found the one who stuck on a night when everybody was on mushrooms.

e01755e3-58ab-4a5b-a9e9-a0a3bd3dff4c.name: Parquet Courts
e01755e3-58ab-4a5b-a9e9-a0a3bd3dff4c.label: Rough Trade
e01755e3-58ab-4a5b-a9e9-a0a3bd3dff4c.lede: Four Texans in Brooklyn put their second album out as 500 records cut during sick days, refused to stay in frame for photo shoots, and a decade later were cutting 40-minute jams in the Catskills for Rough Trade.

09d8290b-6ada-422f-8ce3-19349fb1c15d.name: Sleaford Mods
09d8290b-6ada-422f-8ce3-19349fb1c15d.label: Rough Trade
09d8290b-6ada-422f-8ce3-19349fb1c15d.lede: Jason Williamson was a 43-year-old benefits adviser for Nottingham City Council when people started listening: one man ranting in an East Midlands accent over Andrew Fearn's laptop loops, on a label run by a city bus driver.

4afbef0a-05ee-4551-b0e0-f1f1870d8f1c.name: black midi
4afbef0a-05ee-4551-b0e0-f1f1870d8f1c.label: Rough Trade
4afbef0a-05ee-4551-b0e0-f1f1870d8f1c.lede: Four BRIT School students played their first gig at a Brixton pub before most of them were 18, made three albums in four years, and ended it through an Instagram Live chat box.

7550b236-f9c2-450c-81a6-fac63bf9d23e.name: Die Kreuzen
7550b236-f9c2-450c-81a6-fac63bf9d23e.label: Touch and Go
7550b236-f9c2-450c-81a6-fac63bf9d23e.lede: Die Kreuzen were one of the fastest hardcore bands in the Midwest, then slowed down on purpose, and somebody wrote "You suck now" on their van for it.

ea19687e-8d08-4abe-901e-3135269e4f74.name: The Ex
ea19687e-8d08-4abe-901e-3135269e4f74.label: Touch and Go
ea19687e-8d08-4abe-901e-3135269e4f74.lede: Four Amsterdam squatters drew straws for their instruments in 1979; the band they started has since played more than 2,000 shows in 45 countries, from CBGB to Ethiopian marketplaces, and never settled on one sound.

a3e6d60a-34ff-4d99-8397-2db6b5b2333e.name: Laughing Hyenas
a3e6d60a-34ff-4d99-8397-2db6b5b2333e.label: Touch and Go
a3e6d60a-34ff-4d99-8397-2db6b5b2333e.lede: John Brannon left hardcore behind, Larissa Strickland taught herself guitar in an Ann Arbor basement, and Butch Vig miked their PA so loud he worried about his fillings. Ten years, three albums, and a sound Brannon says nobody can recreate.

5856ffe4-0171-495b-9986-03b96069200e.name: Tar
5856ffe4-0171-495b-9986-03b96069200e.label: Touch and Go
5856ffe4-0171-495b-9986-03b96069200e.lede: A DeKalb hardcore band moved to Chicago, asked a local luthier for guitars they couldn't break, and got aluminum. Seven years and six records on Amphetamine Reptile and Touch and Go later, worn out from the road, Tar finished one last album and called it.

af8bb921-4d67-4f0d-ba17-6215315f92e4.name: Dirty Three
af8bb921-4d67-4f0d-ba17-6215315f92e4.label: Touch and Go
af8bb921-4d67-4f0d-ba17-6215315f92e4.lede: A violinist, a guitarist and a drummer worked up a set in Warren Ellis's kitchen and played it that night in a Melbourne pub with no stage. Thirty-odd years and nine albums later, there's still no singer.

24d2e33e-6493-49c9-a5b1-fc82eb2f7d4d.name: Seam
24d2e33e-6493-49c9-a5b1-fc82eb2f7d4d.label: Touch and Go
24d2e33e-6493-49c9-a5b1-fc82eb2f7d4d.lede: Sooyoung Park left the noise of Bitch Magnet for something slower, made four records that a generation of emo bands wore out, and took his band to Seoul before almost any American indie act had tried.

d8e4d102-a8ae-4eda-95f7-9238de41a220.name: Storm & Stress
d8e4d102-a8ae-4eda-95f7-9238de41a220.label: Touch and Go
d8e4d102-a8ae-4eda-95f7-9238de41a220.lede: Ian Williams wanted a band that was Don Caballero turned upside down, so he found a free-jazz drummer at a party, played quietly through a full stack of amps, and made two records nobody could count along to.

5e372a49-5672-4fb8-ba14-18c90780c4f9.name: Calexico
5e372a49-5672-4fb8-ba14-18c90780c4f9.label: Quarterstick (Touch and Go)
5e372a49-5672-4fb8-ba14-18c90780c4f9.lede: Giant Sand's rhythm section named their side project after a border town, filled it with mariachi horns, pedal steel and Tucson heat, and outgrew the band that made them.

7b16e4ca-a204-4158-8293-20cb44c11d88.name: Rachel's
7b16e4ca-a204-4158-8293-20cb44c11d88.label: Quarterstick (Touch and Go)
7b16e4ca-a204-4158-8293-20cb44c11d88.lede: An art-school guitarist from Rodan and a conservatory violist met on a Baltimore trolley, a Louisville pianist named Rachel taught one of them to read music, and Touch and Go's arthouse label put strings, piano and an orchestral bass drum into indie record stores.

584c04d2-4acc-491b-8a0a-e63133f4bfc4.name: Yeah Yeah Yeahs
584c04d2-4acc-491b-8a0a-e63133f4bfc4.label: Touch and Go
584c04d2-4acc-491b-8a0a-e63133f4bfc4.lede: Karen O, Nick Zinner and a drummer recruited the day before their first show put out a five-song EP on their own label, let Touch and Go take it national, then turned down the majors, paid for their own debut and spent twenty-five years refusing to make the same record twice.

b1b5e551-95bb-4cff-b740-0c6fa11c66e3.name: Arcwelder
b1b5e551-95bb-4cff-b740-0c6fa11c66e3.label: Touch and Go
b1b5e551-95bb-4cff-b740-0c6fa11c66e3.lede: Two Graber brothers and a drummer who sings got sued out of their first name by the company that makes the Tilt-A-Whirl, made four albums for Touch and Go around their day jobs, and came back twenty-four years later with a record mixed by J. Robbins.

fd0f1d5f-5d8c-4fcd-9d3c-0c9f20cddc08.name: The Black Heart Procession
fd0f1d5f-5d8c-4fcd-9d3c-0c9f20cddc08.label: Touch and Go
fd0f1d5f-5d8c-4fcd-9d3c-0c9f20cddc08.lede: Two Three Mile Pilot members, both freshly dumped, started writing songs for a musical saw and a creaky piano in San Diego. They numbered the first three albums because, as Tobias Nathaniel put it, they hadn't learned that 4 existed.

13e78eec-9ee4-47f2-a50e-2a9f519cb6e2.name: Pegboy
13e78eec-9ee4-47f2-a50e-2a9f519cb6e2.label: Quarterstick (Touch and Go)
13e78eec-9ee4-47f2-a50e-2a9f519cb6e2.lede: John Haggerty walked out of Naked Raygun, grabbed his little brother and two guys from the Bhopal Stiffs, and gave Touch and Go's new sister label its very first record. Steve Albini once filled in on bass.

9cb56cf1-bd4a-4d59-8ecb-dc412f595dd3.name: Uzeda
9cb56cf1-bd4a-4d59-8ecb-dc412f595dd3.label: Touch and Go
9cb56cf1-bd4a-4d59-8ecb-dc412f595dd3.lede: In 1991 a noise band from Catania mailed a demo to Steve Albini, and he got on a plane to Sicily. Nearly four decades on, three of the five founders are still in the band, and still doing it on their own terms.

b3d5b1c9-95df-42ea-83eb-c86b18f61f8d.name: The New Year
b3d5b1c9-95df-42ea-83eb-c86b18f61f8d.label: Touch and Go
b3d5b1c9-95df-42ea-83eb-c86b18f61f8d.lede: When Bedhead ended, Matt and Bubba Kadane kept the three guitars, kept Steve Albini, changed the name and spread the band across four cities.

3df29542-402a-49a5-ae1f-82f936184b3b.name: Quasi
3df29542-402a-49a5-ae1f-82f936184b3b.label: Touch and Go
3df29542-402a-49a5-ae1f-82f936184b3b.lede: Sam Coomes and Janet Weiss were married for four years and have been a band for more than thirty: one man on a rocksichord, one woman on drums, and a sound bigger than two people should make.

f26c72d3-e52c-467b-b651-679c73d8e1a7.label: Touch and Go
f26c72d3-e52c-467b-b651-679c73d8e1a7.lede: A Sacramento band named after the click consonants in a movie subtitle moved to New York, wrote a nine-minute song about Rudy Giuliani's war on dancing, and has been jamming its way around the festival circuit ever since.

e162b2eb-6a42-4240-8c1b-c94d9a0acb73.name: CocoRosie
e162b2eb-6a42-4240-8c1b-c94d9a0acb73.label: Touch and Go
e162b2eb-6a42-4240-8c1b-c94d9a0acb73.lede: Two sisters who hadn't spoken in years made a record in a Paris bathroom with toy pianos and one microphone, and Touch and Go talked them out of giving it only to friends.

1f16a425-2606-4137-a6b7-234b6dabe037.name: Pinback
1f16a425-2606-4137-a6b7-234b6dabe037.label: Touch and Go
1f16a425-2606-4137-a6b7-234b6dabe037.lede: Two San Diego roommates named their band after a crewman in a 1974 John Carpenter space comedy, made the first album on a home computer, and kept Pinback going for more than a quarter century.

ce49b1f2-a903-46fc-8b84-b5699f019a06.name: Enon
ce49b1f2-a903-46fc-8b84-b5699f019a06.label: Touch and Go
ce49b1f2-a903-46fc-8b84-b5699f019a06.lede: After Brainiac ended, John Schmersal built a band around a junk-kit drummer and a Moog, lost his label to 9/11, and found a co-singer in a bassist who had just quit her last band.

31095622-5a1e-4f22-8ad1-b08eb6255f37.name: Ted Leo and the Pharmacists
31095622-5a1e-4f22-8ad1-b08eb6255f37.label: Touch and Go
31095622-5a1e-4f22-8ad1-b08eb6255f37.lede: Ted Leo named his band after a dub-soaked solo record, rode out money trouble at Lookout! and Touch and Go's shutdown, and took Shake the Sheets back on the road twenty years after it came out.

0e1a1b82-904f-49b0-8955-086f0bf28afa.name: The Delta 72
0e1a1b82-904f-49b0-8955-086f0bf28afa.label: Touch and Go
0e1a1b82-904f-49b0-8955-086f0bf28afa.lede: Gregg Foreman moved to D.C. for Fugazi, bought a Farfisa, and built a band that played Booker T. soul like punk rock, with the White Stripes and the Strokes opening.

69dbd702-9073-49dd-b73a-67c33f030a4f.name: The Monorchid
69dbd702-9073-49dd-b73a-67c33f030a4f.label: Touch and Go
69dbd702-9073-49dd-b73a-67c33f030a4f.lede: Two Circus Lupus veterans got back together, made a run of singles and one LP for small labels, and broke up before Touch and Go released the second album. The sleeve says so: R.I.P. May 1995 to Sept. 1997.

fc0bd304-cfd4-4478-9224-3446134d57fe.name: Tubeway Army
fc0bd304-cfd4-4478-9224-3446134d57fe.label: Beggars Banquet
fc0bd304-cfd4-4478-9224-3446134d57fe.lede: A London punk trio that couldn't hold on to a drummer found a Minimoog someone had left in the studio, and within a year had the first synth-led No. 1 of the electronic era.

6cb79cb2-9087-44d4-828b-5c6fdff2c957.name: Gary Numan
6cb79cb2-9087-44d4-828b-5c6fdff2c957.label: Beggars Banquet
6cb79cb2-9087-44d4-828b-5c6fdff2c957.lede: Gary Numan had two No. 1 singles and three No. 1 albums before he was 23, walked away from the stage at Wembley, spent fifteen years losing fans and money, and then watched [[Nine Inch Nails]], [[Fear Factory]] and [[Marilyn Manson]] line up to cover his songs.

dc78f9b6-afcd-46d6-894e-2149f40a4884.name: The Associates
dc78f9b6-afcd-46d6-894e-2149f40a4884.label: Beggars Banquet
dc78f9b6-afcd-46d6-894e-2149f40a4884.lede: Alan Rankine and Billy Mackenzie wrote "Party Fears Two" on a hungover Sunday in 1977, sat on it for five years, then took it onto Top of the Pops with a banjo, a beret and a voice nobody else in British pop could touch.

8846e4ff-0c19-4af2-872b-7a8dc7497f68.name: The Cult
8846e4ff-0c19-4af2-872b-7a8dc7497f68.label: Beggars Banquet
8846e4ff-0c19-4af2-872b-7a8dc7497f68.lede: Ian Astbury and Billy Duffy started out as goths in feathers and a white Gretsch, got the wrong producer for their biggest song, then let Rick Rubin tell them to plug a Les Paul into a Marshall and turn into a hard rock band. They have been arguing with their own past, mostly happily, ever since.

8cb3aa4a-3b4c-48b8-be0a-e57010fc1430.name: Love and Rockets
8cb3aa4a-3b4c-48b8-be0a-e57010fc1430.label: Beggars Banquet
8cb3aa4a-3b4c-48b8-be0a-e57010fc1430.lede: Three-quarters of Bauhaus named themselves after a comic book, made psychedelic pop for American college radio, and then Daniel Ash wrote 'So Alive' in a studio basement in about an hour and took it to No. 3 on the Billboard Hot 100.

ff3a293a-76d1-49a7-a5c5-fede02e7e648.name: Tones on Tail
ff3a293a-76d1-49a7-a5c5-fede02e7e648.label: Beggars Banquet
ff3a293a-76d1-49a7-a5c5-fede02e7e648.lede: Daniel Ash started it in a flat with the Bauhaus roadie, Kevin Haskins joined when Bauhaus died, and in three years the trio made one album, toured America in white suits, and left 'Go!' to the dance floors.

b78346af-e3ce-4b36-a0d5-032414de8a27.name: Peter Murphy
b78346af-e3ce-4b36-a0d5-032414de8a27.label: Beggars Banquet
b78346af-e3ce-4b36-a0d5-032414de8a27.lede: The voice of Bauhaus spent his first solo years learning to make records without a band behind him, then landed a seven-week number one on American modern rock radio and moved to Istanbul.

8434409e-baa9-4e12-b4aa-566a91c7d7cf.name: The Charlatans
8434409e-baa9-4e12-b4aa-566a91c7d7cf.label: Beggars Banquet
8434409e-baa9-4e12-b4aa-566a91c7d7cf.lede: Rob Collins's Hammond organ made the Charlatans, and his death in 1996, halfway through their biggest record, should have ended them. They finished it with a borrowed keyboard player and went to number one.

488e2f56-76bc-446f-8089-d790a5402904.name: The Lurkers
488e2f56-76bc-446f-8089-d790a5402904.label: Beggars Banquet
488e2f56-76bc-446f-8089-d790a5402904.lede: Four pub regulars from Ickenham rehearsed in a record shop basement, and the shop started a label to put them out. Beggars Banquet's first record is a Lurkers single, cut in an hour and a half.

d72c9ab4-0b73-44e3-8601-c4da02a43b25.name: Gene Loves Jezebel
d72c9ab4-0b73-44e3-8601-c4da02a43b25.label: Beggars Banquet
d72c9ab4-0b73-44e3-8601-c4da02a43b25.lede: Two identical twins from Porthcawl took turns at the microphone, fought over every lead vocal, and ended up running two bands with the same name on two continents.

1159e0d0-a782-471a-9dae-93ac046eac72.name: Buffalo Tom
1159e0d0-a782-471a-9dae-93ac046eac72.label: Beggars Banquet
1159e0d0-a782-471a-9dae-93ac046eac72.lede: Three UMass students got a leg up from J Mascis, found a following in Britain before America, and wrote "Taillights Fade", the song they'll be playing at every show for the rest of their lives.

03143cba-d359-4bd9-8ab3-5ba6590f9933.name: The Icicle Works
03143cba-d359-4bd9-8ab3-5ba6590f9933.label: Beggars Banquet
03143cba-d359-4bd9-8ab3-5ba6590f9933.lede: A Liverpool trio named after a Frederik Pohl story put "Birds Fly (Whisper to a Scream)" into the American top 40, then watched their US label turn down the next album.

a262543f-6ab4-4ac7-86f3-4fc09ff56f3b.name: Fields of the Nephilim
a262543f-6ab4-4ac7-86f3-4fc09ff56f3b.label: Beggars Banquet
a262543f-6ab4-4ac7-86f3-4fc09ff56f3b.lede: Five men from Hertfordshire dressed like spaghetti-western gunslingers, rolled in flour and made goth heavier than it had ever been. Then Carl McCoy split the band at its peak and kept the name.

892500b7-09a6-4049-ba92-2d192dd70563.name: Biffy Clyro
892500b7-09a6-4049-ba92-2d192dd70563.label: Beggars Banquet
892500b7-09a6-4049-ba92-2d192dd70563.lede: Three teenagers from Ayrshire spent three Beggars Banquet albums hiding their choruses on purpose. Then Simon Neil decided they were the best band in the world, and they went on to headline Reading.

4306a798-e2f8-4192-9a45-2fd41cdae60c.name: Tindersticks
4306a798-e2f8-4192-9a45-2fd41cdae60c.label: Beggars Banquet
4306a798-e2f8-4192-9a45-2fd41cdae60c.lede: Six people from Nottingham named themselves after a box of German matches, demoed their first album in a Kilburn kitchen and spent a decade making strings, soul and Claire Denis scores. Half of them left in 2006; the other half built a studio in a French barn and kept going.

7b1cf87e-c54f-4abc-893d-90245a31900d.name: Mercury Rev
7b1cf87e-c54f-4abc-893d-90245a31900d.label: Beggars Banquet
7b1cf87e-c54f-4abc-893d-90245a31900d.lede: Four Buffalo film students made soundtracks for movies, got shut down by the mayor of Denver, nearly broke apart in debt, and then came out of a Catskills attic with strings, Levon Helm and NME's album of the year.

dc17118a-9e18-4bec-9d87-f8c7d1c53d35.name: Flesh for Lulu
dc17118a-9e18-4bec-9d87-f8c7d1c53d35.label: Beggars Banquet
dc17118a-9e18-4bec-9d87-f8c7d1c53d35.lede: Flesh for Lulu came out of Brixton squats in eyeliner and a Stonesy swagger, got a song into a John Hughes movie and limousines on Paramount's tab, then came apart in a Sydney studio just as American college radio caught up.

ac8f8330-1270-4a56-89c4-3318f8fa5c3b.name: Red Lorry Yellow Lorry
ac8f8330-1270-4a56-89c4-3318f8fa5c3b.label: Beggars Banquet
ac8f8330-1270-4a56-89c4-3318f8fa5c3b.lede: Chris Reed built a Leeds band on a drum machine, a guitar drone and a demo tape that went out as a single untouched, then spent the next forty years insisting it was never a goth band.

3c911700-4bd0-4aba-8b38-adeff24130dc.name: The Bolshoi
3c911700-4bd0-4aba-8b38-adeff24130dc.label: Beggars Banquet
3c911700-4bd0-4aba-8b38-adeff24130dc.lede: Two Wiltshire punks moved to London, turned their dark streak into pop songs, toured from Poland to South America, and left a fourth album sitting on reference cassettes for 27 years.

a67cecf3-7544-4687-a4aa-cc0eeb0a7605.name: Thee Hypnotics
a67cecf3-7544-4687-a4aa-cc0eeb0a7605.label: Beggars Banquet
a67cecf3-7544-4687-a4aa-cc0eeb0a7605.lede: A High Wycombe band that worshipped the MC5 and the Stooges became Sub Pop's British connection, survived a Minneapolis bus wreck, and made its last album with a Black Crowe producing.

adbd993c-fd28-4885-ad2d-0349546119ab.name: Freeez
adbd993c-fd28-4885-ad2d-0349546119ab.label: Beggars Banquet
adbd993c-fd28-4885-ad2d-0349546119ab.lede: John Rocca borrowed from his grandmother to press a jazz-funk single, walked into Arthur Baker's New York office without an appointment, and came home with "I.O.U."

2baf3276-ed6a-4349-8d2e-f4601e7b2167.name: Playboi Carti
2baf3276-ed6a-4349-8d2e-f4601e7b2167.label: AWGE / Interscope
2baf3276-ed6a-4349-8d2e-f4601e7b2167.lede: An Atlanta kid who freestyles nearly every verse turns a baby voice, long silences and a vampire alter ego into the records rage rap is built on.

8837b875-3689-4646-b3fd-d8b53815c7a8.name: Lil Uzi Vert
8837b875-3689-4646-b3fd-d8b53815c7a8.label: Generation Now / Atlantic
8837b875-3689-4646-b3fd-d8b53815c7a8.lede: A Philadelphia kid named for a machine-gun flow turns a breakup into "XO Tour Llif3," spends two years fighting a label to free Eternal Atake, and a decade on walks out independent, owning the masters.

987d3d86-0d7a-4292-ae96-a8d59e456436.name: Destroy Lonely
987d3d86-0d7a-4292-ae96-a8d59e456436.label: Opium / Interscope
987d3d86-0d7a-4292-ae96-a8d59e456436.lede: The son of a Disturbing tha Peace rapper started recording at fourteen, got a call from [[Playboi Carti]] at nineteen, and has spent the years since turning Opium's black-on-black sound into what he calls sonic horror movies.

4585749c-5489-4699-9daf-1ffa9717179f.name: Nettspend
4585749c-5489-4699-9daf-1ffa9717179f.label: Grade A / Interscope
4585749c-5489-4699-9daf-1ffa9717179f.lede: Gunner Shepardson from Richmond, Virginia, recorded his breakout in about ten minutes in his mom's car, played Rolling Loud at sixteen, and put out his debut album on Interscope at eighteen.
